instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Lay the beef slices flat on a clean surface and season them lightly with salt and pepper. | Place a slice of prosciutto on each beef slice, then sprinkle with grated Parmesan and add a fresh basil leaf. | Roll each beef slice tightly around the fillings and secure with toothpicks or kitchen twine. | Heat olive oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat. | Sear the beef rolls on all sides until browned, about 2-3 minutes per side. | Remove the skillet from heat and pour the red wine and beef broth into the pan to deglaze, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. | Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake for 15-20 minutes, until the beef is cooked through and tender. | Remove the involtini from the oven, transfer to a serving dish, and let rest for a few minutes. | Remove toothpicks or twine before serving, and spoon the pan sauce over the beef rolls.

name: Banbanji
description: Banbanji, or Bang Bang Chicken Salad, is a flavorful Chinese dish featuring shredded chicken dressed in a creamy, spicy sesame sauce, often enjoyed as a refreshing main or appetizer.
instructions: Boil water in a pot and cook chicken breast until fully cooked, about 15 minutes. Remove the chicken and let it cool, then shred it into thin pieces. | In a bowl, combine tahini, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, minced garlic, grated ginger, chili oil, and sesame oil to make the dressing. Whisk until smooth. | Place the shredded chicken in a large mixing bowl. Add sliced cucumber and chopped scallion. | Pour the dressing over the chicken and vegetables, then toss gently to combine and coat everything evenly. | Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds and chopped cilantro over the top for garnish before serving.

name: Bara Chirashi
description: Bara Chirashi is a vibrant Japanese diced sushi bowl featuring seasoned sushi rice topped with a colorful array of diced seafood, tamagoyaki, and fresh vegetables, served with traditional condiments.
instructions: Cook sushi rice according to package instructions and let it cool to room temperature. | In a bowl, mix the cooked sushi rice with rice vinegar, sugar, and salt; stir gently to combine and set aside. | Prepare the toppings by dicing fresh tuna, salmon, cooked shrimp, and tamagoyaki (Japanese omelette) into bite-sized cubes. | Thinly slice cucumber and shred nori sheets into fine strips. | In serving bowls, place a generous portion of the seasoned sushi rice as the base. | Arrange the diced seafood, tamagoyaki, cucumber slices, and nori strips attractively on top of the rice. | Garnish with pickled ginger, a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds, and chopped green onion. | Serve the Bara Chirashi with soy sauce and wasabi on the side, according to taste.

name: Basashi
description: Basashi is a traditional Japanese dish consisting of thinly sliced raw horse meat served as sashimi. It is enjoyed for its tender texture and delicate flavor, often complemented by soy sauce, ginger, and spicy mustard.
instructions: Chill the horse meat thoroughly in the refrigerator until very cold but not frozen to facilitate slicing. | Using a very sharp knife, slice the horse meat thinly into sashimi-style pieces about 2-3 mm thick. | Arrange the sliced horse meat neatly on a chilled plate or wooden platter to keep it fresh and visually appealing. | Garnish with sliced fresh ginger, finely chopped green onion, and optionally thinly sliced garlic for traditional accompaniments. | Serve with small dishes of soy sauce and a dab of spicy mustard (karashi) on the side for dipping. | Optionally, serve with shiso leaf and finely grated daikon radish as garnishes to enhance flavor and presentation. | Consume immediately to enjoy the fresh taste and texture of the horse meat sashimi.

name: Basashi
description: Basashi is a traditional Japanese dish from Kumamoto featuring thinly sliced raw horse meat served as sashimi. It offers a tender texture and rich flavor, often accompanied by ginger, garlic, and soy sauce for dipping.
instructions: Clean the horse meat thoroughly using cold water and pat dry with paper towels. | Slice the horse meat into thin, bite-sized sashimi pieces using a sharp knife. | Arrange the horse sashimi slices neatly on a chilled plate to keep them fresh and cool. | Serve the basashi with finely chopped green onion, grated ginger, and garlic on the side for added flavor. | Provide soy sauce and horse meat dipping sauce (basashi sauce) for dipping. | Enjoy the basashi fresh as a raw delicacy, appreciating the tender texture and unique taste of horse meat.

name: Basque Cheesecake Japanese-style
description: A Japanese-style Basque cheesecake is a creamy, lightly burnt crust cheesecake famous for its custardy interior and caramelized top, blending Spanish Basque origin with Japanese soft texture.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210°C (410°F). Grease a 20 cm (8 inch) springform pan with butter and line it with parchment paper, allowing the paper to extend above the rim of the pan. | In a large mixing bowl, beat 450 g cream cheese until smooth and creamy using an electric mixer. | Add 150 g granulated sugar and continue beating until combined and smooth. | Add 4 large eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. | Pour in 300 ml heavy cream and 15 g all-purpose flour, then mix gently until the batter is smooth and homogenous. | Pour the batter into the prepared pan and tap gently on the counter to release any air bubbles. | Bake in the preheated oven for 50 to 60 minutes, or until the top is deeply browned and the center is still slightly jiggly. | Remove the cheesecake from the oven and allow it to cool in the pan for several hours at room temperature; the cheesecake will set as it cools. | Once cooled, remove from the pan and slice to serve. | Optionally, chill in the refrigerator for a few hours before serving for a firmer texture.

name: Battera
description: Battera is a traditional pressed sushi from Osaka, featuring lightly cured mackerel layered with sushi rice and wrapped with konbu seaweed, creating a compact and flavorful dish.
instructions: Rinse the mackerel fillet under cold water and pat dry with paper towels. | Lightly salt the mackerel fillet and let it sit in the refrigerator for 30 minutes to draw out moisture. | Meanwhile, prepare sushi rice by rinsing the rice until water runs clear, then cook according to package instructions. | While the rice cooks, heat rice vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan until sugar dissolves; let it cool to make sushi vinegar. | Once rice is cooked, transfer to a large bowl and gently fold in the sushi vinegar, allowing the rice to cool to room temperature. | Soak the konbu (kelp) in water for a few minutes, then pat dry and set aside for assembly. | Cut the mackerel fillet into rectangular pieces that will fit your oshizushi (press sushi) mold. | Place the konbu sheet at the bottom of the oshizushi mold, then layer the salted mackerel on top, skin side up. | Add an even layer of sushi rice over the fish, pressing firmly with the mold's lid or wooden press to compact the sushi into a neat block. | Remove the sushi block from the mold and cut it into rectangular pieces about 2 inches wide. | Serve the Battera with soy sauce, pickled ginger, and wasabi as desired.

name: Battera
description: Battera is a traditional Osaka-style pressed sushi featuring salted mackerel layered with vinegared sushi rice and pickled kelp, pressed into a compact rectangular shape and sliced into bite-sized pieces.
instructions: Lightly clean the mackerel fillets and pat dry. | Sprinkle salt evenly over the mackerel fillets and let them rest for about 30 minutes to draw out moisture. | Rinse the salted mackerel under cold water and pat dry thoroughly. | Prepare sushi rice by cooking short-grain rice, then mix it with rice vinegar, sugar, and salt while it is still warm. Let the rice cool to room temperature. | Lay a bamboo sushi press (oshizushihako) on a flat surface and line it with plastic wrap. | Place the mackerel fillets skin side down in the sushi press, ensuring they cover the base evenly. | Thinly slice pickled kelp (konbu) and place a layer over the mackerel fillets. | Spread the cooled sushi rice evenly on top of the konbu layer, pressing down gently. | Using the top part of the sushi press, press firmly to compact the layers. | Remove the top of the press, lift the sushi block using the plastic wrap, and place it on a bamboo mat or cutting board. | Remove the plastic wrap carefully. | Using a sharp knife, slice the pressed sushi block into bite-sized rectangles. | Serve with pickled ginger, soy sauce, and wasabi as accompaniments.

name: Beni Shoga
description: Beni Shoga is a traditional Japanese condiment made from thinly sliced ginger pickled in red shiso vinegar, offering a characteristic bright red color and sharp flavor that complements many dishes.
instructions: Slice fresh ginger into thin julienne strips about 5 cm long. | Mix red shiso leaves with salt in a bowl to create the characteristic red color and flavor. | Combine sliced ginger with salted red shiso leaves and let it sit for about 30 minutes. | In a separate pot, bring rice vinegar, sugar, and salt to a boil and stir until dissolved. | Pour the hot vinegar mixture over the ginger and shiso mix, ensuring the ginger is fully submerged. | Transfer the mixture to a clean jar, cover, and let it pickle at room temperature for 3 to 5 days for best flavor. | After pickling, refrigerate the Beni Shoga; it can be consumed immediately but flavor improves after a week. | Use as a condiment for various Japanese dishes, especially in okonomiyaki, takoyaki, or with rice dishes.

name: Beniimo Tart
description: Beniimo Tart is a Japanese-inspired dessert showcasing the naturally vibrant purple sweet potato in a creamy, smooth tart filling within a buttery crust.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Prepare the tart crust by mixing flour, sugar, and butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. | Add egg yolk and water to the crust mixture and combine until a dough forms. Wrap in plastic and chill for 30 minutes. | Roll out the chilled dough and fit it into a tart pan. Prick the base with a fork and bake for 15 minutes until lightly golden. | Peel and boil purple sweet potato until soft, then mash until smooth. | In a bowl, mix the mashed purple sweet potato with sugar, heavy cream, egg, melted butter, and vanilla extract until well combined. | Pour the sweet potato filling into the pre-baked tart crust. | Bake the tart for 25-30 minutes at 180°C until the filling is set and slightly browned on top. | Allow the tart to cool before serving.

name: Beppu Jigoku Mushi
description: Beppu Jigoku Mushi is a traditional Japanese dish from Beppu, where various fresh ingredients like seafood, eggs, and vegetables are steamed using natural hot spring steam, resulting in a healthy and gently cooked meal.
instructions: Fill a large pot or steamer with water and bring it to a boil to generate steam. | Place the food items suitable for steaming (such as seafood, vegetables, and eggs) into a steamer basket or metal container that can withstand direct steam heat. | Once the water is boiling, carefully place the steamer basket or container into the pot so the steam cooks the food without submerging it in water. | Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid and cook the food using the steam for about 10 to 20 minutes, depending on the ingredients' size and type. | Check the doneness by piercing with a fork or skewer; seafood should be opaque and vegetables tender but firm. | Carefully remove the steamer basket or container from the pot to avoid burns from steam. | Serve the steamed food immediately with dipping sauces such as soy sauce or ponzu, and garnish with optional fresh herbs or lemon wedges if desired.

name: Atole with Guava
description: A traditional Mexican warm beverage made by thickening corn masa with milk and sweetened guava paste, creating a rich and comforting guava-flavored atole.
instructions: In a medium saucepan, combine the masa harina with half of the water and whisk until smooth to form a slurry. | Add the remaining water, milk, and sugar to the saucepan and stir to combine. | Place the saucepan over medium heat and cook, stirring continuously, until the mixture thickens and is smooth, about 10-15 minutes. | Once thickened, add the guava paste pieces to the atole and stir until the guava paste dissolves fully into the mixture. | Simmer the atole with guava for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. | Remove from heat and pour the atole into cups. | Serve warm, optionally garnished with a cinnamon stick or a sprinkle of ground cinnamon if desired.

name: Avocado Salsa
description: Avocado salsa is a creamy, fresh Mexican accompaniment made by blending ripe avocado with onion, tomato, cilantro, and lime juice. It is a versatile condiment perfect for tacos, grilled meats, or as a dip.
instructions: Cut the ripe avocado in half, remove the pit, and scoop out the flesh into a bowl. | Finely chop the onion, tomato, cilantro, and jalapeno pepper, then add them to the bowl. | Add the juice of one lime to the mixture to add acidity and prevent the avocado from browning. | Season with salt and pepper to taste. | Gently mash and mix all ingredients together until you achieve a chunky but cohesive salsa texture. | Adjust seasoning with extra lime juice or salt if needed. | Serve chilled or at room temperature as a dip or accompaniment for Mexican dishes.

name: Año Nuevo Lentil Soup
description: A traditional New Year lentil soup symbolizing prosperity, hearty and flavorful with vegetables and spices, perfect for a warming and auspicious start of the year.
instructions: Rinse the lentil thoroughly under cold water and drain. | Peel and chop the carrot, celery, onion, and garlic. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. | Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery, and sauté until the vegetables are softened, about 5 minutes. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Add the rinsed lentils to the pot along with vegetable broth, diced tomato, bay leaf, cumin, salt, and pepper. | Bring the soup to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for about 40 minutes, or until lentils are tender. | Remove the bay leaf and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

name: Bacalao a La Vizcaina
description: Bacalao a la Vizcaina is a traditional Basque Christmas dish featuring salted cod simmered in a rich red pepper and tomato sauce, highlighting the region's flavors.
instructions: Soak the salted cod in cold water for 48 hours, changing the water every 8 hours to desalt it. | Drain the cod and remove any skin and bones, then cut it into serving portions. | Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. | Finely chop the onion, garlic, and red bell pepper. | Add the onion and garlic to the pan and sauté until softened. | Add the chopped red bell pepper and cook until softened. | Add the diced tomato and cook until the mixture thickens into a sauce. | Add the pimenton (paprika), bay leaf, salt, and pepper to the sauce and stir well. | Gently add the cod pieces to the sauce and simmer on low heat for about 15 minutes, ensuring the cod absorbs the flavors. | Remove the bay leaf and sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Baja California Fish Tacos
description: Baja California fish tacos are a popular Mexican dish featuring beer-battered fried fish served in warm corn tortillas with fresh cabbage, cilantro, and a creamy sauce, capturing coastal Baja flavors.
instructions: Prepare the fish by cutting firm white fish fillets into strips about 1 inch wide and patting them dry. | In a bowl, combine flour, cornmeal, baking powder, salt, chili powder, and black pepper. | Whisk in cold beer gradually until batter reaches a smooth, thick consistency. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet or fryer to 180°C (350°F). | Dip each fish strip into the batter, allowing excess to drip off, and carefully place into the hot oil. | Fry fish strips for 3 to 4 minutes until golden brown and crispy, then remove and drain on paper towels. | Warm corn tortillas on a skillet or grill until pliable. | Assemble tacos by placing fried fish on each tortilla, topping with shredded cabbage, chopped cilantro, and sliced radish if desired. | Drizzle with a creamy sauce made from mixing mayonnaise, sour cream, lime juice, garlic powder, and hot sauce. | Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side.

name: Baja California Langosta Puerto Nuevo
description: Baja California Langosta Puerto Nuevo is a traditional Mexican dish featuring deep-fried spiny lobster served with tortillas and beans, originating from the coastal village of Puerto Nuevo in Baja California. The lobster is coated in flour and fried to a crispy golden finish resulting in a delicious and iconic seafood meal.
instructions: Start by cleaning and preparing 2 live spiny lobsters by removing the shell and cutting them in half lengthwise, but keep the tail intact. | Heat 2 cups of vegetable oil in a deep skillet or fryer to 180°C (350°F). | Meanwhile, season the lobster halves with salt and pepper to taste. | In a shallow dish, combine 200 g of all-purpose flour and 1 tsp of salt. | Dredge each lobster half thoroughly in the seasoned flour, shaking off any excess. | Carefully place the floured lobster halves into the hot oil, frying for about 5-7 minutes on each side until the shell is crispy and the meat is cooked through and opaque. | Remove the fried lobster and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. | Serve the lobster immediately with freshly cut lemon wedges and a side of Mexican-style beans and handmade flour tortillas. | Optionally, you can add a fresh salad made with iceberg lettuce, tomato, and avocado dressed with lime juice and olive oil. | Traditionally, this dish is accompanied by rice, beans, and handmade tortillas or flour tortillas, so prepare those as desired to serve alongside.

name: Baja Med Grilled Fish Tacos
description: Baja Med grilled fish tacos combine freshly marinated and grilled fish with vibrant cabbage slaw and creamy chipotle sauce, showcasing the fusion flavors of Baja California cuisine.
instructions: Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. | In a bowl, combine olive oil, lime juice, garlic, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper to create a marinade. | Coat the fish fillets with the marinade and let them marinate for 15 minutes. | Grill the fish fillets for about 3-4 minutes on each side or until cooked through and slightly charred. | Warm the corn tortillas on the grill for about 30 seconds on each side. | In a separate bowl, mix shredded cabbage, chopped cilantro, lime juice, and a pinch of salt to make a fresh slaw. | Assemble the tacos by placing grilled fish on each tortilla, topping with the cabbage slaw, diced avocado, and a drizzle of chipotle mayo or crema. | Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side.

name: Baked Chicken with Herbs
description: Baked chicken infused with a fragrant blend of fresh herbs and garlic, resulting in a flavorful and juicy main dish.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | In a bowl, combine olive oil, minced garlic, chopped fresh rosemary, thyme, parsley, salt, and pepper to create the herb marinade. | Place the whole chicken or chicken pieces in a baking dish and rub the herb marinade all over, ensuring it is well coated. | Let the chicken marinate for at least 15 minutes at room temperature to allow flavors to develop. | Bake the chicken in the preheated oven for 45-60 minutes, or until the internal temperature reaches 75°C (165°F) and the skin is golden and crisp. | Remove the chicken from the oven and let it rest for 10 minutes before serving to retain its juices. | Serve the baked chicken garnished with additional fresh herbs if desired.

name: Baked Plantains with Cream
description: Baked plantains with a creamy sauce is a delicious and simple dessert popular in Latin American cuisine, highlighting the natural sweetness of ripe plantains.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Peel the ripe plantains and slice them diagonally into 1-inch thick pieces. | Place the plantain slices in a baking dish in a single layer. | Lightly brush the plantains with melted butter on both sides. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 20 minutes or until the plantains are golden and tender, flipping them halfway through. | While the plantains are baking, prepare the cream sauce by mixing heavy cream, a pinch of salt, and a teaspoon of sugar in a bowl. | Once the plantains are baked, remove them from the oven and transfer to a serving dish. | Pour the cream sauce evenly over the warm plantains. | Optionally, garnish with a sprinkle of cinnamon or fresh mint leaves before serving.

name: Banana Smoothie
description: A simple and creamy banana smoothie made with fresh banana and milk, sweetened optionally with honey. A popular refreshing beverage in many Latin American countries.
instructions: Peel the banana and cut it into slices. | Place the banana slices into a blender. | Add the milk and honey to the blender. | Blend the mixture until smooth and creamy. | Pour the smoothie into a glass and serve immediately.

name: Beef Fillet with Cream Sauce
description: A tender beef fillet pan-seared to perfection and served with a rich, creamy mustard sauce, ideal for an elegant main course.
instructions: Season the beef fillets with salt and pepper on both sides. | Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat until hot. | Sear the beef fillets in the skillet for about 3-4 minutes on each side for medium rare, or cook to desired doneness. | Remove the fillets from the skillet and set aside to rest. | In the same skillet, reduce the heat to medium and add butter. | Add chopped shallot and garlic, sauté until softened and fragrant. | Pour in white wine and cook until reduced by half. | Add heavy cream and Dijon mustard to the skillet, stirring to combine. | Simmer the sauce until it thickens slightly, about 5 minutes. | Season the cream sauce with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve the rested beef fillets topped with the cream sauce, garnished with chopped parsley.

name: Beef Heart Skewers Grilled
description: Grilled beef heart skewers marinated with garlic and spices, providing a flavorful and tender alternative cut of meat that is both nutritious and delicious.
instructions: Rinse the beef heart thoroughly and trim away any fat and membranes, then cut into 1-inch cubes. | In a bowl, combine olive oil, minced garlic, ground cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper to create the marinade. | Add the beef heart cubes to the marinade and toss to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight for better flavor. | Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes to prevent burning during grilling. | Preheat the grill to medium-high heat. | Thread the marinated beef heart cubes onto skewers, leaving a little space between pieces for even cooking. | Grill the skewers for about 3-4 minutes per side, turning to ensure all sides are nicely charred and cooked to medium-rare or desired doneness. | Remove the skewers from the grill and let them rest for a few minutes before serving. | Serve hot, optionally garnished with fresh parsley and accompanied by lemon wedges for squeezing over the meat.

name: Beef Liver with Onions
description: Beef Liver with Onions is a classic, hearty dish featuring tender slices of liver cooked to perfection and topped with sweet, caramelized onions, delivering a rich and flavorful experience.
instructions: Slice the beef liver into thin pieces and pat dry with paper towels. | Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. | Add the sliced onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until they are golden brown and caramelized, about 15 minutes. Remove the onions from the skillet and set aside. | Season the liver slices with salt and black pepper. | In the same skillet, add a little more oil if needed and cook the liver slices for about 2-3 minutes on each side until browned but still slightly pink inside. | Return the caramelized onions to the skillet with the liver, stir gently to combine, and cook for another minute to heat through. | Serve the liver topped with the caramelized onions.

name: Beef Meatballs Algarve Style
description: Beef Meatballs Algarve Style is a traditional Portuguese dish from the Algarve region featuring tender beef meatballs simmered in a fragrant tomato and white wine sauce flavored with garlic, paprika, and fresh herbs.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine ground beef, finely chopped onion, minced garlic, chopped parsley, breadcrumbs, beaten egg, salt, black pepper, and ground paprika. | Mix all ingredients thoroughly until well combined, but do not overmix to keep the meatballs tender. | Form the mixture into small, evenly sized meatballs, about 1.5 inches in diameter. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. | Add meatballs to the skillet and brown them on all sides, turning gently to avoid breaking. | Remove the meatballs and set aside. | In the same skillet, add chopped tomatoes, white wine, chopped garlic, bay leaf, and a pinch of ground cumin. | Simmer the sauce for about 10 minutes until it thickens slightly. | Return the meatballs to the skillet, cover, and simmer together for another 15-20 minutes, allowing the meatballs to cook through and absorb the sauce flavors. | Adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper as needed. | Serve hot with rice, crusty bread, or potatoes, garnished with fresh parsley.

name: Beef Oxtail Stew
description: Beef Oxtail Stew is a rich and hearty dish where oxtail is slow-cooked with vegetables, herbs, and red wine until tender, creating a flavorful and comforting meal.
instructions: Soak the oxtail pieces in cold water for 30 minutes to remove excess blood, then drain and pat dry. | Season the oxtail with salt and pepper. | Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the oxtail pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside. | In the same pot, add chopped onion, garlic, celery, and carrot, and cook until softened. | Add tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes while stirring. | Pour in red wine to deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits, and let it reduce by half. | Add beef broth, bay leaf, thyme, and the browned oxtail back into the pot. | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover, simmering for about 3 hours or until the oxtail is tender and meat is falling off the bone. | Remove the oxtail pieces, shred the meat off the bone, and discard bones and bay leaf. | Return shredded meat to the stew and add peeled and chopped potatoes and chopped parsley. | Simmer uncovered for another 30 minutes until the potatoes are cooked and the stew thickens slightly. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve hot, garnished with extra parsley if desired.

name: Beef Patties with Egg Inside
description: Beef patties wrapped around hard-boiled eggs, pan-fried to golden perfection, making a hearty and protein-rich main dish.
instructions: In a bowl, combine ground beef, finely chopped onion, minced garlic, salt, black pepper, and paprika. Mix thoroughly until well combined. | Divide the beef mixture into equal portions according to the number of eggs. | Shape each portion into a small patty, then flatten it to form a disc large enough to wrap around an egg. | Carefully place a hard-boiled egg in the center of each beef disc, then mold the beef around the egg, sealing it completely to form a patty with the egg inside. | Heat vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium heat. | Place the beef patties in the pan and cook for about 5-7 minutes on each side, or until the beef is fully cooked and browned outside. | Remove the patties from the pan and let them rest for a couple of minutes before serving.

name: Beef Ragout with Turnip
description: Beef Ragout with Turnip is a hearty stew featuring tender beef slow-cooked with turnip and aromatic vegetables, showcasing a rich, comforting flavor.
instructions: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes and season with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and brown the beef cubes on all sides, then remove and set aside. | In the same pot, add chopped onion, garlic, and carrots, and cook until softened. | Add tomato paste and cook for a minute while stirring. | Pour in red wine and let it simmer until reduced by half. | Return the beef to the pot, add beef broth, dried thyme, and bay leaf. | Peel and cut the turnip into cubes and add to the pot. | Cover and simmer gently on low heat for about 1.5 hours, or until the meat is tender and the sauce thickens. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. | Serve hot, garnished with chopped parsley.

name: Beef Ragu with Pasta
description: Beef Ragu with Pasta is a classic Italian meat sauce slowly simmered with tomatoes and herbs, served over pasta for a hearty and comforting meal.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat until shimmering. | Add finely chopped onion, carrot, and celery; sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Increase heat to medium-high; add ground beef and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until browned and no longer pink. | Pour in red wine and let it simmer until mostly evaporated. | Stir in crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, beef broth, dried oregano, dried thyme, salt, and pepper. | Lower heat to a gentle simmer, cover partially, and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and beef is tender. | Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook pasta according to package instructions until al dente. | Drain the pasta and mix with a few spoonfuls of the ragu sauce to coat. | Serve pasta topped with generous portions of beef ragu and sprinkle with grated Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley.

name: Beef Roulade with Ham
description: Beef Roulade with Ham is a classic European dish featuring thin beef slices rolled around ham, then seared and simmered in a flavorful broth, resulting in tender and savory rolls perfect for a hearty meal.
instructions: Lay the beef slices flat on a clean surface and season both sides with salt and pepper. | Place a slice of ham on each beef slice, covering the surface evenly. | Optionally, add a thin layer of mustard over the ham for extra flavor. | Roll up each beef slice tightly and secure it with kitchen twine or toothpicks. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. | Sear the beef roulades on all sides until evenly browned. | Remove the roulades and set aside. | Add chopped onion and carrot to the skillet and sauté until softened. | Pour in beef broth and scrape any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. | Return the roulades to the skillet, cover, and simmer gently for about 60 minutes or until the beef is tender. | Remove the roulades and keep warm. | Strain the sauce, return it to the skillet, and simmer until reduced and thickened slightly. | Slice the beef roulades and serve with the sauce spooned over. | Garnish with fresh parsley leaves before serving.

name: Beef Rump Roast with Potatoes
description: A classic roast beef rump served with tender roasted potatoes and carrots, enhanced by savory pan juices. This hearty dish is perfect for a comforting family meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Season the beef rump roast generously with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and dried rosemary. | Heat olive oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat. | Sear the beef roast on all sides until browned, about 3-4 minutes per side. | Remove the roast and set aside. | In the same skillet, add peeled and halved potato and carrot pieces; sauté for 5 minutes. | Add beef broth and bring to a simmer. | Place the roast back into the skillet on top of the vegetables. | Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and roast for about 1 hour or until the internal temperature reaches 60°C (140°F) for medium-rare. | Remove the roast and vegetables from the oven; cover loosely with foil and let rest for 15 minutes. | Slice the roast against the grain and serve with the roasted potatoes and carrots, spooning pan juices over the top.

name: Arroz Con Gambas
description: Arroz con Gambas is a traditional Spanish rice dish featuring succulent prawns cooked in a flavorful tomato and paprika-infused broth. This dish offers a vibrant taste of coastal Spain with tender rice and juicy prawns.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear and drain well. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet or paella pan over medium heat. | Add chopped onion and garlic, sauté until softened and translucent. | Add diced tomato and cook for a few minutes until the tomato breaks down. | Stir in the rice and coat it well with the tomato mixture and oil. | Pour in the fish stock and bring to a simmer. | Add smoked paprika, salt, and pepper, stirring gently to combine. | Simmer uncovered on medium-low heat for about 15 minutes without stirring, allowing the rice to absorb the liquid. | Distribute the peeled and deveined prawns evenly over the rice and continue cooking for another 5-7 minutes until the prawns are cooked through and the rice is tender. | If the liquid is absorbed too quickly and rice is not cooked, add a little more stock or water as needed. | Remove from heat and let it rest for 5 minutes covered with a clean kitchen towel. | Sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Arroz Con Garbanzos
description: Arroz con Garbanzos is a traditional Spanish rice dish combining chickpeas with aromatic spices, vegetables, and simmered to create a hearty, flavorful meal.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear and set aside. | Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. | Add chopped onion, minced garlic, and chopped tomato to the pan and sauté until softened and fragrant. | Stir in ground cumin and smoked paprika and cook for another minute. | Add rinsed chickpeas and cook for 2 minutes to combine flavors. | Pour in vegetable broth and bring to a boil. | Add rice and salt to the pan, stir well, then reduce heat to low and cover the pan with a lid. | Simmer gently for about 18-20 minutes until the rice is cooked and liquid absorbed. | Remove from heat and let it rest covered for 5 minutes. | Fluff the rice with a fork, garnish with chopped fresh parsley, and serve warm.

name: Arroz Con Habichuelas
description: Arroz con Habichuelas is a classic Latin American dish featuring seasoned rice cooked with kidney beans, onions, and bell peppers, delivering comforting and hearty flavors.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear and set aside to drain. | Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté chopped onion, bell pepper, and garlic until soft and fragrant. | Add the tomato sauce, ground cumin, dried oregano, salt, and pepper to the pot and cook for a few minutes to combine the flavors. | Add the rinsed rice to the pot and stir well to coat it with the sauce and vegetables. | Pour in the chicken broth and bring the mixture to a boil. | Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let the rice simmer for about 15 minutes. | In a separate saucepan, heat the canned kidney beans with their liquid gently over low heat, seasoning with salt, pepper, and a pinch of cumin if desired. | When the rice is done, fluff it with a fork and gently fold in the cooked beans. | Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro and serve hot.

name: Arroz Con Leche
description: Arroz con Leche is a traditional Spanish rice pudding made by slowly cooking rice in milk with sugar, cinnamon, and lemon zest, resulting in a creamy and comforting dessert.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear to remove excess starch. | In a large saucepan, combine the rice, water, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil over medium heat. | Reduce the heat to low and simmer the rice, covered, until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender, about 15 minutes. | Add the milk, sugar, and cinnamon stick to the cooked rice in the saucepan. | Cook over low heat, stirring frequently to prevent sticking, until the mixture thickens to a creamy consistency, about 20-25 minutes. | Remove from heat and discard the cinnamon stick. | Allow the rice pudding to cool slightly, then stir in the lemon zest and vanilla extract. | Serve warm or chilled, sprinkled with ground cinnamon on top as a garnish if desired.

name: Arroz Con Leche Asturiano
description: Arroz con Leche Asturiano is a traditional creamy rice pudding from Asturias, Spain, flavored with cinnamon and lemon peel, offering a comforting and sweet dessert experience.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear. | In a large pot, combine the milk, sugar, cinnamon sticks, lemon peel, and a pinch of salt. | Heat the mixture over medium heat until it begins to simmer, stirring occasionally to prevent the milk from burning. | Add the rinsed rice to the pot and reduce the heat to low, allowing the mixture to simmer gently. | Cook the rice in the milk mixture, stirring frequently to avoid sticking, until the rice is tender and the pudding has thickened, about 40 to 45 minutes. | Remove the pot from heat and discard the cinnamon sticks and lemon peel. | Stir in the butter and vanilla extract until fully incorporated and smooth. | Pour the rice pudding into individual serving dishes and sprinkle with ground cinnamon. | Let the pudding cool slightly before serving warm or at room temperature. It can also be chilled if preferred.

name: Arroz Con Leche Quemado
description: Arroz con Leche Quemado is a traditional Spanish-style rice pudding with a creamy texture topped with a crisp burnt sugar layer created by torching, adding a delightful caramelized flavor and texture contrast.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear to remove excess starch. | In a medium saucepan, combine the rice, whole milk, and water. Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat. | Reduce the heat to low and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the rice is tender and has absorbed most of the liquid, about 20-25 minutes. | Add the sugar, cinnamon stick, and a pinch of salt to the rice mixture. Stir well to combine. | Continue to cook over low heat, stirring frequently, until the mixture thickens to a creamy consistency, about 10 minutes. | Remove the cinnamon stick and stir in the heavy cream and vanilla extract. Cook for an additional 2 minutes. | Ladle the rice pudding into shallow, heatproof ramekins or a wide, shallow dish, spreading it evenly. | Sprinkle an even layer of granulated sugar over the top of the pudding to cover the surface. | Using a kitchen torch, carefully caramelize the sugar by moving the flame evenly over the surface until the sugar melts and turns a deep amber color, forming a crisp burnt top. | Let the pudding sit for a few minutes to allow the toffee crust to harden before serving.

name: Arroz Con Mejillones
description: Arroz con Mejillones is a flavorful Spanish dish featuring rice cooked with tender mussels and infused with aromatic spices like saffron and smoked paprika.
instructions: Clean the mussels thoroughly by scrubbing the shells and removing the beards. | Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat and sauté chopped onion, garlic, and bell pepper until softened. | Add diced tomato and cook for a few minutes until the tomato breaks down. | Stir in the rice and coat it well with the vegetable mixture. | Pour in fish broth and season with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, and saffron threads. | Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, partially covered, for about 15 minutes. | Add the cleaned mussels on top of the rice, cover the pan, and cook for an additional 5-7 minutes until the mussels open. | Discard any mussels that do not open. | Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and serve hot.

name: Arroz Con Pato
description: Arroz con Pato is a traditional Latin American dish featuring tender duck cooked with rice and a flavorful blend of herbs and spices, resulting in a hearty and aromatic meal.
instructions: Marinate the duck pieces with garlic, cumin, salt, and pepper. Set aside for at least 30 minutes. | Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and brown the marinated duck pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside. | In the same pot, add diced onion, chopped red bell pepper, and garlic; sauté until softened. | Add diced tomato paste and cook for a few minutes until the mixture thickens. | Pour in some beer and let it simmer for 5 minutes to develop flavor. | Return the duck pieces to the pot and add chopped cilantro, chopped parsley, and chopped oregano. | Pour in duck broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. | Cover and simmer the duck until tender, about 45 minutes to 1 hour. | Once the duck is tender, remove the duck pieces and set aside, shredding some meat off the bones and reserving the broth. | Add washed rice to the pot with the broth, stir, and cook the rice until tender and liquid absorbed, about 20 minutes. | Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a skillet and gently brown the shredded duck meat. | When the rice is cooked, mix in the browned shredded duck, adjusting seasoning with salt and pepper. | Let the rice rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Arroz Con Pimientos
description: Arroz con Pimientos is a flavorful Spanish-inspired rice dish featuring sautéed bell peppers and aromatic seasonings, perfect as a vibrant and comforting main or side dish.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. | Add chopped onion and garlic and sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. | Add diced bell peppers and cook for 5 minutes until they begin to soften. | Stir in the rice and cook, stirring frequently, for 2 minutes to toast the rice lightly. | Pour in the chicken broth and add salt, pepper, and smoked paprika. | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover the skillet. | Simmer for 15-20 minutes until the rice is cooked and liquid absorbed. | Remove from heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes. | Fluff the rice with a fork and stir in chopped parsley before serving.

name: Arroz Con Pollo
description: Arroz con Pollo (Spanish Chicken with Rice) is a traditional Spanish dish featuring seasoned chicken cooked with rice, vegetables, and saffron, known for its rich flavors and vibrant colors.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet or paella pan over medium heat. | Season chicken pieces with salt and pepper, then brown them in the hot oil until golden on all sides. Remove and set aside. | In the same pan, sauté chopped onion, garlic, and bell pepper until softened. | Add diced tomato and cook until the mixture thickens slightly. | Stir in rice and cook for a few minutes, coating the rice in the oil and vegetables. | Pour in chicken broth and add saffron threads, paprika, and salt. Stir to combine. | Return the browned chicken pieces to the pan, distributing them evenly. | Cover and simmer on low heat until the rice is cooked and the chicken is tender, about 20 minutes. | Add frozen peas in the last 5 minutes of cooking and cook until heated through. | Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Gaeng Aom Isan
description: Gaeng Aom Isan is a traditional sour and herbal soup from the Isan region of Thailand, known for its fresh herbs, sour flavors, and light, aromatic broth.
instructions: Prepare the broth by boiling water with lemongrass stalks, kaffir lime leaves, galangal slices, dried chilies, and shallot. Simmer for 20 minutes to infuse the flavors and then strain the broth to remove solids. | Add thinly sliced indigo bush leaves (or substitute with spinach if unavailable), pennywort leaves, and fresh dill into the strained broth. | Add fish sauce and lime juice to season the soup to a balanced salty and sour taste. | Optionally, add small pieces of fish or shrimp for protein, simmer until cooked through. | Serve hot garnished with fresh coriander and additional lime wedges on the side.

name: Gaeng Bon
description: Gaeng Bon is a traditional Northern Thai curry featuring tender taro stems and aromatic local herbs simmered in a rich coconut milk base with a flavorful shrimp paste curry paste.
instructions: Prepare the taro stems by peeling and cutting them into 2-inch pieces. Rinse thoroughly to remove any dirt. | In a mortar and pestle, pound the chili, garlic, and shrimp paste into a smooth curry paste. | Heat vegetable oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the curry paste and stir-fry until fragrant. | Add coconut milk and bring to a simmer, stirring to combine with the curry paste. | Add the taro stems and stir well. Pour in the water and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the taro stems are tender, about 20 minutes. | Add the sliced northern herbs (such as holy basil, culantro, or other available local herbs) and cook for another 5 minutes. | Season with fish sauce and palm sugar to balance salty and sweet flavors. Adjust seasoning as needed. | Serve the curry hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Gaeng Bon Taro Stem Curry
description: Gaeng Bon Taro Stem Curry is a traditional Northern Thai curry featuring tender taro stems cooked in a rich and aromatic coconut-based curry paste with dried chilies and local spices, delivering a unique regional flavor experience.
instructions: Wash and peel the taro stem, then cut into 2-inch pieces and soak in water to remove slime. | Prepare the curry paste by pounding dry red chilies soaked until soft, garlic, shallot, dried shrimp, coriander root, cumin seed, peppercorn, and salt until a smooth paste forms. | Heat vegetable oil in a wok over medium heat and fry the curry paste until aromatic, about 2-3 minutes. | Add coconut milk and stir well, bringing it to a gentle boil. | Add the taro stem pieces and cook until tender, about 10-15 minutes. | Add fish sauce and palm sugar to balance the salty and sweet flavors. | Simmer the curry until the taro stems are fully cooked and the flavors are well blended. | Garnish with fresh herbs like cilantro or Thai basil before serving as desired.

name: Gaeng Hang Lay
description: Gaeng Hang Lay is a classic Northern Thai pork curry, rich in aromatic spices and tamarind, known for its unique blend of flavors and tender pork.
instructions: Place pork pieces in a pot with water and bring to a boil. Skim off any scum, then simmer until pork is tender, about 1-1.5 hours. Drain and set aside the pork and broth separately. | In a dry pan, lightly toast dried red chili, coriander seed, cumin seed, garlic, shallot, and galangal until fragrant. Grind toasted spices and herbs into a fine powder using a mortar and pestle or spice grinder. | Heat vegetable oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the curry paste and sauté until fragrant. | Add pork pieces to the pot and stir to coat with the curry paste. | Pour in about 500 ml of pork broth or water. Add tamarind juice, fish sauce, palm sugar, and sliced ginger. | Simmer the curry for about 30 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly. | Taste and adjust seasoning with additional fish sauce or sugar if needed. | Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice and fresh coriander garnish.

name: Gaeng Hed
description: Gaeng Hed, or Mushroom Forest Curry, is a traditional Thai curry featuring a rich and fragrant coconut milk base with an aromatic homemade curry paste and a variety of mushrooms, offering an earthy and savory dish popular in Thai cuisine.
instructions: Clean and slice the mushrooms into bite-sized pieces. | Prepare the curry paste by blending together garlic, shallots, dried red chilies, lemongrass, galangal, coriander root, cumin seeds, and shrimp paste until smooth. | Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large pan over medium heat and fry the curry paste until fragrant, about 2-3 minutes. | Add coconut milk to the pan and bring it to a gentle boil, stirring to combine with the curry paste. | Add the sliced mushrooms to the curry and simmer for 5-7 minutes until the mushrooms are tender and have absorbed the curry flavors. | Season the curry with fish sauce and palm sugar, adjusting to taste for a balanced salty and sweet flavor. | Add Thai basil leaves and kaffir lime leaves to the curry and cook for another minute to release their aroma. | Remove the curry from heat and serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Gaeng Hed Khon Muang
description: Gaeng Hed Khon Muang is a traditional Northern Thai curry featuring dried local mushrooms simmered in a fragrant and spicy coconut milk curry paste with fresh herbs, highlighting the unique flavors of the region.
instructions: Clean and soak the dried northern mushrooms in warm water for 20 minutes until softened, then drain and slice them if large. | In a mortar and pestle or blender, pound or blend lemongrass, galangal, coriander root, dried red chili, garlic, and shrimp paste into a smooth curry paste. | Heat vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat and stir-fry the curry paste until fragrant. | Add coconut milk and bring to a gentle boil, stirring occasionally. | Add the softened northern mushrooms, mushroom stems, and kaffir lime leaves to the pan, and simmer for 10-15 minutes until the mushrooms are tender and the flavors are blended. | Season the curry with fish sauce and palm sugar to balance the salty and sweet flavors. | Add Thai basil leaves and stir for another minute before turning off the heat. | Serve the northern mushroom curry hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Gaeng Heed Baan
description: Gaeng Heed Baan is a traditional spicy and aromatic village mushroom curry from the Isan region of Thailand, featuring local mushrooms simmered in a fragrant coconut milk broth with herbs and spices.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a pot over medium heat. | Add sliced shallot, sliced garlic, and sliced fresh galangal; sauté until fragrant. | Add sliced fresh chili and chopped lemongrass; continue to stir for 1-2 minutes. | Add the chopped village mushrooms and stir well to coat with the aromatics. | Pour in coconut milk and water; bring the mixture to a gentle boil. | Add kaffir lime leaves and crushed roasted rice powder; stir to combine. | Season with fish sauce and palm sugar; adjust to taste balancing salty and sweet flavors. | Simmer the curry on low heat until mushrooms are tender and flavors meld, about 15 minutes. | Garnish with fresh Thai basil leaves before serving.

name: Gaeng Ho
description: Gaeng Ho is a traditional Northern Thai mixed curry featuring a fragrant and spicy curry paste combined with chicken and a variety of vegetables, resulting in a rich and aromatic dish.
instructions: Prepare all the ingredients by washing and cutting the vegetables and meat into bite-sized pieces. | Toast dried chilies in a dry pan until fragrant, then soak them in warm water until soft, about 15 minutes. | Grind the soaked chilies with garlic, shallot, galangal, lemongrass, coriander root, cumin seed, turmeric, and shrimp paste into a smooth curry paste using a mortar and pestle or food processor. | Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat, then add the curry paste and fry until fragrant, about 3-5 minutes. | Add the chicken pieces to the pot and stir to coat with the curry paste, cooking until the chicken is lightly browned. | Pour in enough water or chicken broth to cover the ingredients, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer. | Add the chopped vegetables such as eggplant, bamboo shoots, and long beans to the pot. | Simmer the curry gently until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender, about 20 minutes. | Season the curry with fish sauce and palm sugar to balance the flavors, adjusting to taste. | Finally, stir in the chopped fresh basil and cilantro leaves, then turn off the heat. | Serve the Gaeng Ho Northern Mixed Curry hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Gaeng Hung Lay
description: Gaeng Hung Lay is a traditional Northern Thai pork curry known for its rich flavors combining ginger, garlic, tamarind, and unique curry paste. This dish offers a sweet, tangy, and slightly spicy taste typical of Northern Thai cuisine.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat and add sliced ginger and garlic. Sauté until fragrant. | Add thinly sliced pork shoulder to the pan and cook until browned on all sides. | Add gaeng hung lay curry paste to the pork and stir well to coat the meat evenly. Cook for a few minutes until the paste is aromatic. | Pour in water and tamarind paste, stir to combine, and bring to a simmer. | Lower the heat, cover the pan, and let it cook gently for about 1 hour until the pork is tender. | Add palm sugar and fish sauce to the curry. Adjust seasoning with salt if necessary. | Add sliced shallots and continue to simmer uncovered for another 15 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly. | Serve hot garnished with fresh cilantro and accompany with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Gaeng Isan
description: Gaeng Isan is a spicy and aromatic mixed curry from the Isan region of Thailand, featuring a vibrant homemade curry paste with pork and a variety of fresh vegetables, creating a uniquely flavorful and traditional Thai dish.
instructions: Prepare the herbs by soaking the dried chillies in warm water until soft, then drain them. | In a mortar and pestle or food processor, pound or grind the soaked chillies, garlic, shallot, lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime zest, coriander root, and roasted dry rice until you get a fine curry paste. | Heat a pot over medium heat and add the mixed curry paste, stirring until fragrant. | Add the pork and cook until it changes color. | Pour in the pork broth and bring it to a boil. | Add the straw mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes. | Add the sliced eggplant and simmer until tender. | Add fish sauce and palm sugar to taste, balancing salty and sweet flavors. | Add the chopped kaffir lime leaves and Thai basil leaves just before turning off the heat. | Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Arabaşı Soup
description: Arabaşı Soup is a traditional chicken and dough soup from Kastamonu, Turkey, featuring hand-rolled wheat dough cooked in rich chicken broth, known for its comforting and hearty taste.
instructions: Mix the wheat flour and warm water in a large bowl to form a smooth, thick dough. Cover and let it rest while preparing the broth. | In a large pot, add the chicken pieces and cover with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook until the chicken is tender, about 45 minutes. | Remove the chicken from the broth and set aside to cool. Strain the broth to remove impurities and return the clear broth to the pot. | Shred the cooled chicken into small pieces and return some of it to the broth for flavor. | Shape the rested dough into thin, flat sheets or ribbons by rolling it out and cutting it thinly. | Bring the broth to a gentle boil and add the dough strips carefully to avoid sticking. | Cook the dough in the broth until it becomes tender and floats to the surface, about 8-10 minutes. | Season the soup with salt, crushed red pepper, and if desired, add a drizzle of melted butter or chili oil for extra flavor. | Serve hot, garnished with the shredded chicken and optionally fresh parsley for a fresh touch.

name: Armut Tatlisi
description: Armut Tatlisi is a traditional Turkish dessert featuring tender pears poached in a fragrant syrup with cinnamon and lemon, served with optional crushed nuts for texture.
instructions: Peel the pears and cut them in half, removing the cores carefully to keep the halves intact. | Place the pear halves in a large pot and add water, sugar, lemon juice, and cinnamon stick to make the syrup. | Bring the mixture to a boil over medium heat, then reduce the heat and let it simmer until the pears are tender and the syrup thickens, about 20-30 minutes. | Remove the pot from heat and let the pears cool in the syrup to absorb the flavors. | Arrange the pear halves on serving plates and drizzle some of the syrup over them. | Optionally, garnish with crushed walnuts or pistachios before serving.

name: Arnavut Boregi
description: Arnavut Boregi is a traditional Albanian-style savory pastry made with phyllo dough filled with a mixture of mashed potatoes, ground beef, feta cheese, and herbs, baked to golden perfection.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and mash them well in a bowl. | Heat butter in a pan, add chopped onion and sauté until translucent, then add ground beef and cook until browned. Season with salt and pepper and set aside to cool. | In a large bowl, combine the mashed potatoes, cooked ground beef mixture, crumbled feta cheese, and chopped parsley. Mix well to form the filling. | Lay out one sheet of phyllo dough on a clean surface, brushing it lightly with melted butter. | Spread a thin layer of the filling over the phyllo sheet evenly. | Roll the phyllo sheet tightly into a log shape. | Curve the rolled log into a spiral (like a snail shell) and place it onto a greased baking tray. | Repeat the layering, filling, rolling, and spiraling steps with the remaining phyllo sheets and filling until all the mixture is used. | Brush the top of the pastries generously with melted butter. | Bake in the preheated oven for 35-40 minutes or until the phyllo is golden brown and crisp. | Remove from the oven and let it cool slightly before slicing and serving.

name: Arnavut Cigeri
description: Arnavut Cigeri is a traditional Albanian dish featuring bite-sized pieces of liver, seasoned, floured, and fried until crispy, then topped with sautéed onions and parsley. It is typically served with lemon wedges for added zest.
instructions: Rinse the liver under cold water and pat dry with paper towels. Cut the liver into bite-sized cubes about 2 cm in size. | Heat vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium heat for frying the liver. | In a bowl, combine the flour, salt, and black pepper. Dredge each piece of liver in the seasoned flour, shaking off excess. | Carefully place the floured liver pieces into the hot oil and fry until golden brown and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes per side. Avoid overcrowding the pan; fry in batches if necessary. | Once cooked, remove the liver pieces with a slotted spoon and place on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil. | In a separate pan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent and soft, about 5 minutes. | Add the finely chopped parsley to the softened onion and sauté for 1 more minute. | Arrange the fried liver on a serving plate. Spoon the onion and parsley mixture over the liver. | Serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side to squeeze over the dish if desired.

name: Artichoke Heart Salad
description: A fresh and tangy Turkish-style salad featuring tender artichoke hearts dressed with olive oil, lemon, garlic, and fresh parsley, perfect as a light side dish.
instructions: Drain the canned artichoke hearts and cut them into halves or quarters if large. | In a bowl, combine olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, salt, and black pepper to prepare the dressing. | Add chopped fresh parsley to the dressing and mix well. | Place the artichoke hearts in a serving bowl and pour the dressing over them. | Toss gently to coat all pieces evenly with the dressing. | Chill the salad in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld. | Before serving, optionally garnish with thinly sliced red onion and additional parsley leaves.

name: Artichoke Rice Pilaf
description: Artichoke Rice Pilaf is a traditional Turkish dish that combines tender artichokes with fluffy rice, sautéed in olive oil and cooked in vegetable broth. This flavorful and aromatic pilaf makes a delicious vegetarian main course or side dish.
instructions: Clean the artichokes by removing tough outer leaves and trimming the stems. Cut them into quarters and soak in water with lemon juice to prevent browning. | Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain well. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet or pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent. | Add the artichoke pieces to the skillet and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. | Add the rice to the skillet and stir to coat with the oil and mix with the onions and artichokes. | Pour in the vegetable broth and season with salt and pepper. Bring to a boil. | Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for about 15-20 minutes until the rice is cooked and all the liquid is absorbed. | Remove from heat and let it rest covered for 5 minutes. | Fluff the rice pilaf gently with a fork and transfer to a serving dish. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Artichoke Soup
description: Enginar Çorbası is a traditional Turkish artichoke soup that is creamy and flavored with lemon, offering a light and refreshing taste perfect as a starter or light meal.
instructions: Clean the artichokes by removing tough outer leaves and trimming the stems and tips of the remaining leaves. | Rub the cleaned artichokes with lemon to prevent browning and then finely chop them. | In a pot, melt the butter over medium heat and sauté the chopped onion until translucent. | Add the chopped artichokes to the pot and cook for a few minutes, stirring occasionally. | Pour in the water and chicken broth, bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the artichokes are tender, approximately 20-25 minutes. | Use an immersion blender to puree the soup until smooth and creamy. | Return the pot to low heat, stir in the lemon juice and heavy cream, and warm through without boiling. | Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste. | Serve the soup hot, optionally garnished with a sprig of dill or parsley.

name: Artichoke Stew with Meat
description: A traditional Turkish stew featuring tender beef and fresh artichokes, slowly cooked to bring out rich, comforting flavors.
instructions: Wash the artichokes thoroughly and trim the outer tough leaves. Remove the hairy choke inside and cut the artichokes into quarters. | Peel and chop the onion finely. Peel and grate the carrot. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and grated carrot and sauté until softened. | Add the meat pieces to the pot and cook until browned on all sides. | Season with salt and black pepper to taste, then add the tomato paste and stir well to combine. | Pour in the water or meat broth and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer for about 30 minutes until the meat is tender. | Add the prepared artichokes to the pot, cover, and cook for another 20-25 minutes until artichokes are tender. | Adjust seasoning if needed and sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving.

name: Artichoke in Olive Oil
description: Zeytinyağlı Enginar is a Turkish dish of tender artichokes cooked gently in olive oil, lemon, and herbs, served cold or at room temperature as a refreshing and healthy side dish.
instructions: Peel the artichoke by removing tough outer leaves and trim the stems and tips, then immediately place them in water with lemon to prevent browning. | Chop the onion finely and sauté it in a pot with olive oil until soft and translucent. | Add the artichokes to the pot and gently stir to combine with the sautéed onions. | Pour water and freshly squeezed lemon juice into the pot, then season with salt and sugar, stirring gently to mix. | Cover the pot and let the artichokes simmer on low heat until tender, about 30-40 minutes. | Once cooked, let the artichokes cool in their cooking liquid to absorb flavors. | Serve the artichokes chilled or at room temperature, drizzled with a little extra olive oil and garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

name: Artvin Cornmeal Halva
description: Artvin Cornmeal Halva is a traditional Turkish dessert from Artvin region made by toasting cornmeal and cooking it with sugar syrup and butter to create a rich, nutty, and sweet treat.
instructions: Toast the cornmeal in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring constantly until it becomes aromatic and golden brown, about 10-15 minutes. | In a separate saucepan, bring the water and sugar to a boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves completely to make a syrup. | Heat the butter in a large pan over medium heat until melted. | Slowly add the toasted cornmeal to the melted butter, stirring continuously to coat the cornmeal and prevent clumping. | Gradually pour the hot sugar syrup into the cornmeal mixture while stirring constantly to combine. | Reduce the heat to low and cook the mixture, stirring frequently, until it thickens and starts to pull away from the sides of the pan, about 10-15 minutes. | Remove from heat and let it rest, covered, for a few minutes to allow the halva to set. | Scoop the halva onto a serving dish and garnish with chopped walnuts if desired. | Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: BBQ Chicken Thighs
description: Grilled BBQ chicken thighs marinated with spices and coated with barbecue sauce for a smoky, flavorful dish.
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat. | In a bowl, mix olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, chili powder, salt, pepper, and brown sugar to create a marinade. | Coat the chicken thighs thoroughly with the marinade and let them marinate for at least 30 minutes or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator. | Place the chicken thighs on the preheated grill, skin side down, and cook for about 6-7 minutes until the skin is crispy and has grill marks. | Flip the chicken thighs and brush generously with barbecue sauce. | Continue grilling for another 6-7 minutes, brushing with barbecue sauce every few minutes, until the internal temperature reaches 75°C (165°F). | Remove the chicken thighs from the grill and let them rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: BBQ Loaded Baked Potato
description: BBQ Loaded Baked Potato is a hearty and flavorful dish featuring baked potatoes topped with barbecue sauce, shredded meat, melted cheese, and fresh garnishes, perfect for a comforting meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees Celsius (400 degrees Fahrenheit). | Wash the potatoes thoroughly and prick them several times with a fork. | Rub the potatoes with olive oil and sprinkle with salt. | Place the potatoes directly on the oven rack and bake for about 45 to 60 minutes until tender when pierced with a fork. | While the potatoes bake, heat the barbecue sauce in a small saucepan over low heat. | Once baked, remove the potatoes from the oven and let them cool slightly. | Cut a slit lengthwise across the top of each potato and gently squeeze the sides to open them up. | Fluff the inside of the potatoes with a fork, then spoon in the barbecue sauce. | Top each potato with cooked and shredded barbecue chicken or pulled pork. | Sprinkle shredded Cheddar cheese over the meat and potatoes, then return to the oven for 5-7 minutes until the cheese melts. | Remove from the oven and top with chopped green onion, sour cream, and bacon bits. | Serve hot as a hearty main dish.

name: BBQ Meat Platter Combo
description: A hearty platter featuring a variety of grilled barbecue meats including ribs, brisket, sausage, and chicken, seasoned with a smoky dry rub and basted with flavorful barbecue sauce. Perfect for sharing and enjoying a classic BBQ meal combo.
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat. | Season the various cuts of meat (such as ribs, brisket, sausage, and chicken) with a dry rub consisting of salt, pepper, paprika, garlic powder, and brown sugar. | Place the meats on the grill, starting with the cuts that take the longest to cook, like ribs and brisket. | Grill the meats slowly for about 1.5 to 2 hours, turning occasionally and basting with barbecue sauce during the last 30 minutes to add flavor and moisture. | Grill the sausages and chicken pieces for 15 to 20 minutes each, ensuring they are cooked through and have nice grill marks. | Once all meats are cooked, let them rest for 10 minutes before slicing. | Arrange the sliced brisket, ribs, sausage, and chicken pieces on a large platter. | Serve the meat platter combo with additional barbecue sauce on the side and optional sides such as coleslaw, baked beans, or cornbread if desired.

name: BBQ Nachos with Brisket
description: BBQ Nachos with Brisket is a hearty and flavorful snack combining smoky shredded brisket, melted Cheddar, and classic nacho toppings for a satisfying treat.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). | Spread tortilla chips evenly on a large baking sheet or oven-safe platter. | Evenly distribute shredded cooked brisket over the chips. | Sprinkle black beans over the brisket and chips. | Generously sprinkle shredded Cheddar cheese over the entire surface. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 10 minutes or until the cheese is fully melted and bubbly. | Remove from oven and top with diced tomato, sliced jalapeno, and chopped red onion. | Drizzle barbecue sauce evenly over the nachos and add dollops of sour cream. | Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro before serving.

name: BBQ Pork Belly Burnt Ends
description: BBQ Pork Belly Burnt Ends are smoky, caramelized cubes of pork belly slow-smoked and coated in a flavorful dry rub and barbecue sauce, offering a rich and tender bite-sized treat.
instructions: Cut the pork belly into 1.5-inch cubes for even cooking. | In a bowl, mix brown sugar, paprika, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and chili powder to create the dry rub. | Toss the pork belly cubes in the dry rub until all pieces are evenly coated. | Preheat the smoker to 110°C (225°F). | Place the coated pork belly cubes on a wire rack and set them in the smoker. | Smoke the pork belly cubes for about 2 hours, until they develop a good bark and internal temperature reaches around 70°C (160°F). | Remove the pork belly cubes from the smoker and place them in an aluminum tray. | Drizzle barbecue sauce and honey over the pork belly cubes and toss to coat evenly. | Cover the tray with foil and return it to the smoker. | Continue cooking for another 1 to 1.5 hours until the pork belly is tender and caramelized. | Remove from the smoker and let rest for 10 minutes before serving. | Serve the burnt ends as a flavorful appetizer or main dish.

name: BBQ Pork Chops
description: BBQ pork chops are juicy and flavorful grilled pork chops basted with a smoky barbecue sauce, perfect for a quick and tasty meal.
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat. | In a small bowl, mix barbecue sauce, olive oil, garlic, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper to create the marinade. | Brush the pork chops with the marinade on both sides and let them sit for 10 minutes to absorb the flavors. | Place the pork chops on the grill and cook for 5-7 minutes on each side or until the internal temperature reaches 145°F (63°C). | During grilling, occasionally brush more barbecue sauce on the pork chops to enhance the flavor. | Remove the pork chops from the grill and let them rest for 3-5 minutes before serving to retain the juices.

name: BBQ Pulled Chicken
description: BBQ pulled chicken is a tender and flavorful dish where chicken breasts are slow-cooked in barbecue sauce and shredded, perfect for sandwiches or as a main dish.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C (320°F). | Place chicken breasts in a baking dish and season with salt and pepper. | Pour barbecue sauce evenly over the chicken breasts. | Cover the baking dish tightly with foil and bake in the preheated oven for 2 hours until the chicken is tender and easily shredded. | Remove the chicken from the oven and shred it using two forks in the baking dish, mixing with the barbecue sauce to coat evenly. | If desired, return the shredded chicken to the oven uncovered for an additional 10 minutes to thicken the sauce. | Serve the BBQ pulled chicken on buns, over rice, or as desired.

name: BBQ Pulled Jackfruit
description: BBQ pulled jackfruit is a popular vegan alternative to pulled pork, featuring young jackfruit cooked in smoky barbecue sauce for a flavorful and tender dish perfect for sandwiches.
instructions: Drain and rinse the canned jackfruit thoroughly, then pat dry with a clean towel. | Using your hands or two forks, shred the jackfruit to create a pulled meat texture, removing any seeds or tough core pieces. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, then add the shredded jackfruit and cook for about 5 minutes until slightly browned. | Add chopped onion and minced garlic to the skillet, cooking until softened and fragrant, about 3 minutes. | Stir in smoked paprika, chili powder, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper to the jackfruit mixture, coating evenly. | Pour in the barbecue sauce and apple cider vinegar, stirring to combine. | Reduce the heat to low and simmer the mixture for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken, stirring occasionally. | Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. | Serve the BBQ pulled jackfruit on toasted hamburger buns or as desired, garnished with coleslaw if preferred.

name: BBQ Pulled Pork Mac and Cheese
description: A comforting American-inspired dish combining creamy macaroni and cheese with smoky, tender BBQ pulled pork baked to perfection with a crispy topping.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Cook the macaroni pasta in boiling salted water until al dente, then drain and set aside. | In a large saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat, then whisk in the flour to create a roux, cooking for about 2 minutes without browning. | Gradually whisk in the milk and cream, stirring continuously until the mixture thickens and becomes smooth. | Remove from heat and stir in the shredded Cheddar cheese and grated Parmesan until fully melted and combined. Season with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika. | Mix the cooked macaroni into the cheese sauce until evenly coated. | Gently fold in the pulled pork and about half of the barbecue sauce to ensure the pork is well coated. | Transfer the mac and cheese mixture into a baking dish. Drizzle the remaining barbecue sauce on top and sprinkle extra Cheddar cheese and crispy fried onions over the surface. | Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes until bubbly and golden on top. | Remove from oven and let rest for 5 minutes before serving. | Serve warm, optionally garnished with chopped parsley.

name: BBQ Rib Tips
description: BBQ rib tips are flavorful, tender pieces of pork ribs cooked with smoky barbecue sauce, perfect for grilling and casual meals.
instructions: Preheat your grill to medium-high heat. | In a bowl, combine your favorite barbecue sauce with a little honey or brown sugar for sweetness if desired. | Season rib tips with salt, pepper, and smoked paprika. | Place the rib tips on the grill and cook for about 10 minutes per side, turning occasionally to avoid burning. | During the last 10-15 minutes, brush the rib tips generously with barbecue sauce while turning to coat evenly. | You can also finish the rib tips in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 20 minutes if you want them extra tender. | Remove from grill or oven and let rest for a few minutes before serving. | Serve hot with extra barbecue sauce and your choice of sides.

name: Beef Paupiettes
description: Beef paupiettes are thin beef slices rolled around a savory herb and breadcrumb stuffing, then braised until tender and served with reduced pan sauce. This classic French dish offers a flavorful and elegant main course.
instructions: Slice the onion and garlic thinly. | Wash and dry the parsley, then chop finely. | In a bowl, mix chopped parsley with minced onion and garlic, breadcrumbs, and egg. | Place beef slices flat on a clean surface, season with salt and pepper. | Spread the stuffing mixture evenly over each beef slice. | Roll up each beef slice tightly, securing with kitchen twine or toothpicks if necessary. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. | Brown the beef rolls on all sides until nicely seared. | Add sliced carrots and celery to the skillet and sauté briefly. | Pour in beef broth and bay leaf, bring to a simmer. | Cover and cook on low heat for about 45 minutes, turning occasionally. | Remove the rolls and keep warm. | Increase heat and reduce the cooking liquid to a sauce consistency. | Season the sauce with salt and pepper as needed. | Serve the beef paupiettes topped with the sauce, garnished with fresh parsley.

name: Beef Pavé with Bearnaise Sauce
description: Beef pavé is a prime cut of beef cooked to perfection and served with a rich and creamy French béarnaise sauce made from egg yolks, butter, and fresh tarragon. This classic French dish highlights exquisite flavors and elegant presentation.
instructions: Remove the beef pavé from the refrigerator and let it come to room temperature for 30 minutes. | Season the beef pavé generously with salt and freshly ground black pepper on all sides. | Heat a heavy skillet over medium-high heat and add the butter and olive oil. | When the butter is melted and foaming, sear the beef pavé on all sides until browned, about 3-4 minutes per side. | Transfer the seared beef to a baking sheet and finish cooking in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for about 10-15 minutes for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. | Remove the beef from the oven and let it rest for 10 minutes before slicing. | Meanwhile, prepare the béarnaise sauce: in a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, water, chopped shallot, fresh tarragon, and peppercorns. | Bring to a simmer and reduce the liquid by half. Strain and set aside the vinegar reduction. | In a heatproof bowl set over a pot of simmering water, whisk together egg yolks and the vinegar reduction until the mixture thickens and doubles in volume. | Slowly drizzle in melted butter while continuously whisking until the sauce is thick and creamy. | Stir in chopped fresh tarragon and season with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve slices of beef pavé topped with warm béarnaise sauce and garnish with a sprig of tarragon.

name: Beef Ragout
description: Beef ragout is a classic slow-cooked meat stew originating from European cuisine, known for its rich flavor and tender beef chunks simmered in a savory sauce.
instructions: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes and season with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and brown the beef cubes on all sides in batches. Remove and set aside. | In the same pot, add diced onion, carrot, and celery, and sauté until softened. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Return the beef to the pot and sprinkle with flour, stirring to coat the meat evenly. | Pour in red wine and beef broth, scraping the bottom of the pot to deglaze and lift browned bits. | Add tomato paste, bay leaf, and dried thyme, then bring to a simmer. | Cover the pot and simmer gently for about 2 hours or until the beef is tender, stirring occasionally. | About 15 minutes before serving, add chopped fresh parsley and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed. | Serve the ragout hot, optionally over mashed potatoes, polenta, or pasta.

name: Beef Tongue with Piquant Sauce
description: A traditional dish featuring tender beef tongue served with a tangy and spicy piquant sauce, combining rich flavors for a distinctive meal.
