instructions: Simmer the beef tongue in a large pot of water with salt, bay leaf, and peppercorns. Cook for about 2 to 3 hours until the tongue is very tender. | Remove the tongue from the pot and let it cool slightly. Peel off the outer skin while it is still warm. | Slice the peeled tongue into thin slices and keep warm. | For the piquant sauce, heat olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. | Add chopped onion, garlic, and chopped green pepper. Cook until soft and fragrant. | Stir in tomato paste and cook for a minute. | Add white wine vinegar, sugar, mustard, and hot sauce, mixing well. | Pour in beef broth and simmer the sauce for about 15 minutes until it thickens slightly. | Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve the sliced beef tongue topped with the piquant sauce and garnish with fresh parsley.

name: Beef Wellington French-style
description: Beef Wellington French-Style is a classic dish featuring a tender beef fillet coated in flavorful mushroom duxelles and prosciutto, wrapped in puff pastry and baked to golden perfection.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F). | Season the beef fillet generously with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over high heat and sear the beef fillet on all sides until browned, about 2-3 minutes per side. Remove and let cool. | In a food processor, finely chop mushrooms, shallots, and garlic until a paste forms. | Melt butter in a pan over medium heat and cook the mushroom mixture with thyme sprigs until the moisture evaporates and the mixture becomes a thick paste. Remove thyme and let cool. | Lay out slices of prosciutto on cling film, overlapping slightly to form a rectangle. | Spread the mushroom duxelles evenly over the prosciutto. | Place the cooled beef fillet on top and roll tightly using the cling film to form a log. Chill in the refrigerator for 15 minutes. | Roll out puff pastry on a floured surface to a size that will fully encase the beef. | Remove cling film from beef and place onto puff pastry. | Brush edges of pastry with beaten egg and wrap the pastry around the beef, sealing fully and trimming any excess pastry. | Brush the pastry surface with beaten egg and decorate with pastry scraps if desired. | Chill the wrapped beef for another 15 minutes to set the shape. | Brush the pastry again with egg wash and use a sharp knife to lightly score the surface without cutting through. | Place the beef Wellington on a baking sheet and bake for 25-30 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and beef reaches desired doneness. | Let the beef Wellington rest for 10 minutes before slicing and serving.

name: Beef and Carrots
description: Beef and carrots stew is a simple, comforting dish featuring tender beef simmered with sweet carrots in a flavorful broth.
instructions: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes. | Peel and slice the carrots into thick rounds. | Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. | Add the beef cubes and brown them on all sides. | Remove the beef and set aside. | In the same pot, add the chopped onion and garlic, and sauté until softened. | Return the beef to the pot and add beef broth, salt, and pepper. | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and cover. | Simmer for about 1 hour until the beef is tender. | Add the sliced carrots and cook for another 20-30 minutes until carrots are soft. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. | Serve hot as a hearty stew or with rice or potatoes.

name: Beef in Aspic
description: Beef in aspic is a traditional dish where tender cooked beef is set in a jelly made from flavorful meat broth, served cold as a savory appetizer.
instructions: Cook the beef brisket in a large pot with water, onion, carrot, celery, bay leaf, and peppercorns until tender, about 2-3 hours. | Remove the beef and strain the broth through a fine sieve, discarding the vegetables and spices. | Allow the broth to cool and skim off any excess fat from the surface. | Chop the cooked beef into small, bite-sized pieces and arrange them in a mold or shallow dish. | Season the beef with salt and pepper to taste. | Pour the strained broth over the beef pieces until fully covered. | Chill in the refrigerator for several hours or overnight until the aspic is firmly set. | Serve slices of beef in aspic cold as an appetizer or side dish.

name: Beef on a String
description: Beef on a string is a rustic cooking method where a whole beef cut is tied with string and cooked over an open fire or grill, resulting in tender and flavorful meat.
instructions: Soak a long, sturdy string or butcher's twine in water for about 30 minutes to make it easier to handle and less likely to burn during cooking. | Prepare a whole beef cut, typically a tenderloin or sirloin, by trimming excess fat and silver skin if necessary. | Season the beef generously with salt, pepper, and any preferred spices or herbs to enhance flavor. | Tie the soaked string firmly around the beef at regular intervals to secure its shape for even cooking. | Prepare a grill or open fire to medium-high heat for cooking. | Place the tied beef on the grill or suspend it over the fire using the string, turning periodically to ensure the meat cooks evenly on all sides. | Cook the beef until it reaches the desired internal temperature, typically medium-rare to medium for tenderness and juiciness. | Remove the beef from heat and let it rest briefly to allow the juices to redistribute. | Slice the beef carefully while still on the string or after removing the string, and serve immediately.

name: Beef with Coarse Salt
description: A simple and flavorful dish featuring well-seared beef seasoned with coarse salt to enhance the natural taste of the meat.
instructions: Preheat a grill or heavy skillet over high heat until very hot. | Rub the beef steak with olive oil on all sides. | Sprinkle coarse salt generously over both sides of the beef, pressing it lightly to adhere. | Place the beef on the hot grill or skillet and sear for about 4 minutes per side for medium rare, or adjust timing to preferred doneness. | Remove the beef from heat and let it rest on a cutting board for 5 to 10 minutes to allow juices to redistribute. | Slice the beef against the grain and serve immediately, optionally garnished with fresh rosemary for aroma.

name: Beef with Ginger and Soy
description: A simple and flavorful stir-fry dish featuring tender beef slices marinated and cooked with fresh ginger and soy sauce for a savory Asian-inspired meal.
instructions: Slice the beef thinly against the grain. | Peel and finely grate the ginger. | Mince the garlic cloves. | In a bowl, combine soy sauce, grated ginger, minced garlic, and a pinch of black pepper to make the marinade. | Add the sliced beef to the marinade and let it sit for at least 15 minutes. | Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. | Add the marinated beef and stir-fry until browned and cooked through, about 4-5 minutes. | Remove beef from the skillet and set aside. | In the same skillet, add a splash of vegetable oil if needed and stir-fry sliced onion and bell pepper until tender-crisp. | Return the beef to the skillet, tossing everything together to heat through and combine flavors. | Serve hot, optionally with steamed rice or vegetables.

name: Baked Feta Pasta
description: Baked Feta Pasta is a simple and creamy pasta dish combining roasted tomato and feta cheese, originating from a viral recipe trend. The feta softens in the oven with tomatoes to create a rich, flavorful sauce, mixed with pasta and fresh basil.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees Celsius (400 degrees Fahrenheit). | In a baking dish, place 200 grams of cherry tomato and drizzle with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon of salt and 1 teaspoon of black pepper. | Place a block of 200 grams of feta cheese in the center of the tomatoes. | Drizzle the feta cheese with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and sprinkle 2 cloves of minced garlic over the entire dish. | Bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes until the tomatoes burst and the feta is soft and golden on top. | While the feta and tomatoes bake, cook 250 grams of pasta in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain, reserving 125 ml of pasta water. | Remove the baking dish from the oven and use a fork to mash the tomatoes and feta together, adding fresh basil leaves as desired to create a creamy sauce. | Mix the cooked pasta into the baking dish, adding reserved pasta water little by little until the sauce reaches the desired consistency. | Serve immediately, garnished with additional fresh basil if preferred.

name: Baked Feta with Tomato and Oregano
description: Baked Feta with Tomato and Oregano is a simple and flavorful Greek-inspired dish featuring creamy feta cheese baked with juicy tomatoes and aromatic oregano, perfect as a warm appetizer or side dish.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Place a block of feta cheese in a small baking dish. | Pour cherry tomato halves around the feta cheese. | Drizzle olive oil generously over the feta and tomatoes. | Sprinkle dried oregano and crushed garlic over the top. | Add a pinch of salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 20 minutes, or until the feta is soft and slightly golden and the tomatoes are roasted. | Remove from the oven and garnish with fresh oregano leaves. | Serve warm with crusty bread or as a side dish.

name: Baked Fish with Lemon and Herbs
description: This simple baked fish recipe uses fresh lemon and herbs to enhance the natural flavors of the fish, creating a healthy and flavorful main dish.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Place the fish fillets in a baking dish in a single layer. | Drizzle olive oil over the fish and season with salt and pepper. | Squeeze lemon juice evenly over the fish fillets. | Scatter chopped fresh parsley, thyme, and dill over the fish. | Add lemon slices on top of the fillets for extra flavor. | Bake in the preheated oven for 12 to 15 minutes, or until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork. | Remove from the oven and let it rest for a couple of minutes before serving.

name: Baked Fish with Orzo
description: Baked Fish with Orzo is a wholesome Mediterranean-inspired dish combining tender fish fillets and flavorful orzo pasta baked together with tomatoes and herbs for an easy, comforting meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). | In a large baking dish, combine orzo, diced tomato, chopped onion, garlic, olive oil, vegetable broth, salt, and pepper. Stir well to mix all ingredients evenly. | Place the baking dish in the oven and bake uncovered for about 15 minutes, until the orzo is partially cooked. | Remove the dish from the oven and place the fish fillets on top of the orzo mixture. | Sprinkle the fish with lemon juice, fresh parsley, and a little more salt and pepper. | Return the dish to the oven and bake for an additional 15-20 minutes, or until the fish flakes easily with a fork and the orzo is tender. | Remove from oven and let rest for a few minutes before serving. Garnish with additional parsley and lemon slices if desired.

name: Baked Giant Beans with Sausage
description: Baked Giant Beans with Sausage is a hearty and comforting dish featuring tender giant beans and flavorful sausage baked together with tomato and herbs, popular in Mediterranean cuisine.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Soak the giant beans in water overnight, then drain and rinse. | Cook the soaked beans in boiling water until tender, about 45 minutes, then drain. | In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat and sauté the chopped onion and garlic until translucent. | Add the sausage slices to the skillet and cook until browned. | Mix the cooked beans with the sausage mixture, chopped tomato, tomato paste, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper in a baking dish. | Sprinkle the breadcrumbs and grated Parmesan over the top. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 25-30 minutes until the top is golden and the dish is heated through. | Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Baked Lamb Head
description: Baked lamb head is a traditional dish featuring a whole lamb head seasoned and slow-roasted until tender and flavorful, offering a unique and rustic culinary experience.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Clean the lamb head thoroughly, removing any hair and rinsing well under cold water. | Soak the lamb head in cold salted water for about 1 hour to remove blood and impurities. | Pat the lamb head dry with kitchen towels. | Rub the lamb head with olive oil, salt, pepper, and a mixture of crushed garlic and rosemary. | Place the lamb head on a roasting tray and cover it loosely with aluminum foil. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 2 to 2.5 hours, removing the foil in the last 30 minutes to allow browning. | Check for tenderness by inserting a skewer; the meat should be tender and easily pierced. | Remove from the oven and let it rest for 10 minutes before serving. | Carve and serve with your choice of sides or sauces.

name: Baked Lamb Meatballs with Orzo
description: Baked lamb meatballs served over lemony orzo pasta, combining tender spiced lamb with a light and flavorful Mediterranean-style grain side.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | In a large bowl, combine ground lamb, finely chopped onion, minced garlic, chopped parsley, dried oregano, salt, black pepper, and beaten egg. Mix well until all ingredients are evenly incorporated. | Form the mixture into small meatballs, about 1 inch in diameter, and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. | Bake the meatballs in the preheated oven for about 15-20 minutes, or until cooked through and browned. | While the meatballs are baking, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add chopped onion and minced garlic, sauté until softened and fragrant. | Add orzo to the skillet and toast for 1-2 minutes, stirring frequently. | Pour chicken broth into the skillet with the orzo and bring to a simmer. Cook the orzo according to package instructions until tender and liquid is absorbed, stirring occasionally. | Stir in freshly squeezed lemon juice and chopped parsley into the cooked orzo. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. | Once the meatballs are done, gently toss them into the skillet with the cooked orzo or serve the meatballs on top of the orzo on individual plates. | Garnish with extra chopped parsley and lemon wedges if desired. Serve warm.

name: Baked Oysters Greek-style
description: Baked Oysters Greek-Style is a flavorful Mediterranean appetizer featuring oysters topped with a fresh tomato, onion, garlic, and parsley mixture, finished with crumbled feta cheese and baked until golden. The combination offers a delightful balance of briny seafood and tangy, savory flavors characteristic of Greek cuisine.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F). | Clean the oysters thoroughly and carefully shuck them, preserving the oyster meat in the shell. | In a bowl, mix finely chopped tomato, finely chopped red onion, minced garlic, chopped parsley, a drizzle of olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and black pepper to create the Greek-style topping. | Place the oysters on a baking tray. | Top each oyster with the prepared tomato mixture. | Sprinkle crumbled feta cheese over each oyster. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 10-12 minutes until the oysters are cooked and the topping is slightly browned. | Remove from oven and garnish with a few fresh parsley leaves and a lemon wedge on the side. | Serve warm as an appetizer or side dish.

name: Baked Penne Greek-style
description: Baked Penne Greek-Style is a savory pasta casserole featuring penne mixed with a tomato, spinach, and olive sauce, seasoned with oregano and topped with crumbly feta cheese, inspired by Greek flavors.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). | Cook the penne pasta in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain and set aside. | In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat and sauté chopped onion and minced garlic until translucent. | Add diced tomato and cook for a few minutes until softened. | Stir in chopped spinach, black olives, oregano, salt, and pepper; cook until spinach wilts. | In a mixing bowl, combine cooked penne pasta, the vegetable mixture, crumbled feta cheese, and beaten egg to bind. | Transfer the mixture to a greased baking dish and sprinkle additional feta cheese on top. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 25-30 minutes until the top is golden and bubbly. | Remove from the oven and let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Baked Peppers Stuffed with Rice
description: Baked peppers stuffed with a flavorful mixture of rice, vegetables, and herbs, a classic vegetarian dish popular in many cuisines.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Wash the bell peppers, cut off the tops, and remove the seeds and membranes. | In a large bowl, mix the cooked rice, chopped onion, diced tomato, minced garlic, chopped parsley, salt, black pepper, and olive oil. | Stuff each hollowed bell pepper with the rice mixture, packing it firmly but not too tight. | Place the stuffed peppers upright in a baking dish. | Pour about 100 ml of water into the bottom of the baking dish to help steam the peppers during baking. | Cover the dish with aluminum foil and bake for 35 minutes. | Remove the foil and bake for another 10-15 minutes, until the peppers are tender and the filling is heated through. | Optional: sprinkle some grated cheese on top of the peppers in the last 10 minutes of baking and return to the oven until melted. | Remove from the oven and let cool slightly before serving.

name: Beef Tartare Italian Style
description: Italian-style beef tartare is a finely diced raw beef dish mixed with traditional Italian ingredients like anchovies, capers, olive oil, and fresh herbs, served chilled as an elegant starter.
instructions: Chill the beef tenderloin in the freezer for about 15 minutes to make it easier to cut. | Trim any fat or sinew from the beef and finely dice it into small pieces by hand. | In a bowl, combine the diced beef with finely chopped shallot, capers, and anchovy fillet. | Add a generous drizzle of good quality olive oil, a squeeze of fresh lemon juice, and season with salt and freshly ground black pepper. | Mix gently to combine all ingredients well without mashing the meat. | Add freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley and a pinch of crushed dried chili flakes for a slight kick. | Serve the tartare on chilled plates, optionally accompanied by toasted Italian bread slices or crostini on the side. | Garnish with extra parsley leaves and a drizzle of olive oil before serving.

name: Beet Pasta
description: Beet pasta is a vibrant dish featuring roasted beet puree turned into a creamy, colorful sauce to coat pasta, creating a delicious and nutritious meal with a natural sweetness and earthy flavor.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F). | Wash and peel the beet, then cut into chunks. Toss with olive oil and a pinch of salt. Spread on a baking sheet and roast for about 30-40 minutes until tender. | Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta until al dente according to package instructions. Reserve 100 ml of pasta water, then drain the pasta. | In a blender or food processor, combine the roasted beet, garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Puree until smooth, adding reserved pasta water a little at a time to reach a creamy sauce consistency. | Return the pasta to the pot or a large bowl. Add the beet sauce and toss to coat evenly. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve the beet pasta topped with grated Parmesan and chopped parsley, if desired.

name: Bellini
description: Bellini is a classic Italian cocktail from Venice that combines fresh peach puree with sparkling Prosecco, known for its light and refreshing taste.
instructions: Chill the Prosecco and peach puree before preparing the cocktail. | Peel and pit the peach, then blend it until smooth to create fresh peach puree. | Pour 60 ml of peach puree into a chilled champagne flute. | Slowly add 90 ml of chilled Prosecco to the flute to prevent excessive foaming. | Gently stir the mixture to combine the peach puree and Prosecco evenly. | Serve immediately while cold and enjoy.

name: Bigoli in Salsa
alias: Bigoli Pasta with Onion and Anchovy Sauce
description: Bigoli in Salsa is a traditional Venetian dish featuring thick bigoli pasta served with a savory onion and anchovy sauce. This simple yet flavorful recipe highlights the local anchovies and sweet onions.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the bigoli pasta until al dente according to the package instructions. | While the pasta cooks, peel and finely slice the onion. | In a large pan, heat olive oil over medium heat and add the sliced onion. | Cook the onion gently until it becomes soft and translucent, about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent browning. | Add the anchovy fillets to the pan and stir until they dissolve into the onion and oil, forming a sauce. | Drain the cooked pasta, reserving some pasta water. | Add the drained pasta to the pan with the sauce and toss to combine. | If needed, add a little reserved pasta water to loosen the sauce and help it coat the pasta evenly. | Season with freshly ground black pepper to taste and mix well. | Serve immediately, optionally garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

name: Biscotti Al Burro
description: Biscotti al Burro are traditional Italian butter cookies known for their rich, buttery flavor and crisp texture. Simple to prepare, they make a delightful snack or accompaniment to coffee or tea.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. | In a bowl, cream the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy using a mixer or wooden spoon. | Add the egg and vanilla extract to the butter mixture and mix until fully combined. | In a separate bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, baking powder, and salt. | Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and mix until a soft dough forms. | Using a spoon or your hands, form small balls of dough (about 25 g each) and place them spaced apart on the prepared baking sheet. | Flatten each ball gently with the palm of your hand to form a thick cookie shape. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 12-15 minutes or until the edges are lightly golden. | Remove the cookies from the oven and allow them to cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: Biscotti Di Prato
description: Biscotti di Prato, also known as Cantucci, are traditional crunchy Italian almond biscuits originating from Tuscany, perfect for dipping in coffee or Vin Santo wine.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | In a large bowl, whisk together the sugar and eggs until the mixture is thick and pale. | Add the vanilla extract and mix well. | Gradually add the flour, baking powder, and salt to the egg mixture, stirring to combine into a dough. | Fold in the sliced almond until evenly distributed. | Turn the dough onto a floured surface and shape it into a log approximately 30 cm long and 6 cm wide. | Place the log on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and bake for 25-30 minutes until lightly golden and firm to the touch. | Remove the log from the oven and let it cool for about 10 minutes to firm up slightly. | Reduce the oven temperature to 160°C (320°F). | Slice the log diagonally into 1 cm thick slices using a serrated knife. | Arrange the slices cut side down on the baking sheet and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes, turning them halfway through, until they are dry and crisp. | Let the biscotti cool completely on a wire rack before serving.

name: Biscotto Gelato
description: Biscotto Gelato is a classic Italian ice cream sandwich made by sandwiching creamy vanilla ice cream between two crisp almond biscotti, offering a delightful contrast of textures.
instructions: Soften the ice cream by leaving it out of the freezer for a few minutes until it is spreadable but not melted. | Place one biscotto (Italian almond biscuit) on a flat surface. | Spoon a generous amount of softened ice cream onto the biscotto. | Top with a second biscotto, pressing gently to spread the ice cream evenly between the biscuits. | Wrap the assembled ice cream sandwich in plastic wrap and place it in the freezer for at least 1 hour to firm up before serving. | Serve chilled as a refreshing dessert.

name: Bistecca Alla Fiorentina
description: Bistecca alla Fiorentina is a traditional Tuscan grilled T-bone steak known for its simplicity, quality of meat, and preparation over high heat to produce a rare, juicy interior with a crisp exterior.
instructions: Take a thick T-bone steak (at least 4 cm thick) and bring it to room temperature, about 30-40 minutes before cooking. | Lightly brush both sides of the steak with olive oil and season generously with salt and freshly ground black pepper. | Preheat a charcoal grill or heavy grill pan to very high heat until it’s smoking hot. | Place the steak on the grill and sear for about 5-6 minutes without moving it, until a good crust forms. | Flip the steak and sear the other side for an additional 5-6 minutes. | Check the internal temperature or doneness: it should be rare to medium-rare (about 50-55°C) internally. | Remove the steak from the grill and let it rest for about 5-10 minutes to allow the juices to redistribute. | Optionally, squeeze a little lemon juice over the steak before serving. | Slice the steak across the bone into thick slices and serve immediately, typically with a drizzle of high-quality olive oil and crisp Tuscan bread on the side.

name: Black Risotto
description: Black Risotto is an Italian seafood dish made with squid ink that gives the risotto a distinctive black color and rich, briny flavor. The creamy texture of the Arborio rice complements tender squid pieces and a subtle seafood broth base.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. | Add finely chopped onion and garlic, sauté until translucent. | Add Arborio rice and stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains. | Pour in a splash of white wine and cook until mostly evaporated. | Gradually add warm fish broth, one ladle at a time, stirring continuously until liquid is absorbed before adding the next. | When rice is almost cooked (about 15 minutes), stir in squid ink and cooked squid pieces. | Continue cooking and stirring until rice is creamy and fully cooked, about 5 more minutes. | Remove from heat and stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese. | Season with salt and black pepper to taste. | Serve immediately, garnished with chopped parsley if desired.

name: Blood Orange Sorbet
description: Blood Orange Sorbet is a refreshing and vibrant frozen dessert made from the juice of blood oranges combined with a simple syrup. Its bright color and tangy flavor make it a perfect palate cleanser or light treat.
instructions: Squeeze the blood orange juice into a bowl and strain to remove seeds and pulp. | Combine the sugar and water in a small saucepan and heat over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves to make a simple syrup. | Remove the syrup from heat and allow it to cool to room temperature. | Mix the cooled simple syrup with the blood orange juice and stir well. | Pour the mixture into an ice cream maker and churn according to the manufacturer's instructions until it reaches sorbet consistency. | Transfer the sorbet to a container and freeze for at least 2 hours to firm up before serving. | Serve the blood orange sorbet in chilled bowls or glasses.

name: Black Sesame Ice Cream
description: Black Sesame Ice Cream is a creamy and nutty Japanese-inspired dessert made by incorporating toasted black sesame paste into a rich custard base, delivering a unique flavor and striking color.
instructions: Toast the black sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 3-5 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent burning. | Using a food processor or blender, grind the toasted black sesame seeds into a fine powder. | In a medium saucepan, heat the milk, cream, and sugar over medium heat until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is hot but not boiling. | In a separate bowl, whisk the egg yolks until pale and slightly thickened. | Temper the egg yolks by slowly adding a small amount of the hot milk mixture while whisking constantly, then pour the yolk mixture back into the saucepan with the remaining milk mixture. | Cook the custard over low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon or spatula, until it thickens enough to coat the back of the spoon and reaches about 75-80°C (165°F). | Remove the custard from the heat and stir in the ground black sesame powder until fully incorporated and smooth. | Strain the mixture through a fine mesh sieve into a clean bowl to remove any lumps or seed husks. | Cover the bowl with plastic wrap, pressing it directly onto the surface of the custard to prevent a skin from forming, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours or overnight. | Once chilled, churn the mixture in an ice cream maker according to the manufacturer's instructions until it reaches a soft-serve consistency. | Transfer the ice cream to an airtight container and freeze for at least 2 hours to firm up. | Serve the black sesame ice cream chilled as a refreshing dessert.

name: Black Sesame Purin
description: Black Sesame Purin is a smooth, creamy Japanese custard pudding infused with the rich, nutty flavor of toasted black sesame seeds, offering a unique and delicious dessert experience.
instructions: Lightly toast black sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, then grind them into a fine powder using a spice grinder or mortar and pestle. | In a saucepan, combine milk, heavy cream, and the ground black sesame powder. Warm the mixture over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until it is hot but not boiling. | In a separate bowl, whisk together egg, egg yolk, and sugar until well combined. | Gradually pour the warm milk mixture into the egg mixture, whisking continuously to prevent curdling. | Strain the combined mixture through a fine sieve into a clean bowl to ensure a smooth texture. | Pour the mixture evenly into ramekins or custard cups. | Place the ramekins in a baking dish and add hot water to the dish until it reaches halfway up the sides of the ramekins, creating a water bath. | Cover the baking dish loosely with aluminum foil and bake in a preheated oven at 150°C (300°F) for about 40 minutes, or until the custard is set but still slightly jiggly in the center. | Remove the ramekins from the water bath and let them cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours to fully set. | Before serving, optionally top with a small amount of black sesame paste or roasted black sesame seeds for garnish.

name: Botamochi
description: Botamochi, also known as Spring Ohagi, is a traditional Japanese sweet made of sticky rice covered with sweet red bean paste, enjoyed especially during spring.
instructions: Wash the glutinous rice and regular rice together until water runs clear, then soak the mixture in water for about 1 hour. | Drain the rice and cook it in a rice cooker or pot with the appropriate amount of water until fully cooked and sticky. | While the rice is cooking, prepare the anko (sweet red bean paste) if not using ready-made: rinse azuki beans, boil, drain, then simmer with sugar until soft and paste-like. | Once the rice is cooked, use a wooden pestle and mortar or a rice paddle to slightly mash the rice, creating a sticky and cohesive texture. | Wet your hands with water to prevent sticking, take a portion of the rice mixture, and shape it into a small oval or round ball. | Place a small amount of sweet red bean paste on the palm, then wrap the rice ball around the anko, covering it entirely or partially depending on preference. | Roll the formed botamochi in more anko or alternatively coat it with soybean flour (kinako) with sugar if desired. | Repeat with the remaining rice and anko, then serve the botamochi at room temperature.

name: Buri Daikon
description: Buri Daikon is a traditional Japanese simmered dish featuring yellowtail fish and tender daikon radish cooked in a savory-sweet soy-based broth, highlighting seasonal flavors and simple elegance.
instructions: Peel the daikon radish and cut it into thick round slices about 2-3 cm thick. | Score the surface of the daikon slices lightly to help absorb the flavors during cooking. | Cut the yellowtail fillets into large bite-sized pieces, about 4-5 cm. | In a pot, combine the dashi stock, soy sauce, sake, mirin, and sugar and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. | Add the daikon slices to the pot and simmer gently for about 30 minutes or until the daikon is tender and absorbs the broth flavors. | Add the yellowtail pieces to the pot with the daikon and simmer gently for another 10-15 minutes until the fish is cooked through and infused with the broth. | Skim any foam or impurities off the surface during cooking for a clear broth. | Taste the broth and adjust seasoning if needed by adding a little more soy sauce or sugar for balance. | Remove from heat, garnish with chopped green onion or mitsuba if desired, and serve warm with some of the broth spooned over.

name: Buri Don
description: Buri Don is a traditional Japanese dish featuring fresh yellowtail sashimi served over steamed rice and topped with a savory soy-based sauce. This simple yet flavorful bowl highlights the delicate taste of yellowtail in a comforting meal.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear to remove excess starch. | Cook the rice according to your rice cooker's instructions or on the stove until tender and fluffy. | While the rice is cooking, prepare the yellowtail sashimi by slicing it into thin pieces about 0.5 cm thick. | In a small bowl, mix soy sauce, mirin, and a dash of grated ginger to create a simple marinade or dipping sauce. | Once the rice is cooked, divide it into serving bowls. | Arrange the yellowtail slices on top of the rice in each bowl. | Drizzle the soy sauce mixture over the fish and rice evenly. | Garnish with thinly sliced green onion and sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on top. | Serve immediately with pickled ginger or wasabi on the side if desired.

name: Buri Teriyaki
description: Buri Teriyaki is a classic Japanese dish featuring yellowtail fillets glazed with a savory and slightly sweet teriyaki sauce, delivering rich flavor and a tender texture.
instructions: Prepare the teriyaki sauce by mixing soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a bowl until the sugar dissolves. | Pat the yellowtail fillets dry with a paper towel and season lightly with salt. | Heat vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium heat. | Place the yellowtail fillets skin side down in the pan and cook for about 3-4 minutes until the skin is crispy and golden. | Flip the fillets and cook the other side for another 3-4 minutes or until the fish is cooked through. | Pour the teriyaki sauce into the pan and simmer for 1-2 minutes, spooning the sauce over the fish to glaze it. | Remove the fish from the pan and place it on a serving plate. | Drizzle the remaining sauce from the pan over the fish. | Garnish with chopped green onion and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Buta Kakuni
description: Buta Kakuni is a classic Nagasaki-style braised pork belly dish featuring tender, melt-in-your-mouth pork slowly simmered in a savory-sweet soy-based broth with ginger and sake.
instructions: Cut the pork belly into 5 cm cubes and blanch in boiling water for 5 minutes to remove impurities. | Drain and rinse the pork pieces under cold water. | In a large pot, combine the pork belly, water, sake, sugar, soy sauce, mirin, ginger slices, and scallion whites. | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer gently for about 2 hours, until the pork is very tender. | Occasionally skim off any foam or fat from the surface during cooking. | After 2 hours, add hard-boiled eggs (optional) to the pot and simmer for another 30 minutes to absorb flavor. | Remove pork and eggs from the pot. | Strain the sauce and simmer it separately to reduce and thicken slightly. | Serve the pork belly cubes and eggs drizzled with the reduced sauce, garnished with chopped scallion greens if desired.

name: Buta No Shogani
description: Buta no Shogani is a traditional Japanese dish featuring pork simmered in a ginger-flavored sauce. The aromatic ginger and savory soy-based marinade give the pork a deliciously tender and flavorful profile.
instructions: Thinly slice the pork shoulder into bite-sized pieces. | Peel and finely grate the ginger and garlic. | In a bowl, combine grated ginger, garlic, soy sauce, sake, mirin, and sugar to make the marinade. | Add the pork slices to the marinade and let them soak for at least 15 minutes. | Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. | Add the marinated pork and cook until the meat changes color and is cooked through, stirring occasionally. | Add the marinade liquid to the pan and simmer for 5-10 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the pork. | Serve the simmered pork over steamed rice and garnish with thinly sliced green onion or shichimi togarashi if desired.

name: Buta Shabu
description: Buta Shabu is a Japanese hot pot dish featuring thinly sliced pork and fresh vegetables cooked quickly in kombu broth, typically enjoyed with savory dipping sauces like ponzu and sesame.
instructions: Fill a pot with kombu broth and bring it to a gentle simmer without boiling to preserve the umami flavor. | Prepare the dipping sauces by mixing soy sauce and citrus juice (ponzu) in one bowl, and sesame paste mixed with a little soy sauce and water in another bowl. | Arrange thinly sliced pork on a large plate along with vegetables such as napa cabbage, shiitake mushroom, enoki mushroom, carrot, and tofu cubes nearby. | Using chopsticks, swish a slice of pork in the simmering broth just until it turns pale and opaque, approximately 10-20 seconds. | Quickly dip the cooked pork slice into your choice of dipping sauces before eating. | Cook the vegetables and tofu by placing them in the simmering broth until tender, then dip them into the sauces before eating. | After most ingredients are eaten, add cooked rice or noodles to the remaining broth to enjoy as a soup to finish the meal.

name: Butabara
description: Butabara are Japanese grilled pork belly skewers glazed with a savory-sweet marinade, popular as a delicious and easy-to-make snack or appetizer.
instructions: Cut pork belly into bite-sized pieces suitable for skewering. | Thread the pork belly pieces onto skewers evenly. | In a bowl, mix soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and grated garlic to create the marinade. | Brush the skewered pork belly generously with the marinade and let marinate for 15 minutes. | Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. | Grill the skewers, turning occasionally and brushing more marinade on them, until pork is cooked through and caramelized, about 10-15 minutes. | Serve hot as a savory snack or appetizer.

name: Banderillas
description: Banderillas are sweet, thin bread sticks popular in some cultures as a snack or accompaniment to meals. They are soft with a slightly sweet flavor and a glossy finish.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the warm milk, sugar, and yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy. | Add the softened butter, beaten egg, salt, and half of the flour to the yeast mixture. Mix well until combined. | Gradually add the remaining flour until a soft dough forms. | Turn the dough onto a floured surface and knead for about 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. | Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a clean cloth, and let rise in a warm place for about 1 hour or until doubled in size. | Punch down the dough and divide it into small equal portions (about 50 g each). | Roll each portion into a thin stick shape approximately 6-8 inches long. | Place the dough sticks on a baking tray lined with parchment paper, leaving some space between each. | Cover the sticks and let them rise for another 30 minutes. | Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Brush the sticks with beaten egg to give them a shiny finish. | Optionally, sprinkle sugar lightly over the sticks for extra sweetness. | Bake the banderillas for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown and cooked through. | Remove from the oven and let cool on a wire rack before serving.

name: Barbacoa Broth
description: Barbacoa Broth, or Consome de Barbacoa, is a traditional Mexican clear beef broth made from succulent slow-cooked beef cheek simmered with aromatic chilies and spices. This flavorful and comforting soup is often served with shredded meat and fresh garnishes like onion, cilantro, and lime.
instructions: Soak dried guajillo and ancho chili in hot water for 15 minutes until soft, then blend them with garlic, cumin, cloves, oregano, and vinegar to form a smooth chili sauce. | Season the beef cheek with salt and pepper, then place it in a large pot along with the onion, bay leaf, and enough water to cover the meat. | Pour the prepared chili sauce into the pot, mix well, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. | Reduce heat to low and simmer the broth covered for about 3 hours or until the beef is tender and falling apart. | Remove the beef from the broth and shred it using two forks, discarding any excess fat or gristle. | Strain the broth through a fine sieve or cheesecloth to obtain a clear broth, returning it to the pot and keeping it warm. | Serve the hot broth in bowls with shredded beef, diced onion, chopped cilantro, and lime wedges on the side for garnish.

name: Barbacoa De Borrego
description: Barbacoa de Borrego is a traditional Mexican dish featuring slow-cooked lamb shoulder marinated in a rich, smoky chili sauce. This tender, flavorful meat is commonly served in tacos with fresh onion, cilantro, and lime.
instructions: Soak dried guajillo and ancho chili peppers in hot water until soft, about 20 minutes, then blend them with garlic, cumin, oregano, cloves, vinegar, salt, black pepper, and beef broth to form a smooth marinade. | Cut the lamb shoulder into large pieces and marinate it with the chili sauce, covering all sides well. Let it rest in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight. | Preheat an oven to 150°C (300°F). Place the marinated lamb pieces in a covered roasting pan or Dutch oven, adding any remaining marinade and a little water if needed to keep moist. | Cover tightly with foil and cook in the oven for 4 to 5 hours, or until the meat is tender and can be easily shredded with a fork. | Once cooked, shred the lamb meat, mixing it with the cooking juices to keep it moist and flavorful. | Serve the shredded lamb dressed with chopped onion, cilantro, and lime wedges, accompanied by corn tortillas and optional salsa. | Optionally, for traditional smoky flavor, the lamb can be wrapped in maguey leaves and slow-cooked underground, but the oven method replicates the tenderness and taste for home cooking.

name: Barbacoa De Res
description: Barbacoa de Res is a traditional Mexican slow-cooked beef dish made with tender, marinated brisket cooked in a flavorful chile sauce until it easily shreds. It is perfect for tacos, burritos, or as a hearty main course.
instructions: Soak dried guajillo and ancho chiles in hot water for about 15 minutes until soft, then drain. | Place softened chiles, chopped onion, garlic, ground cumin, dried oregano, ground cloves, apple cider vinegar, beef broth, salt, and pepper in a blender. Blend until smooth to make the marinade. | Cut beef brisket into large chunks and place in a large bowl. | Pour the chile marinade over the beef, making sure all pieces are well coated. Marinate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight in the refrigerator. | Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. | Sear the marinated beef chunks on all sides until browned, then remove from the pot. | Add chopped onion and garlic to the pot, sauté until translucent. | Return the beef to the pot, pour in remaining marinade and beef broth if necessary to cover meat halfway. | Add bay leaves to the pot and bring to a low simmer. | Cover the pot tightly and cook on low heat for 4 to 5 hours until beef is very tender and shreds easily. | Remove beef from the pot and shred with two forks, discarding any excess fat and bones. | Return shredded beef to the pot, mix well with the cooking juices, and heat through before serving.

name: Barbacoa De Res Hidalgo
description: Barbacoa de Res Hidalgo is a traditional Mexican slow-cooked beef dish from Hidalgo, known for its tender, flavorful meat infused with chilies and aromatic spices.
instructions: Cut the beef into large chunks suitable for slow cooking. | In a large pot, combine water, guajillo chili (seeded and soaked), garlic, onion, cloves, allspice, cloves, black pepper, cinnamon stick, oregano, and salt to create a flavorful cooking broth. | Blend the soaked guajillo chilies with garlic, onion, cloves, black pepper, cinnamon stick, oregano, and salt until smooth to form a marinade sauce. | Marinate the beef chunks in the chili sauce for at least 2 hours or overnight for deeper flavor. | Place the marinated beef and marinade into a large pot or oven-safe dish. | Add the cooking broth to cover the meat; bring to a boil and then reduce heat to a low simmer. | Cover the pot tightly and cook the beef slowly for 4 to 6 hours, or until it is very tender and easily shredded with a fork. | Once cooked, shred the beef into pieces and mix it with the cooking juices to retain moisture and flavor. | Serve the barbacoa hot with warmed corn tortillas, chopped onion, cilantro, lime wedges, and salsa as desired.

name: Barbacoa Flautas
description: Barbacoa flautas are crispy rolled tortillas filled with tender, flavorful barbacoa beef, a traditional Mexican dish often served with creamy and fresh toppings.
instructions: Warm the corn tortillas on a skillet until pliable. | Heat the barbacoa meat and shred it finely if needed. | Place a spoonful of barbacoa meat onto each tortilla and roll tightly to form flautas. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat. | Fry the flautas in batches until golden and crispy, about 2-3 minutes per side. | Remove flautas and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. | Serve the flautas topped with sour cream, crumbled cotija cheese, sliced avocado, and chopped cilantro. | Optionally, add salsa or pickled jalapenos for extra flavor.

name: Barbacoa from Texcoco, State of Mexico
description: Barbacoa from Texcoco is a traditional slow-cooked beef dish wrapped and steamed in maguey leaves, resulting in tender, flavorful meat typically served with tortillas and fresh condiments.
instructions: Soak the dried maguey leaves in water to soften them and remove any dust. | Rinse the beef brisket thoroughly and season it with salt, pepper, and garlic powder. | Place the seasoned beef brisket on the maguey leaves and wrap it securely, folding the leaves around the meat. | Traditionally, prepare a pit in the ground, line it with hot stones and place the wrapped beef inside, then cover it with more maguey leaves and earth to seal the pit. Alternatively, use a large covered pot or slow cooker. | Cook the meat slowly for about 8 to 10 hours, allowing it to become tender and infused with the smoky flavor from the maguey leaves. | Once cooked, unwrap the beef carefully, shred the meat finely with forks. | Serve the shredded barbacoa hot with warmed corn tortillas, chopped onion, cilantro, lime wedges, and salsa of choice.

name: Bautizo Feast
description: Bautizo Feast is a traditional Latin American meal celebrating a baptism, featuring savory chicken with rice, fresh salad, and a sweet flan dessert.
instructions: Prepare the rice by rinsing it under cold water until clear, then soak it for 20 minutes and drain. | In a large pot, heat vegetable oil over medium heat and sauté chopped onion and minced garlic until translucent and fragrant. | Add diced tomato and cook until soft, forming the base for the rice. | Stir in the rice and toast it lightly for a few minutes to coat it with the flavors. | Pour in chicken broth, season with salt and pepper, and bring to a boil. | Lower the heat to simmer, cover, and cook until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed, about 15-20 minutes. | While the rice cooks, season chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and paprika. | Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat, then sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy. | Flip chicken and cook until cooked through, about 6-8 minutes per side depending on thickness. | Meanwhile, prepare the side salad by mixing chopped lettuce, tomato slices, cucumber, and red onion. | Dress the salad with olive oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper. | Arrange the cooked chicken over the rice and serve with the fresh salad on the side. | For dessert, prepare flan by heating milk with sugar and cinnamon until warm. | Whisk eggs and sweetened condensed milk in a bowl, then slowly add warm milk mixture. | Pour the custard into caramel-lined molds and bake in a water bath at 160°C (320°F) for 45-50 minutes until set. | Cool the flan before unmolding and serve chilled.

name: Bean Burrito
description: Bean burrito is a popular Mexican-inspired dish consisting of a flour tortilla filled with warm beans, cheese, and fresh toppings, rolled and optionally grilled for a satisfying and hearty meal.
instructions: Warm the flour tortilla in a dry skillet over medium heat until soft and pliable, about 30 seconds per side. | Heat the cooked beans in a saucepan over medium heat until warmed through, stirring occasionally. | Spread the warmed beans evenly over the center of the tortilla, leaving about 2 inches from the edges. | Sprinkle shredded cheese over the beans while still warm to allow it to melt slightly. | Add any desired toppings such as chopped onion, chopped tomato, and fresh cilantro leaves on top of the cheese and beans. | Fold the sides of the tortilla toward the center, then roll tightly from the bottom up to enclose the filling. | Place the burrito seam side down back into the skillet and cook for 1-2 minutes on each side until the tortilla is slightly crispy and the cheese is fully melted. | Serve the burrito warm, optionally with salsa, sour cream, or guacamole on the side.

name: Bean Gorditas
description: Bean gorditas are a traditional Mexican dish featuring thick corn cakes stuffed with warm refried beans, offering a simple yet hearty meal.
instructions: In a mixing bowl, prepare the masa dough by mixing corn flour with warm water and a pinch of salt until it forms a soft dough. | Divide the dough into equal portions and shape each portion into a small thick disk about half inch thick. | Heat a griddle or skillet over medium heat and cook each dough disk for about 2-3 minutes on each side until slightly golden and cooked through. | Heat the cooked gorditas on a separate skillet and gently slice a pocket into the side of each disk without cutting all the way through. | Prepare the refried beans by heating them in a saucepan until warm and creamy. | Stuff each gordita pocket generously with warm refried beans. | Optionally, serve with toppings like crumbled cheese, salsa, avocado, or sour cream as desired.

name: Beef Salpicao Salad
description: Beef Salpicao Salad is a Brazilian-style shredded beef salad mixed with fresh vegetables, apple, walnuts, and a creamy mayonnaise dressing, served cold as a refreshing side dish.
instructions: Cook the beef brisket in boiling salted water until tender, about 1.5 to 2 hours. Let it cool and then shred it finely using forks or your hands. | In a large bowl, combine the shredded beef, diced carrot, diced green bell pepper, diced green apple, sliced green onion, chopped parsley, and chopped walnuts. | Add mayonnaise and lemon juice to the bowl and mix well to combine all ingredients evenly. | Season the salad with salt and black pepper to taste, adjusting the flavors as needed. | Chill the salad in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour before serving to allow the flavors to meld. | Serve the beef salpicao salad cold, garnished with extra parsley or walnuts if desired.

name: Beef Shank Stew with Vegetables
description: A hearty and flavorful beef stew featuring tender beef shank slowly cooked with vegetables and red wine, perfect for comforting meals.
instructions: Cut the beef shank into large chunks and season with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef shank pieces on all sides. | Remove the beef and set aside. In the same pot, add chopped onion, carrot, celery, and garlic; cook until softened. | Return the beef to the pot, add tomato paste and stir well. | Pour in beef broth and red wine, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 2 hours until the meat is tender. | Add diced potato and continue to simmer for 30 minutes until the potatoes are cooked through. | Season with salt, pepper, and chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Beef Shin Stew
description: A rich and hearty beef stew made from slow-cooked beef shin, simmered with vegetables, red wine, and herbs to create a flavorful and tender dish.
instructions: Cut the beef shin into large chunks and pat dry with paper towels. | Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. | Brown the beef shin pieces in batches, ensuring a golden crust on all sides. Remove and set aside. | Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery to the pot and sauté until softened. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Return the beef shin to the pot and sprinkle with flour, stirring to coat the meat evenly. | Pour in red wine and beef broth, scraping the bottom of the pot to release any browned bits. | Add tomato paste, bay leaf, dried thyme, salt, and pepper to the pot and stir to combine. | Bring the stew to a simmer, then cover partially and cook on low heat for about 2.5 to 3 hours until the meat is tender and the sauce is thickened. | Remove bay leaf, adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed. | Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

name: Beef Short Ribs Braised
description: Braised beef short ribs cooked slowly in a rich sauce made from red wine, beef broth, and aromatics until tender and flavorful. This classic comfort dish is perfect for a hearty main course.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C (320°F). | Season the beef short ribs generously with salt and pepper. | Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy ovenproof pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. | Sear the short ribs on all sides until deeply browned, about 3-4 minutes per side, then remove and set aside. | Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery to the pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Pour in red wine to deglaze the pan, scraping up browned bits from the bottom. | Add beef broth, tomato paste, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf, stirring to combine. | Return the short ribs to the pot, ensuring they are partially submerged in the liquid. | Cover the pot with a lid and transfer to the preheated oven. | Braise the short ribs in the oven for 2.5 to 3 hours, until the meat is very tender and falling off the bone. | Remove the short ribs and strain the braising liquid into a saucepan. | Simmer the braising liquid on the stove to reduce and thicken into a sauce, about 10-15 minutes. | Serve the braised short ribs with the reduced sauce spooned over the top.

name: Beef Sirloin with Pepper Sauce
description: A classic dish featuring tender beef sirloin steak served with a rich and creamy peppercorn sauce enhanced with cognac and shallots, delivering bold flavors and a smooth texture.
instructions: Pat the beef sirloin dry with paper towels and season both sides evenly with salt and freshly ground black pepper. | Heat a tablespoon of vegetable oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. | Add the beef sirloin to the skillet and sear for 3 to 4 minutes on each side for medium-rare, or longer to desired doneness. | Remove the beef from the skillet and transfer to a warm plate; cover loosely with foil to rest. | In the same skillet, reduce heat to medium and add a tablespoon of butter. | Add finely chopped shallot to the skillet and sauté until translucent, about 2 minutes. | Add crushed black peppercorns and stir for 30 seconds to release flavor. | Pour in cognac carefully and let it simmer, scraping the browned bits from the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. | Add beef broth and heavy cream to the skillet, stirring constantly until the sauce thickens slightly. | Taste and adjust seasoning with salt as needed. | Return the rested beef to the skillet briefly to warm through in the sauce, then serve immediately with the pepper sauce spooned over the top.

name: Beef Steak Café De São Bento Style
description: Beef Steak Café de São Bento Style is a classic Portuguese bistro dish featuring a tender pan-seared beef steak served with a rich garlic and red wine sauce, embodying the café's traditional flavors.
instructions: Take a thick beef steak, such as ribeye or sirloin, and season it generously with salt and freshly ground black pepper on both sides. | Heat a heavy skillet or frying pan over high heat until very hot, then add a small amount of vegetable oil. | Place the steak in the hot pan and sear for about 3 to 4 minutes on each side for medium-rare, adjusting time for preferred doneness. | During the last minute of cooking, add butter and crushed garlic cloves to the pan, basting the steak with the melted butter and garlic aroma. | Remove the steak from the pan and let it rest for a few minutes to retain its juices. | Meanwhile, in the same pan, add finely diced shallots and cook for a minute until translucent. | Deglaze the pan with red wine, scraping up all the browned bits from the bottom. | Add a splash of beef broth and let the sauce reduce slightly until it thickens. | Finish the sauce by stirring in a pat of butter to give it a glossy shine and rich flavor. | Slice the steak thinly against the grain, arrange on a warm plate, and spoon the sauce over the top. | Serve immediately, optionally accompanied by crispy fries and a simple green salad.

name: Beef Steak with Port Wine Sauce
description: This dish features a juicy beef steak complemented by a rich and flavorful port wine sauce, a classic combination that elevates the meal to a refined dining experience.
instructions: Season the beef steak generously with salt and pepper on both sides. | Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. | Add the beef steak to the skillet and cook for about 4 minutes on each side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. | Remove the steak from the skillet and let it rest on a plate, loosely covered with foil. | In the same skillet, add butter and let it melt over medium heat. | Add finely chopped shallot and sauté until translucent, about 2 minutes. | Pour in the port wine and bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. | Allow the sauce to reduce by half, about 5-7 minutes. | Add beef broth and continue to simmer until the sauce thickens slightly, about 3 minutes. | Stir in additional butter to finish the sauce, and season with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve the beef steak topped with the port wine sauce.

name: Beef Stew Azores Style
description: A traditional Azorean beef stew featuring tender beef slow-cooked with aromatic spices, vegetables, and a splash of white wine, reflecting the rich flavors of the Azores islands.
instructions: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes and season with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and brown the beef cubes on all sides, then remove and set aside. | Chop onion, garlic, and bell pepper, then sauté them in the same pot until softened. | Add the beef back into the pot along with diced tomatoes, white wine, bay leaf, and a pinch of cinnamon. | Pour beef broth into the pot to cover the meat, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for about 1.5 to 2 hours until the beef is tender. | Add diced potatoes and carrots to the pot, continue simmering until the vegetables are cooked through, about 30 minutes. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste and remove the bay leaf before serving. | Serve hot, traditionally accompanied by crusty bread or rice.

name: Beef Stew with Broad Beans
description: A hearty and flavorful beef stew with tender broad beans, simmered in red wine and beef broth with fresh vegetables and herbs, perfect for a comforting main course.
instructions: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes and season with salt and pepper. | Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef cubes on all sides. Remove and set aside. | In the same pot, add chopped onion and garlic; sauté until softened. | Add diced carrot and celery, cook for a few more minutes until slightly tender. | Return the beef to the pot, sprinkle with flour, and stir well to coat the meat. | Pour in beef broth and red wine, scraping the bottom of the pot to deglaze. | Add bay leaf, thyme, and a pinch of black pepper. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 1.5 hours until beef is tender. | Add peeled broad beans and cook for an additional 15-20 minutes until beans are tender. | Remove bay leaf and thyme sprig. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed. | Serve the beef stew hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

name: Beef Stew with Olives
description: A hearty and savory beef stew enriched with the briny flavor of green olives, simmered slowly to tender perfection, inspired by Mediterranean cuisine.
instructions: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes and season with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef cubes on all sides. Remove and set aside. | Add chopped onion and garlic to the pot and sauté until softened. | Return the beef to the pot and add diced carrot and celery. Stir to combine. | Pour in beef broth and red wine, then add tomato paste, dried thyme, and bay leaf. Stir well. | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 1.5 to 2 hours until beef is tender. | About 20 minutes before the end of cooking, add chopped pitted green olives and chopped parsley. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. | Serve the stew hot, garnished with additional parsley if desired.

name: Arroz Con Pollo Y Setas
description: Arroz con Pollo y Setas is a flavorful Spanish-inspired dish combining tender chicken, mushrooms, and rice cooked together with spices and chicken broth for a comforting one-pan meal.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then set aside to drain. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet or paella pan over medium heat. | Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper, then add to the pan and brown on all sides until golden. Remove chicken and set aside. | In the same pan, add the chopped onion, garlic, and bell pepper, sauté until softened. | Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until they release their moisture and start to brown. | Return the chicken to the pan, add paprika, saffron threads (if using), and stir to combine. | Pour in chicken broth and bring to a simmer. | Add the drained rice into the pan and stir to coat the rice with the liquid evenly, distributing the chicken and vegetables. | Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan with a lid or foil, and cook for about 20 minutes or until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. | Remove from heat and let rest covered for 5 minutes. | Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and serve warm.

name: Arroz Con Pulpo
description: Arroz con Pulpo is a traditional Spanish dish featuring tender octopus cooked with rice and aromatic spices, delivering a flavorful seafood meal.
instructions: Clean the octopus thoroughly under cold running water and cut into bite-sized pieces. | Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat and sauté chopped onion and garlic until translucent and fragrant. | Add diced tomato and cook for a few minutes until softened. | Stir in the rice and cook for 1-2 minutes to lightly toast it. | Pour in the fish broth and bring to a gentle boil. | Add the octopus pieces, smoked paprika, and salt. Stir well to combine. | Reduce the heat to low and cover the pan. Simmer until the rice is cooked and liquid is absorbed, about 20 minutes. | If using peas, add them in the last 5 minutes of cooking. | Once cooked, remove from heat and let rest covered for 5 minutes. | Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Arroz Con Sepia
description: Arroz con Sepia is a traditional Spanish rice dish featuring cuttlefish cooked with tomato, garlic, and aromatic spices, offering a flavorful and hearty seafood meal.
instructions: Clean the cuttlefish and cut it into bite-sized pieces. | Heat olive oil in a paella pan or a wide skillet over medium heat. | Add chopped onion and garlic, and sauté until softened. | Add chopped tomato and cook until it forms a sauce. | Add cuttlefish pieces and cook for about 5 minutes until they start to brown. | Add rice and stir to coat the grains with the sauce. | Pour in fish stock, season with salt and paprika, and stir well. | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer without stirring for about 18-20 minutes until rice is cooked and liquid is absorbed. | Add chopped fresh parsley and let the dish rest for a few minutes before serving.

name: Arroz Con Setas
description: Arroz con Setas is a Spanish-inspired dish of rice cooked with sautéed mushrooms, delivering a flavorful and comforting vegetarian meal.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. | Add finely chopped onion and garlic and sauté until translucent. | Add assorted sliced mushrooms and cook until they release their moisture and start to brown. | Stir in short-grain rice and cook for a minute, coating the rice with the oil and flavors. | Pour in vegetable broth and season with salt and pepper to taste. | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover and simmer until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed, about 18-20 minutes. | Remove from heat and let it rest covered for 5 minutes. | Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Arroz De Campaña
description: Arroz de Campaña is a traditional Spanish country-style rice dish that combines sautéed vegetables, tomato, and smoky chorizo, creating a flavorful and rustic meal.
instructions: Rinse the rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear, then drain well. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet or paella pan over medium heat. | Add the chopped onion, garlic, and red bell pepper to the pan and sauté until softened and translucent. | Add the diced tomato and cook until the mixture thickens and the tomato is well incorporated. | Add the rice to the pan and stir well to coat the grains with the tomato and vegetable mixture. | Pour in the chicken broth and stir to combine everything evenly. | Season with salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika, then bring to a boil. | Reduce the heat to low, cover, and let the rice simmer gently for about 18-20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. | In the last 5 minutes of cooking, scatter the cooked chorizo slices over the rice and gently fold in to warm through. | Remove from heat and let the rice rest covered for 5 minutes before serving. | Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and serve warm.

name: Arroz De Matanza
description: Arroz de Matanza is a traditional Spanish rice dish made on slaughter day using various cuts of pork and sausages, resulting in a rich and flavorful one-pot meal.
instructions: In a large heavy-bottomed pot, heat pork fat over medium heat until melted and hot. | Add the chopped pork shoulder and pork ribs, browning them thoroughly to develop flavor. | Add chopped onion and garlic to the pot and sauté until softened and fragrant. | Stir in diced green bell pepper, tomato, and paprika, cooking until the vegetables are tender. | Add rice to the pot and stir well to coat with the pork fat and spices. | Pour in pork broth, season with salt and black pepper, and stir to combine. | Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer until the rice is cooked and liquid absorbed, about 20-25 minutes. | In the last 10 minutes of cooking, add sliced chorizo and sliced blood sausage on top of the rice and cover again to heat through. | Once cooked, remove from heat and let the rice sit covered for 5 minutes. | Fluff the rice with a fork and garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Arroz De Montaña
description: Arroz de Montaña is a traditional Spanish mountain rice dish combining sautéed meats, vegetables, and wild mushrooms cooked together for a flavorful hearty meal.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it for 20 minutes and drain. | In a large pan, heat the olive oil over medium heat and sauté the chopped onion and minced garlic until translucent and fragrant. | Add the diced bell pepper and cook for another 3 minutes, stirring occasionally. | Add the chopped tomato and cook until it softens and the mixture thickens slightly. | Stir in the soaked and drained rice, coating it well with the tomato mixture. | Add the sliced chorizo and cook for 2 minutes to release its flavors. | Pour in the chicken broth and add the dried thyme, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper. | Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and simmer for about 15 minutes or until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. | Meanwhile, heat a separate skillet over medium heat and sauté the wild mushrooms in a little olive oil until browned and cooked through. | Once the rice is cooked, gently fold in the sautéed mushrooms and chopped parsley. | Cover the pan again and let it rest for 5 minutes before serving. | Serve the Arroz de Montaña hot, garnished with additional parsley if desired.

name: Arroz Del Señoret
description: Arroz del Señoret is a flavorful Spanish rice dish from the Valencia region, featuring peeled and ready-to-eat seafood cooked with tomato and saffron-infused broth.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide skillet over medium heat. Sauté minced garlic and chopped onion until softened and translucent. | Add chopped tomato and cook until the tomato breaks down and forms a sauce. | Add rice to the pan and stir to coat it well with the tomato mixture and oil. | Pour in fish broth and bring to a boil. Add smoked paprika and a pinch of saffron, then stir to combine. | Arrange peeled seafood such as shrimp, calamari rings, and peeled mussels evenly over the rice without stirring again. | Reduce heat to a simmer and cook uncovered until the rice is tender and broth has absorbed, about 15-20 minutes. | Remove from heat and let it rest for 5 minutes. Garnish with chopped parsley and lemon wedges before serving.

name: Arroz Empedrado
description: Arroz Empedrado is a traditional rice dish from Jaén, Spain, featuring rice cooked with kidney beans and aromatic vegetables, resulting in a hearty and flavorful one-pot meal.
instructions: Rinse the rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for 20 minutes and drain. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, green pepper, and garlic, and sauté until softened and fragrant. | Add the chopped tomato to the skillet and cook until it breaks down into a sauce, about 5 minutes. | Add the soaked and drained rice to the skillet and stir to coat with the tomato mixture. | Pour in the chicken broth and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. | Add the cooked kidney beans gently over the rice, cover again, and cook for an additional 10 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. | Sprinkle chopped fresh parsley over the dish, fluff the rice gently with a fork, and serve hot.

name: Arroz Meloso De Bogavante
description: Arroz Meloso de Bogavante is a creamy, rich Spanish lobster rice dish that combines fresh lobster meat with a savory tomato sofrito and lobster-infused broth, offering a luxurious and comforting coastal flavor.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and add the lobster. Cook for about 7-8 minutes until bright red and cooked through. Remove the lobster, let it cool, then remove the meat from the shell and chop into bite-sized pieces. Reserve the shells for the broth. | In a large pan, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add chopped onion, garlic, and red bell pepper. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. | Add chopped tomato and cook until the mixture becomes a thick sofrito, about 10 minutes. | Add the lobster shells to the pan and cook for 2 more minutes to enhance flavor. | Pour in water or fish broth (about 1.2 liters) and simmer for 20-25 minutes to make a rich lobster broth. Strain and keep the broth warm. | In a separate large pan, heat olive oil and toast the rice for 2 minutes until coated and slightly translucent. | Add the sofrito to the rice and stir well, then gradually add the warm lobster broth one ladle at a time, stirring continuously. | Cook the rice at medium heat, allowing it to absorb the liquid gradually. When near done (about 15 minutes), fold in the lobster meat gently. | Season with salt and pepper to taste. Remove from heat and let rest for 5 minutes before serving. | Garnish with finely chopped fresh parsley and a drizzle of olive oil. Serve warm.

name: Gaeng Jued Het
description: Gaeng Jued Het is a traditional Thai clear soup featuring delicate straw mushrooms simmered in a savory chicken broth with fresh herbs and tofu, celebrated for its light and comforting flavors.
instructions: Clean and slice the straw mushrooms into bite-sized pieces. | Bring chicken broth to a gentle boil in a pot over medium heat. | Add sliced mushrooms to the boiling broth and simmer for 5 minutes until mushrooms are tender. | Add minced garlic and chopped coriander roots, let simmer for another 2 minutes to infuse the flavors. | Season the soup with fish sauce and a pinch of white pepper powder. | Add sliced tofu pieces and cook for an additional 2 minutes to warm through. | Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary, adding more fish sauce or pepper as desired. | Garnish with chopped cilantro leaves and sliced green onion before serving.

name: Gaeng Jued Mamuang
description: Gaeng Jued Mamuang is a light and clear Thai soup featuring unripe mango, vegetables, and tofu in a savory chicken broth. It is refreshing and mildly flavored, making it a comforting dish.
instructions: Peel the unripe mango and cut it into thin slices or small pieces. | Bring the chicken broth to a gentle boil in a pot over medium heat. | Add the sliced mango to the broth and simmer for about 5 minutes until the mango softens slightly. | Add sliced napa cabbage, mushrooms, and tofu cubes to the pot and continue simmering until the vegetables are tender, about 5 more minutes. | Season the soup with fish sauce and a pinch of salt to taste. | Add chopped cilantro just before serving for freshness. | Serve the soup hot, garnished with additional cilantro leaves if desired.

name: Gaeng Jued Mara
description: Gaeng Jued Mara is a traditional Thai clear soup featuring bitter melon, minced pork, mushrooms, and tofu, known for its light and soothing flavors with a characteristic bitterness from the melon.
instructions: Wash the bitter melon thoroughly and slice it into thin rings, removing the seeds. | Soak the dried shiitake mushroom in warm water for about 20 minutes until softened, then slice. | Prepare the minced pork by mixing it with a little salt and white pepper. | Bring chicken broth to a boil in a pot over medium heat. | Add the sliced bitter melon and shiitake mushroom to the boiling broth and let it simmer for about 5 minutes until the bitter melon softens. | Add the minced pork into the soup, stirring gently to break up the meat and cook through. | Season the soup with fish sauce, salt, and white pepper according to taste. | Add tofu cubes and simmer for another 3 minutes until heated through. | Garnish with chopped spring onion and coriander before serving hot.

name: Gaeng Jued Moo Sab
description: Gaeng Jued Moo Sab is a traditional Thai clear soup made with minced pork, garlic, and white radish, known for its light and comforting flavor.
instructions: Prepare the broth by boiling water in a pot. | Add minced pork to the boiling water and cook until it changes color. | Add chopped garlic and sliced white radish to the pot, simmer until radish is tender. | Season the soup with fish sauce, white pepper, and salt to taste. | Add chopped green onions and cilantro just before turning off the heat. | Serve the hot soup immediately, optionally accompanied by steamed jasmine rice.

name: Gaeng Jued Pak Ruam
description: Gaeng Jued Pak Ruam is a traditional Thai clear mixed vegetable soup known for its light, healthy, and comforting qualities, featuring a variety of fresh vegetables simmered in savory chicken broth.
instructions: Prepare all vegetables by washing thoroughly and cutting them into bite-size pieces. | In a large pot, bring chicken broth to a gentle boil over medium heat. | Add garlic and sliced carrot to the broth and simmer until the carrot is tender, about 5 minutes. | Add napa cabbage, zucchini, and corn and continue to cook for another 5 minutes. | Season the soup with fish sauce, white pepper, and salt to taste. | Add mushrooms and tofu pieces, simmer for an additional 3-4 minutes until tofu is heated through and mushrooms are tender. | Sprinkle chopped cilantro and green onion on top just before serving. | Serve hot as a light and refreshing soup accompanying main dishes.

name: Gaeng Jued Tao Hu
description: Gaeng Jued Tao Hu is a traditional Thai clear soup featuring soft tofu and vegetables in a delicate, flavorful broth. It is light, comforting, and commonly served as part of Thai meals.
instructions: Prepare all ingredients by dicing tofu, slicing mushroom, chopping garlic, and slicing carrot and spring onion. | Heat vegetable oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté garlic until fragrant. | Add mushroom and carrot slices to the pot and stir-fry for a minute. | Pour in chicken broth and bring to a gentle boil. | Add tofu and simmer for about 5 minutes, allowing flavors to meld. | Season the soup with fish sauce, white pepper, and a pinch of salt to taste. | Add chopped spring onion and cilantro just before turning off the heat. | Serve hot, optionally accompanied by steamed rice or as part of a meal.

name: Gaeng Jued Tofu
description: Gaeng Jued Tofu is a Thai mild clear soup curry featuring soft tofu and vegetables in a delicate, flavorful broth. It's a comforting dish known for its lightness and subtle seasoning.
