instructions: In a large bowl, dissolve sugar in warm milk and sprinkle yeast over; let sit until foamy, about 5-10 minutes. | Whisk eggs lightly in a separate bowl. | Add eggs, melted butter, and salt to the yeast mixture and stir to combine. | Gradually add flour to the wet ingredients, mixing until a soft dough forms. | Turn dough onto a floured surface and knead for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. | Place dough in a greased bowl, cover with a towel, and let rise in a warm place until doubled in size, about 1 to 1.5 hours. | Punch down the dough and divide it into three equal pieces. | Roll each piece into a long rope of equal length. | Brush the ropes with melted butter, then braid them together carefully. | Place the braided dough on a lined baking sheet, cover, and let rise again until puffy, about 45 minutes. | Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). | Brush the braid with beaten egg for a glossy finish. | Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, or until the brioche is golden brown and sounds hollow when tapped. | Remove from oven and let cool on a wire rack before slicing.

name: Braised Beef Cheeks
description: Braised beef cheeks are a rich and tender slow-cooked dish where beef cheeks are cooked in red wine and aromatic vegetables until meltingly soft, creating a deeply flavorful meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C (320°F). | Season the beef cheeks with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. | Sear the beef cheeks on all sides until browned, then remove and set aside. | Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery to the pot and cook until softened. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Pour in red wine and bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. | Add beef broth, tomato paste, bay leaf, and thyme sprigs to the pot, then return the beef cheeks to the pot. | Cover the pot and transfer to the preheated oven. | Braise the beef cheeks in the oven for 3 to 4 hours, or until the meat is very tender and easily shredded with a fork. | Remove the beef cheeks from the pot and keep warm. | Strain the cooking liquid and return it to the pot, simmering it on the stove to reduce and thicken into a sauce. | Serve the braised beef cheeks with the sauce poured over the top.

name: Braised Beef Mode
description: Braised beef mode is a tender, slow-cooked beef dish where the meat is seared and then cooked gently in wine and broth with aromatics until richly flavorful and meltingly tender.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C (320°F). | Season the beef mode with salt and pepper on all sides. | Heat olive oil in a heavy, oven-proof pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. | Sear the beef mode in the hot oil until browned on all sides, then remove and set aside. | Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery to the pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Pour in red wine and beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. | Return the beef mode to the pot and add thyme, bay leaf, and tomato paste, stirring to combine. | Cover the pot with a lid and transfer it to the preheated oven. | Cook gently in the oven for about 3 hours, or until the beef is very tender and easily pulls apart with a fork. | Remove the beef from the pot and let it rest for a few minutes before slicing. | Strain the cooking liquid and reduce it on the stovetop over medium heat until it thickens into a sauce. | Serve the sliced braised beef mode with the sauce drizzled over the top, accompanied by your choice of side dishes.

name: Braised Beef with Carrots
description: Braised beef with carrots is a classic slow-cooked dish where beef chuck is seared and then slowly cooked with carrots, onion, garlic, and red wine until tender and flavorful.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C (320°F). | Season the beef with salt and pepper on all sides. | Heat olive oil in a large ovenproof pot over medium-high heat. | Sear the beef on all sides until browned, then remove and set aside. | In the same pot, add chopped onion and garlic; sauté until softened. | Add sliced carrots and cook for a few minutes to start softening. | Pour in beef broth and red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. | Return the beef to the pot, cover, and place it in the oven. | Braise for about 3 hours, or until the beef is very tender. | Remove the beef and carrots, then simmer the liquid on the stovetop to reduce and thicken into a sauce. | Serve the braised beef sliced, topped with carrots and sauce.

name: Braised Cabbage
description: Braised cabbage is a simple and comforting side dish of tender cabbage slowly cooked with onions, garlic, and broth until soft and flavorful. It is a vegan and healthy option often served alongside hearty meals.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. | Add chopped onion and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Add sliced cabbage to the skillet and stir to combine with onion and garlic. | Season with salt, pepper, and caraway seeds (if using). | Pour in vegetable broth, cover the skillet, and reduce heat to low. | Simmer gently until the cabbage is tender, about 25 minutes, stirring occasionally. | Remove the lid and cook for another 5 minutes to allow any excess liquid to evaporate, stirring occasionally. | Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper as desired, then serve warm.

name: Braised Endives
description: Braised endives is a classic French side dish where endives are gently cooked in butter and broth until tender and caramelized, often finished with herbs for freshness.
instructions: Trim the ends of the endives and remove any damaged outer leaves. | Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. | Add the endives to the skillet, cut side down, and cook until lightly browned, about 4 minutes. | Turn the endives and add the sugar and salt. | Pour in the chicken broth and cover the skillet. | Reduce the heat to low and let the endives braise until tender, about 20 minutes. | Remove the lid and cook for an additional 5 minutes to reduce the liquid slightly. | Season with black pepper to taste and garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Braised Fennel
description: Braised fennel is a tender, flavorful side dish made by slowly cooking fennel bulbs in olive oil and vegetable broth until soft and caramelized. Its subtle anise flavor makes it a delightful accompaniment to many meals.
instructions: Trim the fennel bulbs by cutting off the stalks and removing any tough outer layers, then slice each bulb into quarters. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering. | Add the sliced fennel to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 5 minutes. | Pour in the vegetable broth and add salt and pepper to taste. | Cover the skillet, reduce heat to low, and simmer until the fennel is tender, about 20 minutes. | Remove the lid and increase heat to medium-high to evaporate any excess liquid, cooking for an additional 5 minutes. | Sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving.

name: Beef Gyro
description: Beef Gyro is a popular Greek street food featuring seasoned ground beef cooked into patties, served in warm pita bread with fresh vegetables and tangy tzatziki sauce.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine ground beef with minced garlic, dried oregano, ground cumin, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes. | Mix well until all spices are evenly incorporated into the beef. | Form the mixture into small, thin patties or oval shapes that will fit inside pita bread. | Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the beef patties for about 3-4 minutes on each side, until fully cooked and browned. | Warm the pita bread lightly in a dry pan or oven. | To assemble, spread tzatziki sauce on the warm pita bread. | Place cooked beef patties on top of the sauce. | Add sliced tomato, thinly sliced red onion, and chopped lettuce over the meat. | Fold the pita around the fillings and serve immediately.

name: Beef Souvlaki
description: Beef Souvlaki is a traditional Greek dish featuring marinated beef cubes grilled on skewers, often served with pita bread and tzatziki sauce. It is flavorful, simple, and perfect for a quick Mediterranean meal.
instructions: Cut the beef into 2 cm (about 1 inch) cubes and place them in a large bowl. | In a separate small bowl, combine olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper to make the marinade. | Pour the marinade over the beef cubes and mix well to coat all pieces evenly. | Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight for best flavor. | If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 30 minutes to prevent burning during grilling. | Preheat the grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. | Thread the marinated beef cubes onto the skewers, leaving a little space between each piece. | Grill the skewers for about 8-10 minutes total, turning occasionally, until the beef is cooked to your desired doneness and has a nice char. | Remove the skewers from the grill and let them rest for a few minutes before serving. | Serve the beef souvlaki with warm pita bread, sliced onion, tomato, tzatziki sauce, and lemon wedges.

name: Beef Stifado
description: Beef Stifado is a traditional Greek stew featuring tender beef cubes slow-cooked with aromatic spices, tomato, and red wine, resulting in a rich and flavorful dish.
instructions: Cut the beef into large cubes and set aside. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and brown the beef cubes on all sides. | Remove beef and set aside. In the same pot, add chopped onion and garlic, cooking until softened. | Add the beef back to the pot along with red wine, tomato paste, cinnamon stick, cloves, bay leaf, and allspice. | Pour in water or beef broth to cover the meat. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer, covered, for about 2 hours or until the beef is tender. | Add chopped peeled tomatoes, salt, pepper, and sugar to balance acidity. Continue to simmer uncovered for another 30 minutes until the sauce thickens. | Adjust seasoning to taste. Remove the cinnamon stick and bay leaf before serving. | Serve hot with crusty bread or over pasta or rice.

name: Beef Tongue Stew
description: Beef Tongue Stew is a hearty and tender slow-cooked dish featuring peeled and sliced beef tongue simmered with vegetables, herbs, and rich broth, popular in various cuisines for its unique flavor and texture.
instructions: Rinse the beef tongue thoroughly under cold water to clean it. | Place the beef tongue in a large pot and cover with water, then bring to a boil. Boil for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse the tongue to remove impurities. | Refill the pot with fresh water and add the beef tongue back in. Add bay leaf, whole black peppercorns, and a pinch of salt. Simmer gently for about 2 hours or until the tongue is tender when pierced with a fork. | Remove the tongue from the pot and let it cool slightly. Peel off the tough outer skin and slice the tongue into bite-sized pieces. | Heat vegetable oil in a large stew pot over medium heat. Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery, and sauté until softened. | Add minced garlic and tomato paste, cooking for another 2 minutes to develop flavor. | Add the sliced beef tongue pieces back into the pot. Pour in beef broth and red wine, then add thyme and bay leaf. | Bring the stew to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for 1 hour to allow flavors to develop. | Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Remove bay leaf and thyme sprigs before serving. | Serve the beef tongue stew hot, garnished with fresh parsley if desired.

name: Beef and Potato Casserole
description: Beef and Potato Casserole is a hearty dish featuring layers of seasoned ground beef and thinly sliced potatoes baked with cheese and broth. This comforting casserole is perfect for a filling family meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees Celsius (350 degrees Fahrenheit). | Peel the potatoes and cut them into thin slices. | Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and garlic and sauté until translucent. | Add the ground beef to the skillet and cook until browned, breaking it apart with a spoon. | Season the beef mixture with salt, pepper, and dried oregano. Remove from heat. | In a baking dish, arrange a layer of potato slices. | Spread half of the beef mixture over the potatoes. | Sprinkle with some shredded Cheddar cheese. | Repeat the layering with the remaining potatoes, beef mixture, and top with the rest of the cheese. | Pour the beef broth evenly over the casserole. | Cover the dish with aluminum foil and bake for 45 minutes. | Remove the foil and bake for an additional 15 minutes or until the potatoes are tender and the cheese is golden and bubbly. | Remove from oven and let stand for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Beef with Celery Avgolemono
description: This traditional Greek soup combines tender beef and crunchy celery in a rich broth thickened with avgolemono, a lemon and egg sauce that gives the dish its signature tangy and creamy texture.
instructions: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes and rinse under cold water. | Peel and slice celery stalks into thin pieces, and finely chop one onion. | In a large pot, combine the beef cubes with water to cover and bring to a boil. | Skim off any foam that rises to the top to keep the broth clear. | Add the chopped onion, sliced celery, salt, and black pepper to the pot. | Lower the heat and simmer gently for about 1 hour, until the beef is tender and the broth flavorful. | In a bowl, beat the eggs with lemon juice until well combined to make the avgolemono sauce. | Remove about one cup of the hot broth from the pot and slowly whisk it into the egg-lemon mixture to temper the eggs. | Gradually pour the tempered egg mixture back into the soup pot, stirring continuously to prevent curdling. | Heat the soup gently without boiling until it thickens slightly and becomes creamy. | Taste and adjust seasoning with additional salt or lemon juice if desired. | Serve the soup hot, garnished with fresh parsley if available.

name: Beef with Eggplant
description: Moschari me Melitzanes is a classic Greek dish featuring tender beef cooked with fried eggplant in a savory tomato sauce, flavored with cinnamon and herbs. This hearty meal is a staple of Greek home cooking.
instructions: Cut the eggplants into slices about 1 cm thick and sprinkle them with salt. Let them sit for 30 minutes to remove bitterness, then rinse and pat dry. | Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat and fry the eggplant slices until golden brown on both sides. Remove and set aside on paper towels to drain excess oil. | In the same pan, add a little olive oil if needed and sauté chopped onion and garlic until soft and fragrant. | Add ground beef to the pan and cook until browned, breaking up any lumps with a spoon. | Stir in chopped tomato, tomato paste, and cook for a few minutes until the tomatoes soften. | Add cinnamon, salt, and pepper, then pour in water or beef broth. Bring to a simmer and cook for about 20 minutes until the sauce thickens and the beef is tender. | Layer the fried eggplants on the bottom of an oven-safe dish, then pour the beef mixture evenly over the top. | Cover the dish and bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for about 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld. | Remove from oven and garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Beef with Zucchini
description: A traditional Greek dish featuring tender beef stewed with fresh zucchini, tomatoes, and aromatic herbs, offering a hearty and flavorful meal.
instructions: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes and season with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add chopped onion and garlic, sauté until soft and fragrant. | Add the beef cubes to the pan and brown on all sides. | Add diced tomato and tomato paste to the beef, stir well and cook for a few minutes. | Pour in water or beef broth to cover the meat partially, then cover the pan and simmer on low heat until beef is tender, about 45 minutes. | Meanwhile, wash and cut the zucchini into bite-sized pieces. | Once the beef is tender, add the zucchini pieces to the pan, season with salt and pepper, and cook uncovered for 10-15 minutes until zucchini is cooked but still firm. | Adjust seasoning if needed and sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving.

name: Beet Greens with Lemon
description: Sautéed beet greens flavored with garlic and fresh lemon juice make a simple, nutritious side dish with bright, tangy notes.
instructions: Rinse the beet greens thoroughly under cold water to remove any dirt or grit. | Trim the tough stems from the beet greens and chop the leaves roughly. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. | Add minced garlic to the skillet and sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute, being careful not to burn it. | Add the chopped beet greens to the skillet and sauté, stirring frequently, until wilted and tender, about 5 to 7 minutes. | Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. | Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the cooked beet greens and toss to combine. | Remove from heat and serve warm as a side dish.

name: Beetroot and Walnut Salad
description: Beetroot and Walnut Salad is a flavorful and nutritious dish combining the earthiness of roasted beetroot with the crunch of toasted walnuts and creamy feta, dressed in a tangy balsamic vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Wash the beetroot thoroughly and wrap each beetroot in aluminum foil. | Place the wrapped beetroot on a baking sheet and roast in the oven for about 45 minutes or until tender when pierced with a fork. | Remove from oven and allow to cool. Once cooled, peel the beetroot and cut into bite-sized cubes. | In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast the walnuts for about 5 minutes until fragrant, stirring frequently to avoid burning. Set aside to cool. | In a mixing bowl, combine olive oil, balsamic vinegar, honey, salt, and black pepper to prepare the dressing. Whisk well to combine. | Place the beetroot cubes in a salad bowl, add the toasted walnuts, and crumble the feta cheese over the top. | Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine all ingredients. | Garnish with fresh parsley leaves before serving.

name: Brodetto
description: Brodetto is a flavorful Italian seafood stew featuring a variety of fresh seafood cooked in a tomato-based broth with garlic, herbs, and a hint of spice, typically served with crusty bread.
instructions: Clean and prep the seafood by rinsing and drying them thoroughly. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté chopped garlic until fragrant. | Add diced onion and cook until translucent. | Pour in canned crushed tomato and cook for a few minutes to blend flavors. | Add fish stock or water and bring to a simmer. | Season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of red chili flakes for heat. | Add the seafood starting with the firmest, such as cut squid and firm fish pieces, cooking for a few minutes. | Add shellfish like mussels and clams, cover the pot and cook until they open. | Fold in shrimp and delicate fish, cooking until just done. | Stir in chopped parsley and a splash of white wine, letting the alcohol cook off. | Adjust seasoning as needed and serve hot with crusty bread.

name: Brodetto Di Pesce
description: Brodetto di Pesce is a traditional Italian fish stew featuring a hearty mix of fish and seafood cooked in a tomato and white wine broth, typically served with crusty bread.
instructions: Clean and cut the fish and seafood into bite-sized pieces if necessary. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté chopped onion and garlic until translucent. | Add chopped tomato and cook until the tomato softens and releases juice. | Pour in white wine and let it simmer to reduce slightly. | Add fish stock and bring to a gentle simmer. | Add the mixed fish and seafood, season with salt, pepper, and chili flakes to taste. | Let it cook gently until the fish is just cooked through, about 10 minutes. | Adjust seasoning if necessary, then sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving. | Serve hot with toasted rustic bread or crostini on the side.

name: Brodetto Marchigiano
description: Brodetto Marchigiano is a traditional fish stew from the Marche region of Italy, featuring a fresh mix of fish and seafood simmered in a simple tomato and garlic broth, highlighting the flavors of the Adriatic Sea.
instructions: Clean and cut the assorted fish and seafood into bite-sized pieces, set aside. | Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat and sauté chopped garlic until fragrant but not browned. | Add chopped tomato and cook until soft, then pour in fish broth and bring to a simmer. | Season the broth with salt, pepper, and a pinch of chili flakes for subtle heat. | Add the fish and seafood pieces to the broth and cook gently until just cooked through, about 10 minutes. | Finish with chopped fresh parsley and a drizzle of good quality olive oil. | Serve hot with toasted rustic bread on the side.

name: Brodo Di Carne
description: Brodo di Carne is a traditional Italian meat broth made by slow-simmering beef bones and vegetables to create a flavorful, rich stock. It serves as a foundational base for many Italian soups, sauces, and risottos.
instructions: Place the beef bones, beef shank, carrot, celery, onion, and garlic in a large stockpot. | Fill the pot with cold water until all ingredients are covered by about 2 inches. | Slowly bring the water to a boil over medium-high heat. | Once boiling, reduce the heat to low and skim off any foam or impurities that rise to the surface using a slotted spoon. | Add tomato paste, parsley, bay leaf, and whole black peppercorns to the pot. | Cover the pot partially and let the broth simmer gently for at least 4 hours, occasionally skimming off any foam. | After simmering, remove the pot from the heat and strain the broth through a fine mesh sieve into another large pot or container. | Discard the solids and season the broth with salt to taste. | Let the broth cool before using it as a base for soups, sauces, or other dishes.

name: Brodo Di Pesce
description: Brodo di Pesce is a traditional Italian fish broth made by simmering fish bones and aromatic vegetables, used as a flavorful base for seafood dishes and soups.
instructions: Rinse fish bones and heads under cold water to remove any blood or impurities. | Peel and roughly chop carrot, celery, and onion. | In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat and add carrot, celery, and onion. Sauté until vegetables soften, about 5 minutes. | Add garlic cloves and continue to cook for 1 minute, stirring to avoid burning. | Add fish bones and heads to the pot and stir well with the vegetables. | Pour in water and white wine, then add bay leaf, parsley, and a pinch of salt and pepper. | Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Once simmering, reduce heat to low and cook uncovered for 30 to 40 minutes, skimming any foam or impurities from the surface occasionally. | After cooking, strain the broth through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth into another pot or bowl, discarding the solids. | Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper if needed. Use immediately or refrigerate/freeze for later use.

name: Bruschetta Bread
description: Bruschetta bread is a classic Italian appetizer featuring toasted slices of Italian bread topped with a fresh tomato, garlic, and basil mixture. It is simple, flavorful, and perfect for entertaining.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Slice the Italian bread into 1/2-inch thick slices. | Brush each bread slice lightly with olive oil on both sides. | Place the bread slices on a baking sheet and toast in the oven for about 5-7 minutes, or until golden and crisp. | Remove the toasted bread from the oven and let it cool slightly. | In a bowl, combine chopped tomato, minced garlic, chopped fresh basil, olive oil, salt, and pepper. | Spoon the tomato mixture generously onto each toasted bread slice. | Optionally, drizzle with a little more olive oil and garnish with a basil leaf before serving.

name: Bruschetta with Mushrooms
description: Bruschetta with Mushrooms is a simple Italian appetizer featuring toasted bread topped with a savory mixture of sautéed mushrooms, garlic, and herbs. It's flavorful, easy to prepare, and perfect for sharing.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Slice the bread into 1 cm thick slices and arrange them on a baking sheet. | Brush each slice lightly with olive oil. | Bake the bread slices in the oven for about 5-7 minutes until they are golden and crisp. | While the bread is baking, heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. | Add chopped garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute. | Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet and cook until they release their moisture and become tender, about 5-7 minutes. | Season the mushrooms with salt, black pepper, and a pinch of dried thyme while cooking. | Remove the skillet from heat and stir in chopped fresh parsley. | Once the bread slices are toasted, spoon the mushroom mixture evenly over each slice. | Optionally, drizzle a little more olive oil over the top and garnish with additional parsley leaves before serving.

name: Bruschetta with Nduja
description: Bruschetta with Nduja is an Italian appetizer featuring toasted bread topped with spicy Calabrian spreadable pork sausage and fresh tomato and basil, delivering a rich and flavorful bite.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Slice the French bread into 1 cm thick slices and arrange them on a baking sheet. | Drizzle olive oil over the bread slices and toast them in the oven for about 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp. | Remove the bread from the oven and rub each slice with a peeled garlic clove while still warm. | Spread a thin layer of nduja evenly on each toasted bread slice. | Chop the tomato and basil finely and spoon them over the nduja-topped slices. | Drizzle a little more olive oil over the bruschetta and season with a pinch of salt and freshly ground black pepper. | Serve immediately as a flavorful appetizer.

name: Bruschetta with Tomato and Basil
description: Bruschetta with Tomato and Basil is a classic Italian appetizer featuring toasted bread topped with fresh tomato, basil, and garlic, perfect for a light and refreshing starter.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Slice the French bread into 12 slices about 1cm thick. | Place the bread slices on a baking sheet and brush both sides with olive oil. | Toast the bread slices in the oven for about 5-7 minutes or until golden and crisp, turning once. | While the bread toasts, dice the tomatoes and place them in a mixing bowl. | Add the chopped garlic and chopped basil to the tomatoes. | Season the tomato mixture with salt and freshly ground black pepper, then stir gently. | Remove the toasted bread from the oven and rub one side of each slice lightly with a cut garlic clove for added flavor. | Spoon the tomato and basil mixture generously over the toasted bread slices. | Drizzle a little olive oil over the top of each bruschetta. | Serve immediately, garnished with extra basil leaves if desired.

name: Brussels Sprouts Italian Style
description: This Italian-style Brussels sprouts recipe features pan-seared sprouts with garlic, Parmesan cheese, and fresh parsley for a flavorful and simple side dish.
instructions: Rinse the brussels sprouts thoroughly under cold water and trim the ends, then cut them in half. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. | Add minced garlic to the skillet and sauté until fragrant, about 1 minute. | Add the brussels sprouts halves cut side down to the skillet and cook without stirring for 5-7 minutes until they start to brown. | Stir the brussels sprouts and continue cooking for an additional 5 minutes until tender but still crisp. | Season with salt, freshly ground black pepper, and a pinch of red pepper flakes for a mild kick. | Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and chopped fresh parsley, mixing until the cheese melts and coats the sprouts. | Remove from heat and garnish with extra Parmesan and parsley if desired before serving.

name: Chicken Karaage
description: Chicken Karaage is a popular Japanese fried chicken dish characterized by marinated bite-sized pieces coated in starch and fried to a crispy golden brown. It is a flavorful and juicy appetizer or main dish, often served with lemon wedges.
instructions: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces. | In a bowl, combine soy sauce, sake, grated ginger, and grated garlic to make the marinade. | Add the chicken pieces to the marinade, mix well, and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes in the refrigerator. | In a separate bowl, mix potato starch and all-purpose flour. | Drain the excess marinade from the chicken pieces, then coat each piece evenly with the starch and flour mixture. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan or pot to 170°C (340°F). | Fry the chicken pieces in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes per batch. | Remove the fried chicken and drain on paper towels. | Serve hot with lemon wedges on the side.

name: Chicken Katsu
description: Chicken Katsu is a Japanese dish consisting of breaded and deep-fried chicken cutlets, crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, typically served with a savory tonkatsu sauce.
instructions: Pat the chicken breast dry and pound to an even thickness of about 1 cm. | Season both sides of the chicken breast with salt and pepper. | Set up three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten egg, and one with panko breadcrumbs. | Coat the chicken breast first in flour, shaking off excess. | Dip the floured chicken into the beaten egg, ensuring it is fully coated. | Press the chicken into the panko breadcrumbs until fully covered, pressing gently to adhere. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat to about 170°C (340°F). | Fry the chicken cutlets for 4-5 minutes on each side until golden brown and cooked through. | Remove the chicken from the oil and drain on paper towels. | Slice the chicken katsu into strips and serve with tonkatsu sauce and cooked white rice if desired.

name: Chicken Nanban
description: Chicken Nanban is a Japanese dish consisting of fried chicken marinated in a tangy sweet vinegar sauce, served with creamy tartar sauce. This dish blends crispy fried chicken with a flavorful sauce and creamy topping for a unique experience.
instructions: In a bowl, combine egg and a pinch of salt and pepper, and mix well. | Cut chicken thigh into bite-sized pieces and season with salt and pepper. | Dip the chicken pieces into the beaten egg, then coat evenly with potato starch. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan to 170°C (340°F). | Fry the chicken pieces in hot oil until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove and drain on paper towels. | In a separate saucepan, combine vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, and water, then bring to a gentle simmer to make the nanban sauce. | Dip the fried chicken pieces into the warm nanban sauce for a few seconds, then place them on a plate. | To make the tartar sauce, mix chopped boiled egg, diced onion, chopped pickled cucumber, chopped parsley, and mayonnaise in a bowl. | Serve the sauced chicken with a generous spoonful of tartar sauce on top or on the side.

name: Chicken Rice
description: Chicken Rice, also known as Ketchup Rice, is a simple and flavorful dish made with cooked rice stir-fried with chicken, scrambled egg, and ketchup, popular for its sweet and savory taste.
instructions: Cook the rice according to package instructions and set aside. | Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat. | Add chopped onion and minced garlic, sauté until fragrant and translucent. | Add diced chicken pieces and cook until they are no longer pink. | Push the chicken and onions to the side of the pan, then scramble beaten eggs in the cleared space until cooked through. | Mix the eggs with the chicken and onions. | Add cooked rice to the skillet, stirring and breaking up any clumps. | Pour ketchup over the rice mixture and stir well to evenly coat all the ingredients. | Season with salt and pepper to taste. | Cook for a few more minutes until the rice is heated through and flavors are combined. | Garnish with chopped scallion before serving.

name: Chicken Steak Japanese-style
description: A simple Japanese-style chicken steak cooked with a savory and slightly sweet soy-based sauce, often enjoyed with grated daikon and green onion garnish.
instructions: Pat the chicken breast dry and season both sides with salt and pepper. | Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. | Place the chicken breast in the skillet and cook for 5-6 minutes on one side without moving it to get a nice golden crust. | Flip the chicken and cook for another 5-6 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and juices run clear. | Remove the chicken from the skillet and let it rest for a few minutes before slicing. | In the same skillet, add soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar to make the sauce. | Bring the sauce to a simmer while stirring, allowing it to thicken slightly. | Place the sliced chicken steak back into the skillet and coat it with the sauce. | Serve the chicken topped with the sauce and garnish with chopped green onion and grated daikon if desired.

name: Chicken Wings Simmered in Soy
description: This dish features chicken wings slowly simmered in a flavorful soy sauce-based broth, resulting in tender meat infused with a savory and slightly sweet glaze inspired by Asian cuisine.
instructions: Rinse the chicken wings under cold water and pat dry with paper towels. | In a large pot, combine soy sauce, water, sugar, minced garlic, grated ginger, and star anise. | Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring to dissolve the sugar. | Add the chicken wings to the pot and reduce the heat to low to maintain a gentle simmer. | Cover the pot and simmer the wings for about 30 to 40 minutes, occasionally turning the wings to ensure even cooking and absorption of flavors. | Once the wings are tender and have absorbed the sauce, remove the lid and increase the heat to medium-high to reduce the sauce until slightly thickened, about 5 to 10 minutes. | Remove the star anise and discard it. | Serve the wings hot, spooning the reduced soy sauce over them as a glaze.

name: Chikara Udon
description: Chikara Udon, also known as Mochi Udon, is a traditional Japanese noodle soup featuring udon noodles topped with toasted mochi, served in a flavorful dashi-based broth, offering a comforting and fulfilling meal.
instructions: Prepare the mochi by cutting it into bite-sized pieces if using large mochi cakes. | In a pot, bring dashi broth to a gentle boil. Dashi can be made from kombu and bonito flakes or use instant dashi powder mixed with water. | Add the soy sauce, mirin, and sugar into the broth and stir until dissolved to make the soup base. | Add the pre-cooked udon noodles into the broth and simmer gently until heated through, about 2-3 minutes. | Separately, toast or lightly grill the mochi pieces until they puff up and turn slightly golden. | Ladle the udon noodles and broth into serving bowls, then carefully place the toasted mochi on top. | Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and a few strips of toasted nori. | Serve immediately while hot.

name: Chikuwa Isobe Age
description: Chikuwa Isobe Age is a Japanese appetizer featuring fried fish cake wrapped in seaweed, creating a crispy and savory snack perfect for sharing.
instructions: Cut the chikuwa into bite-sized pieces, about 2-3 cm thick. | In a small bowl, beat the egg until well combined. | Place the seaweed sheets on a flat surface and cut them into small rectangles to wrap around the chikuwa pieces. | Wrap each chikuwa piece with a piece of seaweed, using a small amount of egg to seal the edges if needed. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan or pot to 170-180°C (340-360°F). | Dip each seaweed-wrapped chikuwa piece into the beaten egg, ensuring it is coated well. | Carefully place the dipped chikuwa pieces into the hot oil and fry until golden brown and crisp, about 2-3 minutes. | Remove the fried chikuwa from the oil and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. | Serve hot with soy sauce or a dipping sauce of your choice.

name: Chikuwa and Vegetable Nimono
description: Chikuwa and Vegetable Nimono is a comforting Japanese simmered dish featuring fish cake and seasonal vegetables simmered in a flavorful dashi broth with soy sauce, mirin, and sugar.
instructions: Peel the carrot and cut it into bite-sized pieces. Peel the potato and cut it into chunks. Cut the konnyaku into bite-sized pieces by first slicing it thinly, then cutting into rectangles. Blanch the konnyaku in boiling water for 1-2 minutes to remove any odor, then drain. | Cut the chikuwa into bite-sized pieces. | Heat the dashi stock in a pot and add the potato and carrot pieces. Simmer over medium heat until they begin to soften, about 10 minutes. | Add the konnyaku and chikuwa to the pot. Add soy sauce, mirin, and sugar. Continue to simmer gently, partially covered, for another 10-15 minutes until all ingredients are tender and have absorbed the flavors. | Add salt and additional soy sauce to taste if necessary. | Turn off the heat and let the nimono rest for a few minutes to allow flavors to meld before serving.

name: Chikuzen-ni
description: Chikuzen-ni is a classic Japanese simmered dish from Kyushu region featuring braised chicken and a mix of root vegetables in a savory soy-based broth, known for its comforting and rich flavors.
instructions: Soak dried shiitake mushroom in warm water for 30 minutes, then slice thinly and reserve the soaking liquid. | Cut chicken thighs into bite-size pieces and blanch in boiling water briefly to remove impurities, then drain and set aside. | Peel and cut lotus root into 1cm slices and soak in water with a little vinegar to prevent discoloration. | Peel and cut carrot into chunks. | Peel and cut burdock root into thin diagonal slices and soak in water with a little vinegar to remove bitterness. | Peel and cut taro into chunks. | Heat sesame oil in a pot over medium heat, then add chicken pieces and sauté until lightly browned. | Add sliced shiitake mushroom, lotus root, carrot, burdock root, and taro to the pot, and stir-fry together for a few minutes. | Pour in the shiitake soaking liquid (strained), dashi stock, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar into the pot, then bring to a boil. | Reduce heat to low, cover with a drop lid or foil, and simmer gently for about 30 minutes or until vegetables are tender and flavors are absorbed. | Uncover and simmer for an additional 5-10 minutes to reduce liquid slightly if needed. | Serve warm or at room temperature as a side dish or part of a meal.

name: Birria De Res
description: Birria de Res is a traditional Mexican beef stew cooked with a rich blend of dried chiles and spices, resulting in a deeply flavorful and tender meat dish often served with fresh garnishes and corn tortillas.
instructions: Prepare the dried chiles by removing stems and seeds, then soak them in hot water for 20 minutes until softened. | In a blender, combine soaked chiles, garlic, white vinegar, cumin, oregano, cloves, cinnamon, black pepper, and salt to create the marinade sauce. | Cut the beef into large chunks and coat thoroughly with the marinade. Let it marinate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight in the refrigerator. | In a large pot, heat some vegetable oil over medium heat and brown the marinated beef pieces on all sides to seal in the flavors. | Add chopped onion, bay leaves, and enough beef broth to cover the meat. Bring to a boil, then reduce to simmer and cook covered for about 3 hours or until the beef is tender and can be shredded easily. | Once cooked, remove the beef and shred it with forks. Strain the cooking liquid to remove solids and return the liquid to the pot. | Add the shredded beef back into the pot with the broth and keep warm. | To serve, ladle the stew into bowls and garnish with chopped onion, fresh cilantro, and lime wedges. Optionally, serve with warm corn tortillas and chopped radish on the side.

name: Bistec Encebollado
description: Bistec Encebollado is a traditional Latin American dish featuring tender beef steak marinated and cooked with sautéed onions, offering a flavorful and comforting meal.
instructions: Marinate the steak pieces with garlic, salt, pepper, and vinegar for at least 30 minutes. | Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. | Remove the steak from the marinade and cook in the hot oil until browned on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side depending on thickness. | Remove the steak from the skillet and set aside, keeping warm. | In the same skillet, add sliced onion and cook until translucent and slightly caramelized, about 5-7 minutes. | Add the remaining marinade to the skillet with onions and simmer for a couple of minutes to combine flavors. | Return the steak to the skillet with onions and cook together for another 2 minutes to warm through and meld the flavors. | Serve the bistec topped with the sautéed onions and sauce, accompanied by rice or fried plantains if desired.

name: Bistec Ranchero
description: Bistec Ranchero is a traditional Mexican dish featuring a pan-seared seasoned steak served with a fresh tomato-onion-chili sauce, embodying bold flavors typical of ranch-style cooking.
instructions: Pat the steak dry with paper towels and season both sides with salt and pepper. | Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. | Add the steak to the skillet and cook for about 3-4 minutes per side, or until browned and cooked to your desired doneness. | Remove the steak from the skillet and set aside to rest. | In the same skillet, add the chopped onion and garlic, sauté until softened and fragrant, about 2 minutes. | Add the diced tomato, chopped jalapeno, and chopped cilantro to the skillet and cook for another 3 minutes, stirring occasionally. | Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste. | Return the steak to the skillet and spoon the sauce over the top. | Simmer everything together for 2 minutes to allow flavors to meld. | Serve the ranch-style steak hot, garnished with extra cilantro if desired.

name: Bistec a La Mexicana
description: Bistec a la Mexicana is a traditional Mexican dish featuring tender steak strips cooked with fresh tomatoes, onion, jalapeno, and cilantro for a flavorful and colorful meal.
instructions: Slice the steak into thin strips for quicker cooking and better absorption of flavors. | Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. | Add the sliced onion and cook until translucent. | Add the chopped tomato and jalapeno, cooking until softened. | Add the sliced steak to the skillet and cook until browned on all sides. | Season with salt and pepper and continue cooking until steak is cooked through. | Add chopped cilantro at the end, stirring to combine. | Serve hot with warm tortillas and optional sides such as rice or beans.

name: Bistec in Pasilla Chile Sauce
description: Bistec en Salsa de Chile Pasilla is a traditional Mexican dish featuring tender beef steak simmered in a rich and flavorful pasilla chile sauce, offering a balanced heat and smoky taste.
instructions: Rinse the beef steak and pat it dry with paper towels. | Season both sides of the steak with salt and pepper. | Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. | Add the steak to the skillet and sear for about 4 minutes on each side or until cooked to your preferred level of doneness. | Remove the steak from the skillet and keep warm. | In the same skillet, add the sliced onion and cook until translucent, about 3 minutes. | Add the garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Pour in the pasilla chile sauce and stir to combine with the onions and garlic. | Simmer the sauce for 5 minutes to heat through and meld flavors. | Return the steak to the skillet and spoon the sauce over it. | Cook together for another 2-3 minutes to allow the steak to absorb some of the sauce. | Serve the bistec topped with the pasilla chile sauce, garnished with fresh cilantro if desired.

name: Black Bean Soup
description: Black Bean Soup is a hearty, flavorful dish made with simmered black beans and aromatic spices, originating from Latin American cuisine. It is commonly enjoyed as a nutritious and comforting soup.
instructions: Rinse the black beans thoroughly under cold water and soak them overnight in enough water to cover. | Drain the soaked beans and place them in a large pot with fresh water covering by about two inches. | Bring the water to a boil, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook the beans for about 1 to 1.5 hours or until tender. | While the beans cook, heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. | Add diced onion, minced garlic, and diced green bell pepper to the skillet and sauté until the vegetables are soft and translucent. | Add ground cumin, chili powder, and smoked paprika to the vegetables and cook for another minute to release their aroma. | When the beans are tender, add the sautéed vegetables and spices to the pot. | Stir in salt and black pepper to taste and simmer the soup for another 20 minutes to meld flavors. | For a smoother texture, use an immersion blender to partially puree the soup, leaving some beans whole for texture. | Remove from heat and stir in freshly chopped cilantro and lime juice. | Serve the soup hot, optionally garnished with sour cream, avocado slices, or additional cilantro if desired.

name: Black Sapote Ice Cream
description: Black Sapote Ice Cream is a creamy frozen dessert made from the sweet, chocolate-like pulp of black sapote, a tropical fruit. This refreshing treat has a smooth custard base blended with the unique flavor of black sapote, popular in Central America.
instructions: Peel the black sapote and scoop out the pulp into a bowl. | Mash the pulp until smooth and set aside. | In a saucepan, heat the milk, cream, and sugar over medium heat until the sugar dissolves, stirring occasionally. | Remove from heat and let cool slightly. | In a separate bowl, whisk the egg yolks. | Gradually add some of the warm milk mixture into the egg yolks to temper them, whisking constantly. | Return the egg yolk mixture to the saucepan and cook over low heat, stirring constantly until the mixture thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon. | Remove from heat and strain the custard into a clean bowl. | Let the custard cool to room temperature, then stir in the mashed black sapote pulp and vanilla extract. | Cover and refrigerate until thoroughly chilled, at least 4 hours or overnight. | Pour the mixture into an ice cream maker and churn according to the manufacturer's instructions until it reaches a soft-serve consistency. | Transfer the ice cream to a container and freeze until firm, about 4 hours. | Serve the black sapote ice cream chilled.

name: Blue Corn Tortillas
description: Blue Corn Tortillas are traditional Mexican handmade tortillas made from blue corn masa harina, known for their distinctive color and slightly nutty flavor. They serve as a gluten-free, vegan base for many Mexican dishes.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine blue corn masa harina with salt. | Slowly add warm water to the masa harina and mix with your hands or a spoon until a soft dough forms. If the dough is too dry, add water a little at a time; if too sticky, add a bit more masa harina. | Divide the dough into equal portions and roll each into a ball about the size of a golf ball. | Place a ball of dough between two sheets of plastic or parchment paper on a tortilla press or use a flat surface and a heavy skillet to press down the dough ball into a thin, round tortilla. | Carefully peel off the plastic or parchment paper from both sides. | Heat a dry skillet or griddle over medium-high heat until hot. | Place one tortilla on the skillet and cook for about 30 seconds until the edges start to lift, then flip and cook the other side for another 30 seconds. | Flip the tortilla again and cook for a few more seconds until light brown spots appear and the tortilla puffs slightly. | Remove the tortilla and keep warm wrapped in a clean kitchen towel while you cook the remaining tortillas.

name: Borrachitos
description: Borrachitos are traditional Mexican drunken candies made with sugar, fruit flavoring, and tequila or rum, giving them a sweet and boozy flavor. These chewy candies are coated in sugar and enjoyed as a festive treat.
instructions: In a large saucepan, combine water, sugar, and corn syrup. Heat over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves completely. | Bring the mixture to a boil without stirring until it reaches the soft ball stage (about 115°C or 240°F on a candy thermometer). | Remove the saucepan from the heat and stir in the butter and fruit flavoring (such as strawberry or cherry). | Allow the mixture to cool slightly and then add the tequila or rum, stirring gently to combine. | Pour the mixture onto a buttered or parchment-lined flat surface and let it cool until firm but pliable. | Cut the candy into small rectangles or desired shapes while still pliable. | Optional: Roll each candy in granulated sugar to prevent sticking and add sweetness. | Store the candies in an airtight container, preferably refrigerated, and consume within a week.

name: Breaded Fish Fillet
description: Breaded fish fillet is a popular dish where a fish fillet is coated in flour, egg, and breadcrumbs, then fried until golden and crispy. It is a simple and delicious way to enjoy fish with a crunchy exterior.
instructions: Pat the fish fillet dry with paper towels to remove excess moisture. | Season the fillet with salt and pepper on both sides. | Set up three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten egg, and one with breadcrumbs. | Dip the fillet first into the flour, shaking off excess. | Then dip it into the beaten egg, ensuring it is fully coated. | Finally, press the fillet into the breadcrumbs, covering evenly. | Heat vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium heat. | Place the breaded fillet into the hot oil and fry until golden brown and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes per side depending on thickness. | Remove the fish from the pan and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. | Serve hot with lemon wedges and your choice of side.

name: Beef and Turnip Stew
description: A hearty and comforting stew combining tender beef with earthy turnip and root vegetables, simmered in rich beef broth. This traditional dish is perfect for warming up on a cold day.
instructions: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes and season with salt and pepper. | Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef cubes on all sides. Remove and set aside. | Peel and chop the turnip into chunks. | In the same pot, add chopped onion and minced garlic, and sauté until softened. | Return the beef to the pot, add beef broth and bring to a boil. | Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 1 hour until beef is tender. | Add the chopped turnip, diced carrot, and diced potato to the pot. | Continue simmering for another 30-40 minutes until vegetables are tender. | Stir in chopped parsley and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve hot, garnished with additional parsley if desired.

name: Beef and Vegetable Broth
description: A flavorful homemade beef and vegetable broth made by simmering beef bones with aromatic vegetables and herbs, perfect as a base for soups and stews.
instructions: Place beef bones in a large pot and cover with cold water. | Bring to a boil over high heat and then reduce to a simmer. Skim off any foam that rises to the surface. | Add chopped onion, carrot, celery, garlic, bay leaf, thyme, and peppercorns to the pot. | Simmer gently for at least 3 hours, uncovered, to develop rich flavor. | Occasionally skim fat and impurities from the surface. | After cooking, strain the broth through a fine mesh sieve into another pot or large bowl. | Discard solids and let the broth cool slightly. | Season with salt to taste. | Use immediately or refrigerate or freeze for later use.

name: Beef and Wine Pot
description: A classic hearty French-style beef stew slowly cooked with red wine, vegetables, and herbs to develop deep flavors, perfect for a comforting meal.
instructions: Cut the beef into large cubes and season with salt and pepper. | Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef cubes on all sides. | Remove the beef and set aside. | Add the chopped onion, carrot, and celery to the pot and sauté until softened. | Add the garlic and cook for another minute. | Return the beef to the pot and sprinkle with flour, stirring to coat the meat evenly. | Pour in the red wine and beef broth, scraping the bottom of the pot to release any browned bits. | Add the tomato paste, bay leaf, thyme, salt, and pepper. | Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer gently for about 2 hours until the beef is tender. | In the last 20 minutes, add the mushrooms and cook until soft. | Remove the bay leaf and serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley if desired.

name: Beef with Beer Sauce
description: Beef cooked and served with a rich and flavorful beer sauce that combines savory broth and mustard for a hearty main dish.
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper on both sides. | Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and sear the beef for 3-4 minutes per side until browned and cooked to desired doneness. Remove beef and set aside to rest. | In the same skillet, add chopped onion and garlic and sauté until softened. | Pour in the beer and deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. | Add beef broth, Dijon mustard, and Worcestershire sauce, stirring to combine. | Simmer the sauce for 8-10 minutes until it reduces slightly and thickens. | Return the beef to the skillet and coat with the sauce, heating through for 1-2 minutes. | Serve the beef with the beer sauce spooned over the top.

name: Beef with Green Beans
description: Beef with green beans is a simple and flavorful stir-fried dish that combines tender strips of beef with crisp green beans in a savory sauce. It's a popular, quick, and healthy Chinese-inspired meal.
instructions: Trim the ends of the green beans and wash them thoroughly. | Cut the beef into thin strips against the grain. | Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. | Add the beef strips and stir-fry until browned and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes. Remove beef from the skillet and set aside. | In the same skillet, add a little more vegetable oil if needed, then add minced garlic and stir-fry until fragrant, about 30 seconds. | Add the green beans to the skillet and stir-fry for about 4-5 minutes until they are crisp-tender. | Return the beef to the skillet with the green beans. | Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar; stir well to combine and cook for another 1-2 minutes, allowing the sauce to coat the beef and green beans evenly. | Season with salt and black pepper to taste. | Serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Beef with Tomato and Pepper Stew
description: A hearty stew featuring tender beef cubes simmered with fresh tomatoes and bell peppers, flavored with garlic and oregano for a comforting and flavorful dish.
instructions: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes and season with salt and pepper. | Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and sear the beef cubes until browned on all sides, then remove and set aside. | In the same pot, add chopped onion and minced garlic, sauté until translucent and fragrant. | Add diced bell pepper and cook for a few minutes until slightly softened. | Stir in chopped tomatoes, tomato paste, and cook for another 5 minutes to develop flavors. | Return the browned beef to the pot and add beef broth and dried oregano. | Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer covered for about 1.5 to 2 hours until the beef is tender. | Season with additional salt and pepper to taste before serving.

name: Beet and Goat Cheese Salad
description: A fresh and colorful beet and goat cheese salad combining roasted beets with creamy goat cheese, mixed greens, and a tangy balsamic dressing. This salad is a bright and elegant starter perfect for any occasion.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Wash the beetroot thoroughly and wrap each beetroot in aluminum foil. Place on a baking tray and roast in the oven for about 45-60 minutes, until tender when pierced with a fork. | Remove the beets from the oven and let them cool. Once cool, peel the skin off and cut the beets into thin slices or bite-sized pieces. | In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper to make the dressing. | In a large salad bowl, combine the sliced beets, mixed salad greens, and chopped walnuts. | Drizzle the dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine. | Crumble the goat cheese over the top of the salad. | Garnish with fresh parsley leaves and serve immediately.

name: Bifana Sandwich
description: Bifana sandwich is a traditional Portuguese sandwich featuring thinly marinated and cooked pork shoulder served in a crusty roll, known for its flavorful and juicy character.
instructions: Combine minced garlic, paprika, white wine, olive oil, salt, and pepper to make a marinade. | Place thinly sliced pork shoulder in the marinade and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight for more flavor. | Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the marinated pork slices until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. | Split Portuguese rolls (papo secos) horizontally, but do not cut all the way through to keep them hinged. | Place the cooked pork inside the rolls, allowing some juices to soak into the bread. | Optionally, add mustard or piri-piri sauce to taste for extra flavor. | Serve the bifana sandwich warm, as a traditional Portuguese street food.

name: Bifana in Bread
description: Bifana no Pão is a traditional Portuguese sandwich featuring marinated pork served in a crusty bread roll. It is a flavorful and popular street food in Portugal.
instructions: Slice the pork shoulder into thin pieces or small strips for quick cooking. | Marinate the pork with minced garlic, paprika, white wine, white wine vinegar, bay leaf, and salt. Let it rest for at least 1 hour, preferably overnight in the refrigerator. | Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. | Add the marinated pork pieces to the skillet and cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. | Remove the bay leaf from the cooked pork mixture. | Slice the Portuguese bread rolls horizontally, not cutting all the way through, keeping a hinge. | Fill the bread rolls generously with the cooked pork and some of the pan juices. | Optionally, add mustard or piri-piri sauce to taste before serving. | Serve the Bifana sandwiches hot, ideally accompanied by fries or a salad.

name: Black Pork Loin Alentejo Style
description: Black Pork Loin Alentejo Style is a traditional Portuguese dish from the Alentejo region, featuring tender pork loin braised in a savory sauce of white wine, paprika, and herbs, served with potatoes.
instructions: Cut the black pork loin into thick slices and marinate with garlic, white wine, paprika, bay leaf, salt, and pepper for at least 2 hours or overnight in the refrigerator. | Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat and brown the pork slices on all sides until golden but not completely cooked through. | Remove the pork and set aside. In the same skillet, sauté sliced onions until translucent, then add chopped garlic and cook for another minute. | Add diced tomato and cook until softened. Stir in paprika and bay leaf, then return the pork to the skillet. | Pour in white wine and enough water to cover the pork halfway. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for about 45 minutes until pork is tender and the sauce has thickened. | In the last 10 minutes of cooking, add diced potatoes and cook until tender. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Remove bay leaf and garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

name: Bacalao Dorado
description: Bacalao Dorado (Golden Salt Cod) is a traditional Portuguese dish made with salted cod, fried potatoes, onions, and eggs. It is beloved for its comforting flavors and rich, golden texture.
instructions: Soak the salt cod in cold water for 24 to 48 hours, changing the water every 8 hours to remove excess salt. | Drain and rinse the cod, then place it in a pot with fresh water and simmer gently for about 20 minutes until tender. | Drain the cod again and let it cool, then remove any skin and bones and flake the fish into small pieces with your fingers or a fork. | Peel and finely slice the potatoes into thin strips. | In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat and fry the potato strips until golden and crisp. Remove and drain on paper towels. | In the same oil, fry the sliced onion until soft and translucent. | Add the flaked cod to the onions and stir well for a few minutes. | Return the fried potatoes to the skillet and mix everything thoroughly, cooking gently for a few more minutes to blend the flavors. | Crack the eggs into a bowl, beat them lightly, then pour over the cod mixture in the skillet. | Cook on low heat, stirring continuously, until the eggs are softly set but still moist. | Season with freshly ground black pepper and a pinch of salt if needed. | Serve warm as a main dish or appetizer.

name: Bacalao En Salsa Verde
description: Bacalao en Salsa Verde is a traditional Spanish dish featuring tender salted cod cooked in a vibrant green sauce made with garlic, parsley, and white wine, showcasing simple yet fresh Mediterranean flavors.
instructions: Soak the salted cod in cold water for 24 to 36 hours, changing the water several times to desalinate. | Drain the cod and pat dry with paper towels, then cut into portions. | Bring a pot of water to a boil and blanch the cod pieces for about 5 minutes to remove excess salt and firm up the fish; drain and set aside. | Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat, add chopped garlic and gently sauté until fragrant but not browned. | Add chopped fresh parsley and cook briefly with garlic to release aroma. | Add white wine and simmer for a few minutes to reduce the alcohol and blend flavors. | Return the cod pieces to the pan with the sauce and cook gently for 5 to 7 minutes until the cod is heated through and infused with the green sauce. | Optionally, add some cooked peas to the sauce and stir gently to combine. | Season with salt and pepper to taste, keeping in mind the cod was salted beforehand. | Serve the cod hot, spooning ample green sauce over the top, garnished with extra parsley if desired.

name: Bacalao Gratinado
description: Bacalao Gratinado is a traditional Spanish dish featuring cod baked in a creamy bechamel sauce and topped with a golden crust of melted cheese, perfect for a comforting main course.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). | If using salted cod, soak the cod in water for 24-48 hours, changing the water several times to remove excess salt. Drain and pat dry. | Poach the cod in milk over low heat until cooked and tender, about 10-15 minutes. Remove cod from milk and reserve the milk for sauce. | In a pan, melt butter and sauté chopped onion until soft and translucent. | Add flour to the pan and cook while stirring to make a roux, about 2 minutes. | Gradually add the reserved milk to the roux, stirring constantly to make a bechamel sauce. Cook until thickened. | Season the sauce with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. | Flake the cooked cod into large pieces and combine gently with the bechamel sauce. | Place the cod mixture into a buttered baking dish. | Sprinkle grated cheese evenly over the top. | Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, until the top is golden brown and bubbling. | Let it cool for a few minutes before serving.

name: Bacalao Pil Pil
description: Bacalao Pil Pil is a traditional Basque dish featuring salt cod cooked slowly in olive oil with garlic and chili, creating a silky emulsified sauce known as pil pil.
instructions: Soak the dried salt cod in cold water for 48 hours, changing the water every 12 hours to desalinate the fish. | Remove the cod from the water, pat dry, and cut into medium-sized pieces. | Peel and finely slice the garlic cloves. | Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over low heat and add the sliced garlic and dried chili pepper to infuse the oil gently without burning. | Add the cod pieces skin-side down to the pan and cook slowly over low heat until they start releasing gelatin. | Continuously and very gently shake the pan in small circular motions to emulsify the oil with the released gelatin from the fish, forming a creamy pil pil sauce. | Keep this gentle movement for about 20-30 minutes until the sauce thickens and becomes glossy, ensuring the cod is tender and cooked through. | Discard the garlic and chili if desired, season with a pinch of salt if necessary (considering the saltiness of the cod). | Serve the Bacalao Pil Pil hot with some fresh parsley sprinkled on top.

name: Bacalao Rebozado
description: Bacalao Rebozado is a traditional Spanish dish featuring salted cod dipped in a light batter and deep-fried until crispy. This flavorful seafood dish is popular as a main course or tapas item.
instructions: Soak the salted cod in water for 24 to 48 hours, changing the water several times to remove excess salt. | Drain the cod and pat it dry with paper towels, then cut it into medium-sized pieces, about 100 g each. | Prepare the batter by mixing the flour with sparkling water until smooth and slightly thick, and season with a pinch of salt. | Heat the vegetable oil in a deep pan or fryer until hot enough for frying (around 180°C or 350°F). | Dip each piece of cod into the batter, ensuring it is fully coated. | Carefully place the battered cod pieces into the hot oil and fry until golden and crisp, about 3 to 4 minutes per side. | Remove the fried cod from the oil and place on paper towels to drain excess oil. | Serve the battered cod hot, optionally garnished with lemon wedges and fresh parsley.

name: Bacalao a La Llauna
description: Bacalao a la Llauna is a traditional Catalan dish featuring salt cod cooked with garlic, onion, and smoked paprika, offering rich Mediterranean flavors.
instructions: Soak the salt cod in cold water for 48 hours, changing the water every 8 hours to remove excess salt. | Drain the cod and pat it dry with paper towels, then cut into portions if needed. | Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F). | Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. | Add minced garlic and sliced onion, sautéing until softened and fragrant. | Place the cod portions in a shallow ovenproof dish and pour the garlic and onion olive oil mixture evenly over them. | Sprinkle smoked paprika over the cod and season lightly with black pepper and a small pinch of salt if necessary. | Add lemon juice over the fish and drizzle a little more olive oil. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 10-15 minutes, until the cod is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork. | Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and serve hot, traditionally accompanied by roasted potatoes or bread.

name: Bacalao a La Vizcaina
description: Bacalao a la Vizcaina is a classic Basque dish made with salted cod simmered in a rich tomato and red pepper sauce, showcasing traditional flavors from northern Spain.
instructions: Soak the salted cod in cold water for 24 to 48 hours, changing the water several times to remove excess salt. | Drain and pat the cod dry, then cut into serving-size pieces. | Peel and chop the onions and garlic finely. | In a large pan, heat olive oil over medium heat and sauté the chopped onions until translucent. | Add the garlic and cook for another minute without browning. | Add the red peppers (piquillo or roasted bell pepper) sliced into thin strips and cook gently. | Pour in the tomato sauce or crushed tomatoes and cook the sauce on low heat until thickened, about 20 minutes. | Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste. | In a separate pan, lightly fry the cod pieces in olive oil for about 2-3 minutes per side until the fish is just cooked but still moist. | Place the cod pieces in the pan with the sauce, spoon the sauce over the fish, cover, and cook for an additional 5 minutes on low heat to allow flavors to meld. | Serve the Bacalao a la Vizcina hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley if desired.

name: Bacalao a La Vizcaina
description: Bacalao a la Vizcaina is a traditional Basque dish of salted cod simmered in a rich red pepper and tomato sauce, celebrated for its deep flavors and regional heritage.
instructions: Soak the salted cod in cold water for 24 to 48 hours, changing the water several times to remove excess salt. | Drain the cod and cut it into serving-sized pieces, removing any skin and bones. | In a large pan, heat olive oil over medium heat and gently cook finely chopped onion and garlic until soft and translucent. | Add diced fresh tomato and continue cooking until they break down into a sauce. | Add red bell pepper puree to the pan and stir well with the tomato mixture. | Simmer the sauce gently for about 20 to 30 minutes to develop flavor, seasoning with a pinch of salt and pepper. | Carefully add the soaked cod pieces into the sauce and simmer gently for another 15 minutes until the cod is tender and infused with the sauce. | Serve the Bacalao a la Vizcaina hot, garnished with parsley if desired, accompanied by boiled potatoes or crusty bread.

name: Baked Gilthead Bream
description: Dorada al Horno is a simple, traditional Spanish recipe featuring gilthead bream baked with lemon, garlic, and fresh parsley, resulting in a flavorful and tender fish dish.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F). | Clean the gilthead bream by removing scales and innards, then pat dry with paper towels. | Make several diagonal cuts on both sides of the fish to allow even cooking and better flavor absorption. | Season the fish inside and out with salt and pepper. | Stuff the cavity of the fish with lemon slices, garlic cloves, and sprigs of fresh parsley. | Place the fish on a baking tray lined with parchment paper or lightly oiled. | Drizzle olive oil generously over the fish and around it on the tray. | Add a few more lemon slices and extra parsley sprigs on top for flavor and presentation. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 25-30 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork. | Remove from the oven and let rest for a couple of minutes before serving.

name: Baked Hake
description: Baked Hake is a simple Spanish dish featuring tender hake fillets baked with garlic, onion, parsley, and white wine, creating a flavorful and healthy meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F). | Clean the hake fillets and pat dry with paper towels. | Place the hake fillets in a baking dish, skin side down if applicable. | Drizzle olive oil over the fish and season with salt, pepper, and minced garlic. | Scatter sliced onion and chopped parsley over the fish. | Pour white wine evenly around the fillets in the baking dish. | Place lemon slices on top of the fish for added flavor. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 20-25 minutes, or until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork. | Remove from oven and let it rest for a few minutes before serving.

name: Gaeng Om Isan
description: Gaeng Om Isan is a traditional Northern Thai herb stew from the Isan region, known for its aromatic blend of local herbs and tender pork simmered in a flavorful broth.
instructions: Prepare the herbs by washing and roughly chopping the dill, culantro, cha-om leaves, and Vietnamese coriander. | Slice the pork into bite-sized pieces and set aside. | In a pot, bring water to a boil and add the sliced pork and thinly sliced galangal, kaffir lime leaves, and lemongrass to infuse flavor. | Simmer the pork for about 15 minutes until tender, skimming off any foam or impurities. | Add the dried chili paste and fish sauce to the broth, stirring to dissolve. | Add the chopped mushrooms and cook for another 5 minutes until tender. | Stir in the prepared herbs and continue to simmer for 2-3 minutes until the herbs are cooked but still vibrant. | Adjust seasoning with more fish sauce or salt if needed. | Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Gaeng Pa
description: Gaeng Pa is a spicy and aromatic Thai jungle curry known for its vibrant flavors from wild herbs and fresh chilies, featuring tender chicken simmered in a fragrant broth.
instructions: Prepare the curry paste by pounding together garlic, shallot, red chili, lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime zest, coriander root, garlic, and shrimp paste until a smooth paste forms. | Heat oil in a pot over medium heat and add the curry paste, stirring until fragrant. | Add sliced wild herbs such as wild ginger leaves, wild basil, and other local jungle greens along with chopped green chilies. | Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil, then reduce to simmer to let flavors meld. | Add bite-sized pieces of chicken and continue to simmer until the chicken is cooked through and tender. | Add fish sauce and a pinch of sugar to season the curry. | Adjust the heat with fresh green chilies and add additional wild herbs just before serving. | Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Gaeng Phak Ruam
description: Gaeng Phak Ruam is a traditional Northern Thai mixed greens curry known for its rich coconut base, aromatic herbs, and a colorful variety of fresh vegetables, delivering a flavorful and comforting dish.
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a pot over medium heat until hot. | Add the red curry paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. | Add the coconut milk gradually while stirring, allowing it to thicken slightly. | Add the mixed greens and other vegetables, stirring to coat with the curry sauce. | Pour in the mushroom broth and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. | Add the sliced Thai eggplant and baby corn, cooking until tender, about 5-7 minutes. | Add the bamboo shoots and continue to simmer for 3-4 minutes. | Season the curry with fish sauce and palm sugar to balance the flavors. | Add kaffir lime leaves and fresh holy basil leaves, stirring to combine. | Simmer for an additional 2 minutes to let the flavors meld. | Remove from heat and serve the curry hot with steamed jasmine rice if desired.

name: Gaeng Phak Wan
description: Gaeng Phak Wan is a traditional northern Thai curry featuring tender northern sweet leaves cooked in a fragrant and mildly spicy coconut milk curry, balanced with sweet palm sugar and savory fish sauce.
instructions: Wash and prepare the northern sweet leaves by removing tough stems and chopping the tender leaves. | Grind or blend together the curry paste ingredients: dried red chili, garlic, shallot, lemongrass, galangal, coriander root, cumin seed, shrimp paste, and salt until a smooth paste forms. | Heat vegetable oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté the curry paste until fragrant. | Add coconut milk and stir well to combine with the curry paste. Bring to a gentle simmer. | Add the northern sweet leaves to the pot and cook until they are tender and have absorbed the flavors of the curry. | Add palm sugar and fish sauce to the curry, stirring to balance the sweet and salty flavors. Adjust seasoning to taste. | Continue simmering for a few minutes to meld all flavors, then remove from heat. | Serve the northern sweet leaf curry hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Gaeng Phed Moo Daeng
description: Gaeng Phed Moo Daeng is a traditional Thai red curry featuring tender red pork cooked in a fragrant and spicy coconut milk-based red curry paste, enriched with herbs and spices, served typically with jasmine rice.
instructions: Prepare the red curry paste by blending red chili, garlic, shallot, lemongrass, galangal, coriander root, cumin, and shrimp paste into a smooth paste. | Heat coconut milk in a pan over medium heat until it starts to separate and oil appears on the surface. | Add the red curry paste to the coconut milk and stir until fragrant and oil resurfaces. | Add sliced red pork to the curry and cook until the pork is heated through and coated with curry sauce. | Add additional coconut milk to adjust the consistency of the curry and bring to a simmer. | Add kaffir lime leaves and palm sugar to the curry and stir to dissolve the sugar. | Season the curry with fish sauce and fresh Thai basil leaves. | Serve the red curry hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Gaeng Phet Ped Yang
description: Gaeng Phet Ped Yang is a classic Thai red curry featuring tender slices of roast duck simmered in a rich and fragrant coconut-based curry with bamboo shoots and aromatic herbs.
instructions: Prepare the red curry paste by blending dried red chili, garlic, shallot, galangal, lemongrass, kaffir lime zest, coriander seed, cumin seed, white peppercorn, shrimp paste, and salt until smooth. | Heat coconut milk in a wok or deep pan over medium heat until it starts to separate, then add the red curry paste and stir-fry until fragrant. | Add the remaining coconut milk, sliced bamboo shoot, and palm sugar, then bring to a gentle simmer. | Add the roasted duck slices to the curry and simmer for 5 minutes to absorb the flavors. | Add fish sauce, lime leaves, Thai basil leaves, and chillies, stir well and cook for another 2 minutes. | Adjust seasoning with fish sauce or sugar as needed. | Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Gaeng Phet Pet Yang
description: Gaeng Phet Pet Yang is a flavorful Thai red curry featuring tender roasted duck combined with aromatic herbs and creamy coconut milk, served traditionally with jasmine rice.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat and add red curry paste. Stir-fry the paste until fragrant, about 2 minutes. | Add coconut milk to the pan and bring to a simmer, stirring to dissolve the curry paste. | Add sliced roasted duck meat to the curry and stir to coat with the sauce. | Add kaffir lime leaves, Thai basil leaves, and palm sugar to the curry; stir well. | Add fish sauce and continue to simmer gently for 5 minutes to blend flavors. | Add sliced bamboo shoots and baby eggplants; cook until tender, about 5 more minutes. | Adjust seasoning with additional fish sauce or palm sugar as needed. | Serve hot, garnished with fresh Thai basil leaves and accompanied by steamed jasmine rice.

name: Gaeng Phet Pet Yang
description: Gaeng Phet Pet Yang is a traditional Thai red curry featuring tender roasted duck cooked in a rich and fragrant coconut milk-based curry with bamboo shoots and aromatic long basil leaves.
instructions: Heat a wok or large pan over medium heat and add the red curry paste. Stir-fry the curry paste in a little coconut milk until fragrant and the oil begins to separate. | Add the roasted duck pieces to the curry paste and stir to coat them well. | Pour in the remaining coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. | Add sliced bamboo shoots and long basil leaves to the curry.
