description: Camarones Empanizados is a popular Mexican dish featuring shrimp coated in flour, egg, and breadcrumbs, then fried until golden and crispy. This simple yet flavorful recipe makes a delicious appetizer or main course.
instructions: Rinse the shrimp under cold water and pat dry with paper towels. | Season the shrimp with salt and pepper on both sides. | Place flour in a shallow bowl. | Beat the egg in a separate shallow bowl. | Place breadcrumbs in another shallow bowl. | Dip each shrimp first in the flour, coating it completely, then in the beaten egg, and finally in the breadcrumbs, pressing lightly to adhere the coating. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep skillet or frying pan over medium-high heat. | Carefully add the breaded shrimp to the hot oil in batches, making sure not to overcrowd the pan. | Fry the shrimp for about 2-3 minutes on each side or until golden brown and cooked through. | Using a slotted spoon, transfer the shrimp to a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil. | Serve the breaded shrimp hot with lemon wedges and your choice of dipping sauce.

name: Breaded Pork Cutlets
description: Crispy and tender breaded pork cutlets lightly seasoned and pan-fried to golden perfection. A classic, simple dish perfect for a comforting meal.
instructions: Pat the pork cutlets dry with paper towels and season both sides with salt and pepper. | Place the flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs in three separate shallow dishes. | Dredge each pork cutlet in flour, shaking off the excess. | Dip the floured cutlet into the beaten egg, then coat it evenly with breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere. | Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat until hot but not smoking. | Cook the breaded pork cutlets in the hot oil for about 3-4 minutes on each side or until golden brown and cooked through. | Transfer the cooked cutlets to a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil. | Serve the breaded pork cutlets hot with lemon wedges and your choice of side dishes.

name: Brigadeiros Portuguese Style
description: Brigadeiros are a popular Brazilian sweet made from condensed milk, cocoa, and butter, rolled into chocolate-coated bite-sized balls. This Portuguese style version captures the traditional Brazilian flavor with a rich, fudgy texture.
instructions: In a medium saucepan, combine the sweetened condensed milk, cocoa powder, and butter. | Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon or spatula, until the mixture thickens and starts to pull away from the sides of the pan, about 10 to 15 minutes. | Remove from heat and transfer the mixture to a greased plate or bowl to cool to room temperature. | Once cooled, butter your hands lightly and roll small portions of the mixture into bite-sized balls. | Roll each ball in granulated sugar or chocolate sprinkles to coat. | Place the brigadeiros in paper cups for serving. | Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving to set the texture.

name: Broa De Milho
description: Broa de Milho is a traditional Portuguese cornbread known for its crumbly texture and slightly sweet flavor, perfect as a side dish to soups and stews.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F). | In a large bowl, mix the cornmeal, all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt until well combined. | In a separate bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, egg, olive oil, and honey until smooth. | Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir gently until just combined; do not overmix. | Transfer the batter into a greased or parchment-lined round baking pan or cast iron skillet, spreading it evenly. | Bake for about 30 to 40 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. | Remove from the oven and let cool slightly before slicing and serving.

name: Broa with Butter and Presunto
alias: Portuguese Cornbread with Butter and Cured Ham
description: Broa with butter and presunto is a traditional Portuguese snack featuring warm cornbread spread with butter and topped with thin slices of cured ham called presunto, offering a simple yet flavorful combination.
instructions: Slice the broa (Portuguese cornbread) into thick pieces. | Spread a generous amount of butter on each slice while the bread is still warm so it melts nicely. | Layer thin slices of presunto (Portuguese cured ham) over the buttered bread. | Serve immediately as a hearty snack or light meal.

name: Broad Bean Rice
description: Broad Bean Rice is a simple and hearty dish featuring tender broad beans cooked with rice and aromatic herbs, popular in Mediterranean cuisine.
instructions: Rinse the rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear, then drain and set aside. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet or saucepan over medium heat. | Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Add the broad beans to the skillet and cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally. | Add the drained rice and stir well to coat the grains with the oil and mix with the beans and onion. | Pour in the vegetable broth and season with salt and pepper to taste. | Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 15-20 minutes or until the rice is cooked and the liquid is absorbed. | Turn off the heat and let it sit covered for 5 minutes. | Fluff the rice with a fork, sprinkle chopped fresh parsley on top, and serve warm.

name: Broad Bean and Bacon Stew
description: A hearty stew combining tender broad beans and crisp bacon, simmered in a flavorful broth. This rustic dish is comforting and perfect for a satisfying meal.
instructions: Rinse the broad beans and remove them from their pods, then blanch them in boiling water for 2 minutes and drain. | In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat and add the chopped onion and garlic until softened and translucent. | Add the diced bacon to the pot and cook until it is crisp and browned. | Add the blanched broad beans to the pot and stir to combine with the bacon mixture. | Pour in the chicken broth and add the chopped tomato along with salt, black pepper, and dried thyme. | Bring the stew to a simmer, cover, and cook for 20 minutes until the broad beans are tender and flavors meld together. | Remove the lid and cook for an additional 5 minutes to reduce the liquid slightly if needed. | Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as desired. | Serve the stew hot, garnished with fresh parsley if desired.

name: Broad Bean and Mint Salad
description: A fresh and vibrant salad featuring tender broad beans and fragrant mint, tossed with a simple lemon and olive oil dressing. This dish makes a perfect light side or starter, highlighting spring flavors.
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add broad beans and cook for 3-4 minutes until tender. Drain and transfer the beans to a bowl of ice water to cool quickly. | Once cooled, drain the broad beans and remove the outer skins by gently squeezing them to reveal the bright green bean inside. | In a large mixing bowl, combine the peeled broad beans, chopped fresh mint leaves, finely sliced red onion, and crumbled feta cheese (if using). | In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and freshly ground black pepper to make the dressing. | Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients and toss gently to combine all flavors. | Adjust seasoning with additional salt and pepper if needed. Serve immediately or chilled for better flavor integration.

name: Broad Bean and Mint Soup
description: A refreshing and vibrant soup combining tender broad beans and fragrant fresh mint, perfect as a light starter or a nutritious meal.
instructions: Shell the broad beans and rinse them under cold water. | Bring a pot of water to a boil, add the broad beans, and blanch them for 3 minutes. | Drain and rinse the beans with cold water, then remove the outer skin to reveal the bright green inner beans. | In a large saucepan, heat olive oil over medium heat and sauté chopped onion until translucent. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute without browning. | Pour in vegetable broth and bring to a simmer. | Add the peeled broad beans to the pot and cook for about 10 minutes until tender. | Add fresh mint leaves and cook for another 2 minutes. | Use an immersion blender to puree the soup until smooth, or transfer to a blender in batches and blend. | Season with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve the soup hot, garnished with a few fresh mint leaves and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Broad Beans with Chorizo
description: Broad Beans with Chorizo is a traditional dish combining tender broad beans with spicy and rich chorizo sausage, sautéed with onions and garlic for a flavorful hearty meal.
instructions: Rinse the broad beans under cold water and remove any tough outer skins if they are fresh and large. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. | Add the chopped chorizo pieces to the skillet and cook until they release their fat and start to brown, about 5 minutes. | Add the chopped onion and garlic to the skillet and sauté until the onion is soft and translucent. | Add the broad beans to the skillet and stir to combine them with the chorizo, onion, and garlic. | Pour in the chicken broth and bring to a simmer. | Cook the mixture for about 10-15 minutes until the broad beans are tender and the liquid has reduced slightly. | Season with salt and black pepper to taste. | Remove from heat and sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving.

name: Broas De Mel
description: Broas de Mel are traditional Portuguese honey cookies, known for their soft texture and warm cinnamon flavor, perfect for a sweet treat.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | In a large bowl, beat the eggs until frothy. | Add honey, sugar, and olive oil to the eggs and mix well until combined. | In a separate bowl, sift together flour, baking powder, and cinnamon. | Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture, stirring until a soft dough forms. | Shape small portions of dough into oval or round cookies and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. | Bake in the preheated oven for 15 to 20 minutes until the cookies are golden brown. | Remove from the oven and let the cookies cool on a wire rack before serving.

name: Bonito Con Tomate
description: Bonito con Tomate is a traditional Spanish dish featuring tender tuna simmered in a rich, homemade tomato sauce, accented with garlic, onion, and fresh herbs.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. | Add chopped onion and garlic, sauté until softened and translucent. | Add finely chopped green bell pepper and cook for a few minutes until tender. | Stir in chopped ripe tomato and cook until the mixture thickens and forms a sauce. | Add tomato paste to enhance the flavor, stirring to combine. | Season the sauce with salt, black pepper, and a pinch of sugar to balance acidity. | Add canned tuna chunks to the tomato sauce, gently stirring to combine without breaking the tuna too much. | Simmer the mixture for about 5 to 10 minutes so the flavors meld together. | Remove from heat and sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Bonito Del Norte Grilled
alias: Bonito Del Norte a La Plancha
description: Bonito del Norte a la Plancha is a traditional Spanish dish where premium white tuna fillets are simply grilled on a hot plate to highlight their delicate flavor and tender texture, often seasoned simply with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
instructions: Heat a griddle pan or heavy skillet over high heat until very hot. | Brush the bonito del norte fillets lightly with olive oil on both sides. | Season the fillets generously with salt and a pinch of black pepper. | Place the fillets skin-side down on the hot griddle. | Cook without moving for about 3-4 minutes until the skin is crisp and the fish is nearly cooked through. | Flip the fillets gently and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes until the fish is opaque and cooked to your preference. | Remove the fish from the heat and let rest for a minute. | Serve the grilled bonito del norte immediately, optionally drizzled with a little more olive oil and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice. | Garnish with fresh parsley if desired and serve with grilled vegetables or a light salad.

name: Boquerones En Vinagre
description: Boquerones en Vinagre is a classic Spanish appetizer featuring fresh anchovies marinated in vinegar until tender and translucent, then seasoned with garlic, parsley, and olive oil for a fresh, tangy flavor.
instructions: Clean the anchovies by removing heads, guts, and bones, then rinse them gently under cold water and pat them dry with paper towels. | Place the cleaned anchovies in a shallow glass or ceramic container and cover them with white vinegar. | Let the anchovies marinate in the refrigerator for about 4 to 6 hours until they turn white and firm. | After marination, drain the vinegar and rinse the anchovies gently with cold water to remove excess vinegar, then pat them dry. | Arrange the anchovies on a serving plate, drizzle with olive oil. | Add thinly sliced garlic cloves over the anchovies and sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley. | Season with salt to taste and let them rest for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld.

name: Boquerones Fritos
description: Boquerones Fritos is a traditional Spanish dish of fresh anchovies lightly dusted in flour and fried until crispy. It is a popular appetizer, known for its delicate texture and vibrant flavor.
instructions: Clean the anchovies by removing heads and guts, then rinse them under cold water and pat dry thoroughly with paper towels. | Place the flour in a shallow bowl and season with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat until hot but not smoking. | Dredge the dried anchovies in the seasoned flour, shaking off any excess. | Fry the anchovies in batches, being careful not to overcrowd the pan, until golden and crispy, about 2-3 minutes per batch. | Use a slotted spoon to transfer the fried anchovies to a plate lined with paper towels to drain any excess oil. | Sprinkle with a pinch of salt while still warm and serve immediately, optionally accompanied by lemon wedges for squeezing over.

name: Borage with Potato
description: Borraja con Patatas is a traditional Aragonese dish featuring tender borage greens cooked with potatoes and garlic, offering a simple, nutritious, and flavorful vegetable side dish.
instructions: Wash the borage thoroughly and cut into manageable pieces, removing any tough stems. | Peel the potatoes and cut them into medium-sized cubes. | Fill a large pot with water, add a pinch of salt, and bring to a boil. | Add the potatoes to the boiling water and cook for about 10 minutes. | Add the borage to the pot with the potatoes and cook together for another 10-15 minutes until both are tender. | Drain the water from the pot and set the borage and potatoes aside. | In a large skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat. | Add the minced garlic to the skillet and sauté until golden and fragrant. | Add the cooked borage and potatoes to the skillet and toss gently to coat with the garlic and oil. | Season with salt and black pepper to taste and cook for another 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally. | Remove from heat and serve warm as a side dish or light main course.

name: Borrachuelos
description: Borrachuelos are traditional Spanish wine fritters from Malaga, lightly fried and coated with cinnamon sugar, offering a sweet and aromatic treat often enjoyed during holidays.
instructions: In a bowl, mix the flour, sugar, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt gently to combine. | Gradually add the wine and olive oil to the flour mixture and stir until a soft dough forms. | Turn the dough onto a floured surface and knead gently for a few minutes until smooth and elastic. | Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and let it rest at room temperature for about 30 minutes. | Roll out the dough thinly on a floured surface. | Cut the dough into diamond or rectangular shapes approximately 8 cm by 5 cm. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat until hot but not smoking. | Fry the dough pieces in batches until golden brown and puffed, about 2-3 minutes per side. | Remove the fritters and drain on paper towels. | While still warm, dip the fritters in a mixture of sugar and ground cinnamon to coat them generously. | Serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Botifarra Amb Mongetes
description: Botifarra amb Mongetes is a traditional Catalan dish featuring savory pork sausages (botifarra) served with tender white beans cooked with garlic and olive oil, highlighting simple yet rich flavors of Catalonia.
instructions: Place the white beans in a large bowl and cover with cold water. Soak the beans overnight or for at least 8 hours. | Drain and rinse the soaked beans. Transfer them to a large pot and cover with fresh water. | Add a pinch of salt and bring the water to a boil. Reduce the heat and let the beans simmer gently until tender, about 1 to 1.5 hours. Skim off any foam during cooking. | In a separate pan, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant but not browned. | Add the botifarra sausages to the pan and cook until browned and cooked through, turning occasionally, about 10-12 minutes. | Once the beans are tender, drain them and return to the pot. Add the cooked garlic and olive oil mixture to the beans and stir gently to combine. | Warm the beans with garlic and olive oil mixture on low heat for a few minutes to let the flavors blend. | Serve the botifarra sausages alongside the warm beans. Optionally, garnish with chopped fresh parsley and season with black pepper to taste.

name: Braised Veal Cheeks
description: Braised Veal Cheeks is a traditional tender and flavorful Spanish dish where veal cheeks are slowly cooked in red wine and aromatic vegetables until meltingly soft, resulting in a rich and hearty meal.
instructions: Pat the veal cheeks dry and season them with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the veal cheeks on all sides until deeply golden, then remove and set aside. | In the same pot, add chopped onion, carrot, and celery, and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Pour in red wine to deglaze the pan, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom. | Add crushed tomato, beef broth, bay leaf, thyme sprig, and rosemary sprig to the pot and stir to combine. | Return the browned veal cheeks to the pot, ensuring they are mostly submerged in the liquid. | Bring to a simmer, then cover and transfer the pot to a preheated oven at 160°C (320°F). | Braise the veal cheeks for about 3 hours, or until very tender and falling apart. | Remove the veal cheeks from the pot and keep warm. | Strain the cooking liquid and return it to the pot, then reduce it over medium heat to a sauce consistency. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. | Serve the veal cheeks drizzled with the reduced sauce.

name: Braised Veal Shank
description: Braised Veal Shank is a classic Spanish dish where the veal shank is slowly cooked with vegetables, white wine, and herbs until tender and flavorful, creating a rich and comforting meal.
instructions: Season the veal shank with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat and brown the veal shank on all sides. Remove and set aside. | In the same pot, add chopped onion, carrot, and celery, and cook until softened. | Add minced garlic and tomato paste, cooking for another minute. | Pour in white wine to deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. | Add beef broth, bay leaf, and thyme, then return the veal shank to the pot. | Bring to a simmer, then cover and reduce heat to low. Cook gently for about 3 hours or until the meat is tender and falling off the bone. | Remove the veal shank from the pot and keep warm. | Strain the cooking liquid, discard solids, and reduce the liquid over medium heat to thicken into a sauce. | Serve the veal shank with the reduced sauce poured over.

name: Brazo De Gitano
description: Brazo de Gitano is a traditional Spanish rolled sponge cake filled with whipped cream and optionally jam or fruit, known for its light texture and sweet flavor.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180C (350F). | In a clean bowl, beat egg yolks with sugar until pale and creamy. | In a separate bowl, whisk egg whites until stiff peaks form. | Gently fold the egg whites into the yolk mixture, taking care not to deflate the batter. | Sift the flour over the mixture and lightly fold it in until just combined. | Line a large baking tray with parchment paper and pour the batter evenly onto the tray, spreading it out smoothly. | Bake the sponge in the preheated oven for about 10-12 minutes or until golden and springy to the touch. | Remove the sponge from the oven and turn it out onto a clean kitchen towel dusted with sugar. | Peel off the parchment paper carefully, then roll the sponge up with the towel from one short end, and let it cool completely in the rolled shape. | For the filling, beat the heavy cream with sugar until stiff peaks form. | Unroll the cooled sponge carefully and spread the whipped cream evenly over the surface. | Optionally, add a layer of jam or fruit slices over the cream. | Roll the sponge back up tightly without the towel, forming the roll cake. | Chill the roll in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour before serving. | Dust with powdered sugar before slicing and serving.

name: Gai Yang
description: Gai Yang is a traditional Isan-style Thai grilled chicken marinated with fragrant herbs and spices, known for its juicy texture and smoky flavor.
instructions: Make a marinade by combining garlic, cilantro root, coriander seed, white pepper, fish sauce, soy sauce, palm sugar, and lime juice in a blender or mortar and pestle until smooth. | Clean the whole chicken and butterflied it by removing the backbone and flattening it for even grilling. | Rub the marinade all over the chicken, ensuring it is well coated and marinate for at least 1 hour, preferably overnight, in the refrigerator. | Preheat the charcoal grill or gas grill to medium-high heat. | Grill the marinated chicken skin-side down first, basting occasionally with the leftover marinade, and cook until the skin is crispy and chicken is cooked through, about 20-30 minutes, flipping occasionally to avoid burning. | Remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for a few minutes before cutting into pieces. | Serve the grilled chicken with sticky rice and a spicy dipping sauce made from fish sauce, lime juice, chili flakes, and sugar if desired.

name: Gai Yang
description: Gai Yang is a traditional Thai marinated whole grilled chicken known for its flavorful, aromatic, and juicy meat with a crispy skin, typically served with sticky rice and spicy dipping sauce.
instructions: Prepare the marinade by combining chopped garlic, chopped cilantro root, chopped coriander stems, white pepper, fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, oyster sauce, and vegetable oil in a bowl. | Clean the whole chicken and pat it dry with paper towels. | Place the chicken in a large bowl or bag and pour the marinade over it, rubbing the marinade inside and outside the chicken thoroughly. | Cover and refrigerate the chicken for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, to allow the flavors to infuse. | Preheat the grill to medium-high heat. | Thread the chicken onto a rotisserie spit or place it on the grill rack. | Grill the chicken, turning occasionally, for about 45-60 minutes or until the skin is crispy and the internal temperature reaches 75°C (165°F). | Baste the chicken occasionally with leftover marinade or vegetable oil to keep it moist. | Remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for 10 minutes before carving. | Serve the gai yang with sticky rice and a spicy dipping sauce such as nam jim jaew.

name: Gai Yang Isan
description: Gai Yang Isan is a traditional Thai grilled chicken dish from the Isan region, featuring marinated chicken grilled until smoky and juicy, typically served with sticky rice and spicy dipping sauce.
instructions: Clean the whole chicken and cut it into halves, spreading it flat like a butterfly. | In a bowl, combine garlic, coriander root, white pepper, fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, lemongrass, and ground roasted rice to make the marinade. | Marinate the chicken pieces thoroughly with the marinade mixture. Let it sit for at least 1 hour, preferably overnight, in the refrigerator. | Prepare the grill to medium-high heat using charcoal for authentic flavor, or a gas grill if preferred. | Grill the chicken skin-side down first, basting occasionally with leftover marinade or a little oil to keep it moist. | Turn the chicken frequently to ensure even cooking and prevent burning, grilling until the skin is golden brown and the meat is cooked through, about 25-30 minutes. | Remove the grilled chicken from the grill and let it rest for a few minutes before cutting. | Cut the chicken into serving pieces and serve hot with sticky rice, a spicy dipping sauce (nam jim jaew), and fresh vegetables such as cucumber and cabbage.

name: Ginger Tea Nam Khing
description: Ginger Tea Nam Khing is a traditional Burmese hot beverage made from fresh ginger and palm sugar, known for its warming and soothing properties.
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the fresh ginger. | In a saucepan, add the sliced ginger and water. | Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat and let it simmer for about 10 minutes to extract the ginger flavor. | Add palm sugar and stir until it dissolves completely. | Strain the tea into cups to remove the ginger slices. | Serve the ginger tea hot, optionally garnished with fresh ginger slices or a squeeze of lime if desired.

name: Goong Mae Nam Pao
description: Goong Mae Nam Pao is a popular Thai dish of grilled giant river prawns marinated with traditional herbs and spices, known for its smoky flavor and juicy meat.
instructions: Clean the river prawns thoroughly, removing any dirt and brushing them gently under cold water. | Preheat a charcoal grill or barbecue to medium-high heat. | In a bowl, mix garlic, coriander root, cilantro, fish sauce, palm sugar, and white pepper to create a marinade. | Brush the marinade generously over each river prawn, making sure to coat both sides. | Place the prawns on the hot grill shell side down and cook for about 5-7 minutes until the shells turn bright red and the meat is opaque and slightly charred. | Flip the prawns and grill the other side for an additional 2-3 minutes, basting with remaining marinade to enhance flavor. | Remove the prawns from the grill and sprinkle chopped cilantro leaves on top as garnish. | Serve immediately with a side of spicy seafood dipping sauce made from chopped chili, lime juice, fish sauce, garlic, and sugar.

name: Goong Ob Mor Din
description: Goong Ob Mor Din is a traditional Thai claypot dish featuring succulent shrimp and vermicelli noodles baked with a savory sauce made from oyster and soy sauces, delivering rich umami flavors.
instructions: Rinse the shrimp and set aside to drain. | Soak the vermicelli noodle in warm water for about 10 minutes until softened, then drain. | In a bowl, mix the oyster sauce, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, and white pepper to prepare the sauce. | Heat a claypot or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat and add vegetable oil. | Add minced garlic to the pot and sauté until fragrant but not browned. | Add the shrimp to the pot and stir-fry briefly until they start to turn pink. | Add the soaked vermicelli noodles on top of the shrimp evenly. | Pour the prepared sauce mixture over the noodles and shrimp. | Add chopped spring onion and coriander leaves over the top. | Cover the pot with a lid and reduce heat to low, allowing the dish to steam and cook for about 10-15 minutes until the shrimp are fully cooked and the noodles have absorbed the flavors. | Once done, remove from heat and serve hot directly from the claypot, optionally with chili sauce on the side.

name: Goong Ob Wun Sen
description: Goong Ob Wun Sen is a traditional Thai shrimp glass noodle bake cooked in a clay pot that features tender glass noodles mixed with shrimp, Chinese sausage, and flavorful seasonings, resulting in a fragrant and savory dish.
instructions: Soak glass noodle in warm water for about 10 minutes until soft, then drain and set aside. | Heat a wok or large pan over medium heat and add vegetable oil. | Add chopped garlic and minced shallot to the pan and stir-fry until fragrant and translucent. | Add shrimp to the pan and cook until they turn pink and are nearly cooked through. | Add Chinese sausage slices and continue to stir-fry for a minute. | Add sliced shiitake mushrooms and stir-fry gently. | Add soaked glass noodles to the pan along with oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, and white pepper. Mix well to coat noodles and ingredients with the sauce. | Add chicken broth to the pan and stir to combine everything. | Transfer the mixture to a heatproof clay pot or baking dish. | Cover the clay pot or dish with a lid or aluminum foil. | Steam or bake the dish at medium heat for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the noodles to absorb the sauce. | Garnish with chopped coriander, scallion, and fried garlic before serving hot.

name: Goong Pad Kratiam
description: Goong Pad Kratiam is a classic Thai stir-fry featuring shrimp cooked with fragrant garlic and pepper, creating a simple yet flavorful dish.
instructions: Clean and devein the shrimp, then pat dry with paper towels. | Peel and finely chop the garlic cloves. | Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large pan over medium-high heat. | Add the chopped garlic to the hot oil and stir-fry until fragrant and lightly golden. | Add the shrimp to the wok and stir-fry until they turn pink and are nearly cooked through. | Sprinkle ground white pepper over the shrimp and garlic, stirring well to coat evenly. | Add soy sauce and oyster sauce to the wok, mixing everything together for another minute. | Add chopped scallion whites and a pinch of sugar, stir-fry briefly to combine all flavors. | Remove from heat and garnish with chopped scallion greens before serving.

name: Goong Pad Pong Kari
description: Goong Pad Pong Kari is a popular Thai stir-fry dish featuring shrimp cooked in a creamy, fragrant yellow curry powder sauce, combining savory, sweet, and aromatic flavors.
instructions: Peel and devein the shrimp, leaving the tails on if desired, then rinse and drain them. | Cut the onion into thin slices and roughly chop the green onion and celery leaves. | Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat. | Add the minced garlic and sliced onion to the wok and stir-fry until fragrant and translucent. | Add the yellow curry powder to the wok and stir quickly for about 30 seconds to release the aroma. | Add the shrimp to the wok and stir-fry until they start to turn pink. | Pour in the evaporated milk and stir to combine all ingredients well. | Add the chopped celery leaves and green onion, then season with fish sauce, sugar, and white pepper to taste. | Continue to stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes until the shrimp are fully cooked and the sauce has slightly thickened. | Remove from heat and transfer to a serving plate. | Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Goong Pad Prik Sod
description: Goong Pad Prik Sod is a classic Thai stir-fry dish featuring fresh shrimp cooked with spicy fresh chili and garlic, delivering bold and vibrant flavors.
instructions: Peel and devein the shrimp, rinse under cold water, and pat dry with paper towels. | Slice the fresh chilies thinly, remove seeds if less heat is desired, and set aside. | Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat until hot. | Add the minced garlic and sliced fresh chilies to the hot oil, stir-fry briefly until fragrant, about 30 seconds. | Add the shrimp to the wok and stir-fry continuously until they turn pink and are cooked through, about 2-3 minutes. | Add fish sauce and a pinch of sugar to the wok, stirring well to coat the shrimp evenly with the sauce and chilies. | Taste and adjust seasoning by adding more fish sauce or a pinch of sugar as desired. | Remove from heat, transfer to a serving plate, and garnish with fresh basil leaves if available. | Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Blue Cheese Pastry
description: Blue Cheese Pastry, known as Kuflu Peynirli Borek, is a savory Turkish pastry filled with a flavorful mix of blue cheese, feta, and parsley, wrapped in crisp phyllo dough and baked to golden perfection.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). | In a bowl, crumble the blue cheese and mix it with the crumbled feta cheese and chopped parsley. | Lay out one sheet of phyllo pastry on a clean surface and brush it lightly with melted butter. | Place another sheet on top and brush with butter again. | Cut the layered phyllo sheets into strips about 5 cm wide. | Place a spoonful of the cheese mixture at one end of each strip. | Roll the phyllo strip over the filling to form a cylinder or roll shape. | Arrange the rolls seam side down on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. | Brush the tops with melted butter to give a golden finish. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 20-25 minutes or until the pastry is golden and crisp. | Remove from oven and let cool slightly before serving.

name: Bobrek Sis
description: Bobrek Sis is a traditional Turkish shish kebab made with marinated kidney pieces, grilled to perfection and served with fresh herbs and lemon. This flavorful dish highlights the unique taste and texture of kidneys in a simple and satisfying way.
instructions: Clean the kidneys by removing any membranes and fat. Cut them into bite-sized cubes and soak in cold water with a splash of vinegar for 30 minutes to remove any strong odors, then drain and pat dry. | Marinate the kidney pieces with olive oil, minced garlic, ground cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper. Let it rest for at least 1 hour in the refrigerator. | Thread the kidney pieces onto wooden or metal skewers, alternating with slices of onion, and bell pepper if desired. | Preheat the grill to medium-high heat. Grill the skewers for about 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until the kidneys are cooked through and slightly charred on the edges. | Serve the kidney shish kebabs hot with fresh parsley, lemon wedges, and warm pita bread or rice.

name: Bodrum Zucchini Flower Stuffed
description: Bodrum Zucchini Flower Stuffed (Bodrum Kabak Çiçeği Dolmasi) is a traditional Turkish dish featuring tender zucchini flowers filled with a flavorful rice and herb mixture, then gently cooked to perfection. This dish originates from the Bodrum region and is a delightful vegetarian specialty.
instructions: Rinse the zucchini flowers gently to remove any dirt and drain them well. | Prepare the filling by mixing rice, finely chopped onion, chopped dill, chopped mint, chopped parsley, olive oil, salt, and black pepper in a bowl. | Carefully open each zucchini flower and fill it with the rice mixture using a small spoon, being careful not to overfill. | Fold the petals of each flower to enclose the filling without tearing. | Arrange the stuffed zucchini flowers snugly in a deep pot, placing a few mint leaves or herb sprigs on top for aroma. | Drizzle olive oil over the flowers and sprinkle with salt. | Pour water over the flowers until just covering them, then place a heat-resistant plate on top to keep the flowers from moving during cooking. | Cover the pot with a lid and cook on low heat for about 30-40 minutes, until the rice is cooked and the flowers are tender. | Remove from heat and let it rest for 10 minutes before serving. | Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally with a side of yogurt.

name: Boiled Egg Breakfast
description: A simple traditional boiled egg breakfast, commonly served in Turkey, featuring perfectly cooked eggs that can be enjoyed warm or cold with optional seasoning.
instructions: Place eggs in a single layer in a saucepan and cover them with cold water by about an inch. | Bring water to a rolling boil on high heat. | Once boiling, cover the saucepan with a lid and remove it from heat. | Let the eggs sit in hot water for about 10-12 minutes for hard-boiled eggs. | Drain the hot water and run cold water over the eggs to cool them and stop cooking. | Peel the eggs by gently tapping them on a hard surface and removing the shell. | Serve the boiled eggs warm or cold, seasoned with salt and pepper as desired.

name: Bolu Abant Lake Trout Dish
description: Bolu Abant Lake Trout is a traditional Turkish dish featuring fresh lake trout pan-fried to perfection and served with a flavorful garlic-lemon parsley sauce, highlighting the fresh flavors of the fish.
instructions: Clean and scale the lake trout thoroughly, then pat dry with paper towels. | Season the trout inside and out with salt, black pepper, and a pinch of dried oregano. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat until hot. | Add the trout to the skillet and cook for about 5-7 minutes on each side until the skin is crispy and the flesh is opaque and flakes easily with a fork. | Remove the fish from the skillet and keep warm. | In the same skillet, add butter and allow it to melt. | Sauté minced garlic until fragrant without browning, then add lemon juice and chopped fresh parsley, stirring to mix. | Pour the garlic-lemon sauce over the cooked trout. | Serve the trout garnished with additional fresh parsley and lemon wedges on the side.

name: Bolu Lake Fish Specialty
description: This Bolu Lake Fish Specialty is a traditional Turkish dish featuring fresh lake fish pan-fried with onions, garlic, and fresh herbs, offering a simple yet flavorful taste of Bolu cuisine.
instructions: Clean and scale the lake fish thoroughly under cold running water. | Pat the fish dry with paper towels and season the inside and outside with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. | Add finely chopped onion and sauté until translucent. | Add minced garlic and cook for one minute until fragrant. | Place the fish in the pan and cook for about 5-7 minutes on each side until the skin is crispy and the flesh is cooked through. | Add lemon juice and chopped fresh parsley over the fish in the last minute of cooking. | Remove the fish from the pan and serve hot with lemon wedges and fresh parsley garnish.

name: Bolu Special Pilaf
description: Bolu Special Pilaf is a traditional Turkish dish from the Bolu region featuring rice cooked with sautéed chicken and onions, enriched with butter and chicken broth for a flavorful, hearty meal.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for 30 minutes and drain. | Heat butter in a large pan over medium heat and sauté the chopped onions until translucent. | Add the diced chicken pieces and cook until they are browned on all sides. | Add the drained rice to the pan and sauté gently with the chicken and onions for a few minutes to coat the rice with butter and flavors. | Pour in the hot chicken broth, add the salt and pepper, and bring the mixture to a boil. | Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan with a lid, and simmer gently for about 20 minutes or until the rice is tender and all the liquid is absorbed. | Turn off the heat and let the pilaf rest covered for 10 minutes to let the flavors meld and the steam finish cooking the rice. | Garnish with chopped parsley before serving.

name: Borani Spinach Yogurt Meat Stew
description: Borani Spinach Yogurt Meat Stew is a traditional Persian dish featuring tender lamb cooked with spinach and a creamy yogurt sauce, offering a comforting and flavorful meal.
instructions: Soak 200 g of lamb meat cubes in water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat dry. | Heat 2 tbsp of vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat, then add 1 chopped onion and sauté until translucent. | Add 3 cloves of minced garlic, 1 tsp of ground cumin, 1 tsp of paprika, 1 tsp of ground coriander, and 1 tsp of salt; cook for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. | Add the lamb meat cubes and brown them on all sides for about 5-7 minutes. | Pour in 500 ml of water and bring to a boil; then reduce heat to low and simmer covered for 45 minutes until the meat is tender. | While the meat simmers, rinse and chop 300 g of fresh spinach leaves. | In a separate bowl, whisk 500 g of plain yogurt until smooth. | Once the meat is tender, add the chopped spinach to the pot and cook for 5 minutes until wilted. | Remove the pot from heat and gradually stir in the whisked yogurt, mixing well to combine and prevent curdling. | Return the pot to low heat and cook gently for another 5-7 minutes without boiling, stirring occasionally. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve hot, garnished with a sprig of fresh mint or parsley if desired.

name: Borek
description: Borek is a traditional Turkish savory pastry made with phyllo dough and filled with a cheesy herb mixture, perfect for a flavorful breakfast.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | In a bowl, crumble the feta cheese and mix it with the chopped parsley and one beaten egg until well combined. | Lay one sheet of phyllo dough on a clean surface and brush it lightly with melted butter. | Place another sheet of phyllo on top and brush with butter again. | Cut the phyllo stack into strips about 5 cm wide. | Place a spoonful of the cheese mixture at one end of each strip. | Fold the strip over to form a triangle shape, continuing to fold along the strip until completely rolled up. | Place the rolled borek pastries on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. | Brush the tops with the remaining beaten egg for a golden finish. | Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes, or until golden brown and crisp. | Remove from oven and let cool slightly before serving.

name: Borek Cesitleri
description: Borek Cesitleri is a traditional Turkish mixed pastry platter featuring a variety of filled pastries such as spinach and feta, minced meat, and potato borek, commonly served warm as a popular appetizer or main dish.
instructions: Prepare the dough by combining flour, water, salt, and olive oil to form a smooth and elastic dough. Let it rest covered for about 30 minutes. | Divide the dough into equal portions and roll each portion into thin sheets on a floured surface. | For the spinach feta borek, mix chopped spinach, crumbled feta cheese, finely chopped onion, salt, and pepper. | For the minced meat borek, sauté minced beef with onion, salt, pepper, and spices until cooked and cooled. | For the potato borek, boil and mash potatoes, season with salt, pepper, and chopped parsley. | Place filling on one edge of each dough sheet and roll or fold into desired shapes like spirals, triangles, or cigar shapes. | Brush each pastry with beaten egg or olive oil to help browning. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan for frying or preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) for baking. | Fry the pastries until golden brown on all sides or bake on a parchment-lined tray until golden and crisp, about 20-30 minutes. | Drain fried pastries on paper towels to remove excess oil before serving. | Arrange a variety of borek on a platter and serve warm, often accompanied by yogurt or ayran (a yogurt drink).

name: Caramelized Onions
description: Caramelized onions are slowly cooked to develop a rich, sweet flavor and deep color, perfect as a flavorful addition to many dishes.
instructions: Peel the onions and cut them into thin, even slices. | Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat until melted and combined. | Add the sliced onions to the skillet and stir to coat them evenly with the oil and butter. | Cook the onions slowly, stirring occasionally, allowing them to soften and become translucent over about 10 minutes. | Reduce the heat to low and continue to cook the onions, stirring every few minutes to prevent burning. | Add a pinch of salt to help draw moisture out of the onions and enhance flavor. | Continue cooking for about 30-40 minutes, stirring frequently until the onions turn a deep golden brown and develop a sweet, caramelized flavor. | If the onions begin to stick to the pan, add a splash of water to deglaze and scrape up the browned bits. | Once the onions are richly caramelized, remove them from heat and let cool slightly. | Use immediately or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to a week.

name: Caramelized Pork Ribs
description: Caramelized Pork Ribs is a savory and sweet dish featuring tender pork ribs cooked with a caramelized glaze made from sugar and soy-based sauces, popular in various Asian cuisines.
instructions: Rinse the pork ribs and pat them dry with paper towels. | Cut the ribs into individual pieces if they are not already separated. | In a bowl, mix sugar, salt, pepper, and five-spice powder. | Rub the spice mixture evenly over the ribs and let them marinate for at least 30 minutes. | Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. | Add the ribs and sear them on all sides until browned and caramelized, about 5-7 minutes. | Add minced garlic and sliced ginger, stir-frying briefly until fragrant. | Pour in soy sauce, fish sauce, and water to just cover the ribs. | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer gently for 45-60 minutes, until the ribs are tender and the sauce has thickened. | Remove the lid and increase heat to medium-high to reduce the sauce, stirring occasionally until the ribs are glossy and caramelized. | Garnish with chopped scallion and serve hot with steamed rice.

name: Cardoon Gratin
description: Cardoon gratin is a traditional French dish featuring tender cardoons baked in a creamy cheese sauce, creating a rich and comforting vegetable side.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Trim the cardoons, removing outer strings and tough parts, then cut into 3-4 cm pieces. | Boil the cardoon pieces in salted water with lemon juice for about 30 minutes until tender, then drain well. | In a saucepan, melt butter and stir in flour to make a roux, cooking for a minute without browning. | Gradually whisk in milk and cream, cooking and stirring until the sauce thickens. | Add grated cheese to the sauce and season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. | Arrange the cooked cardoon pieces in a buttered baking dish and pour the cheese sauce over them. | Sprinkle additional grated cheese and breadcrumbs on top for a golden crust. | Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling. | Let cool slightly before serving.

name: Cardoons with Bone Marrow
description: A classic Italian dish celebrating the unique flavor of cardoons paired with rich, roasted bone marrow, creating a luxurious and earthy main course.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Trim the cardoons by removing the tough outer fibers and cut them into 10 cm (4 inch) pieces. | Fill a large bowl with cold water and lemon juice to prevent the cardoons from browning, then immerse the cardoon pieces in it. | Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and blanch the cardoons for about 20 minutes until tender but still firm. | Drain the cardoons and pat them dry with a kitchen towel. | Place the bone marrow bones on a baking tray and roast them in the oven for about 15 minutes until the marrow is soft and slightly browned. | In a large skillet, heat some olive oil over medium heat and sauté minced garlic and chopped parsley until fragrant. | Add the blanched cardoons to the skillet and sauté gently for 5 minutes, seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. | Spoon the softened bone marrow out of the bones and mix it into the cardoons in the skillet, coating them well. | Serve the cardoons topped with the reserved marrow and a sprinkle of fresh parsley. | Optionally, serve with toasted rustic bread to scoop up the marrow and cardoon mixture.

name: Carnival Doughnuts
description: Carnival doughnuts are classic deep-fried sweet treats, fluffy and dusted with sugar, popular at fairs and carnivals.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon and whisk together. | In a separate bowl, beat the eggs. | Add milk and vanilla extract to the eggs and mix well. | Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined; do not overmix to keep the batter light. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or large heavy pot to 180°C (350°F). | Using two spoons, drop small spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil, being careful not to overcrowd the pan. | Fry the doughnuts for about 2 to 3 minutes on each side, until golden brown and puffed up. | Remove the doughnuts with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. | While still warm, dust the doughnuts generously with powdered sugar. | Serve warm for the best taste.

name: Carnival Fritters
description: Carnival fritters called Bugnes are a traditional French fried pastry, light and crispy, often enjoyed during the carnival season dusted with powdered sugar.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, sugar, salt, and baking powder and mix well. | Make a well in the center and add eggs, melted butter, milk, and a splash of rum (optional). | Mix everything together until a smooth dough forms. | Turn the dough onto a floured surface and knead for about 5 minutes until elastic. | Cover the dough with a cloth and let it rest for 1 hour at room temperature. | Roll out the dough thinly to about 2-3 mm thickness. | Cut the dough into diamond shapes or rectangles and make a small slit in the center of each piece. | Thread one end of the dough through the slit to create a twisted shape. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or fryer to 175°C (350°F). | Fry the bugnes in batches until golden brown and puffed, about 2-3 minutes per side. | Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. | Once cool, dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.

name: Carpentras Berlingot Candy
description: Carpentras Berlingot is a traditional French hard candy known for its bright colors and diamond shape, made by boiling sugar syrup and pulling it to achieve a glossy texture.
instructions: In a heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine sugar, water, and glucose syrup over medium heat. | Stir gently until the sugar dissolves completely and the mixture begins to boil. | Attach a candy thermometer to the saucepan and continue boiling without stirring until the mixture reaches 150°C (hard crack stage). | Remove the pan from heat and carefully stir in the white vinegar and any desired flavoring or food coloring. | Pour the hot syrup onto a greased marble slab or a silicone mat and allow it to cool slightly until it is cool enough to handle but still pliable. | Once cool enough, begin pulling the candy by stretching and folding it repeatedly to incorporate air, which gives it a glossy appearance and a lighter color. | Shape the pulled candy into a long rope, then cut it into small diamond-shaped pieces using scissors or a knife. | Wrap individual pieces in wax paper or cellophane to prevent sticking and preserve freshness.

name: Carrot Flan
description: Carrot Flan is a smooth and creamy French-style savory custard made with pureed carrots, eggs, and cream, baked to tender perfection. It makes a delightful and elegant starter or side dish.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Peel and chop the carrot into small pieces. | Steam the chopped carrot until very tender, about 15 minutes. | In a blender, combine the steamed carrot, eggs, heavy cream, salt, pepper, and grated nutmeg, then blend until smooth and creamy. | Grease individual ramekins or a baking dish with butter. | Pour the carrot mixture into the prepared ramekins or dish. | Place the ramekins or dish in a water bath by putting them in a larger baking pan filled halfway with hot water. | Bake in the preheated oven for 30-40 minutes, or until the flan is set and a knife inserted comes out clean. | Remove from the oven and let cool slightly before unmolding or serving. | Serve warm or at room temperature, optionally garnished with chopped parsley.

name: Carrot Puree
description: Carrot puree is a smooth and creamy side dish made from cooked carrots blended into a velvety texture, perfect to accompany main courses or as a baby food.
instructions: Peel the carrots and cut them into evenly sized pieces for uniform cooking. | Place the carrots in a pot and cover with water, add a pinch of salt to the water. | Bring the water to a boil and cook the carrots until they are very tender, about 15-20 minutes. | Drain the carrots and transfer them to a blender or food processor. | Add butter, salt, and pepper to the carrots. | Blend until smooth and creamy, adding a little water or cream to reach desired consistency if needed. | Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary. | Serve warm as a side dish or base for other dishes.

name: Cassoulet
description: Cassoulet is a traditional French hearty casserole made with white beans, pork, sausage, and duck confit, slow-cooked to develop rich flavors and a crispy top.
instructions: Soak the dried white beans in cold water overnight, then drain and rinse them. | In a large pot, cover the beans with fresh water, add a pinch of salt and a sprig of thyme, and simmer gently for about 1 hour until tender. Drain and set aside, reserving some cooking liquid. | In a heavy casserole or Dutch oven, heat olive oil and brown the pork shoulder pieces until golden. Remove and set aside. | In the same pot, brown the sausages and duck confit pieces until well colored. Remove and set aside with the pork. | Add chopped onion, carrot, and garlic to the pot and cook until softened. | Return the meats to the pot and add the cooked beans, crushed tomatoes, duck stock or broth, bay leaf, parsley, and chopped garlic. | Season with salt and black pepper to taste. | Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook in a low oven (around 160°C / 320°F) for 2 to 3 hours, adding reserved bean cooking liquid if the mixture becomes too dry. | Towards the end of cooking, remove the lid to allow the cassoulet to brown and develop a crust on top, occasionally pushing the crust down into the stew to blend flavors. | Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley. | Enjoy your rich and hearty cassoulet!

name: Chicken Phyllo Pie
description: Kotopita is a traditional Greek savory pie made with shredded chicken and feta cheese wrapped in crispy phyllo dough, offering a flavorful and satisfying meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees Celsius (350 degrees Fahrenheit). | In a large pan, heat olive oil over medium heat and sauté the chopped onion until translucent. | Add minced garlic and cook briefly until fragrant. | Add the shredded cooked chicken to the pan and stir to combine. | Season with salt, pepper, and dried oregano, and cook for a few more minutes to blend the flavors. | Remove from heat and stir in crumbled feta cheese and chopped fresh parsley. | Prepare the phyllo dough by layering sheets in a greased baking dish, brushing each sheet lightly with olive oil before adding the next. | Spread the chicken mixture evenly over the layered phyllo sheets. | Cover the filling with additional phyllo sheets, again brushing each sheet with olive oil. | Tuck in the edges of the phyllo and brush the top layer generously with olive oil to achieve a golden crust. | Bake in the preheated oven for approximately 45 minutes or until the phyllo is crisp and golden brown. | Allow to cool slightly before slicing and serving.

name: Chicken Souvlaki
description: Chicken Souvlaki is a traditional Greek dish featuring grilled marinated chicken skewers, known for its vibrant flavors from lemon, garlic, and oregano. It's simple to prepare and perfect for a flavorful meal.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and place in a bowl. | In a separate bowl, mix olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper to create the marinade. | Pour the marinade over the chicken pieces and toss to coat evenly. | Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, preferably overnight, to marinate. | If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 30 minutes to prevent burning. | Thread the marinated chicken pieces onto the skewers. | Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. | Cook the chicken skewers for about 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until fully cooked and slightly charred. | Remove from grill and let rest for a few minutes. | Serve hot with pita bread, tzatziki sauce, sliced onions, and tomato if desired.

name: Chicken Souvlaki Pita Wrap
description: Chicken Souvlaki Pita Wrap is a traditional Greek dish featuring marinated grilled chicken served inside warm pita bread with fresh vegetables and creamy tzatziki sauce.
instructions: In a bowl, combine olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, dried oregano, salt, and pepper to create the marinade. | Cut chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and add to the marinade. Mix well to coat and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. | Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. | Thread the marinated chicken pieces onto skewers. | Grill chicken skewers for about 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked through and slightly charred. | Warm pita bread on the grill or in a pan until soft and pliable. | Prepare tzatziki sauce by mixing Greek yogurt, grated cucumber, minced garlic, lemon juice, chopped dill, salt, and pepper in a bowl. | To assemble, spread tzatziki sauce on the warm pita, add grilled chicken pieces, sliced tomato, sliced red onion, and chopped lettuce. | Fold the pita wrap around the fillings and serve immediately.

name: Chicken Souvlaki Platter
description: Chicken Souvlaki Platter is a traditional Greek dish featuring marinated grilled chicken skewers served with pita bread and fresh vegetables, accompanied by creamy tzatziki sauce. It's a flavorful and healthy Mediterranean meal.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into bite-sized cubes and place in a bowl. | In a separate bowl, combine olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper to make the marinade. | Pour the marinade over the chicken cubes and mix well to coat all pieces. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, preferably 4 hours. | Preheat the grill or grill pan to medium-high heat. | Thread the marinated chicken cubes onto skewers, leaving some space between pieces for even cooking. | Grill the chicken skewers for about 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked through and lightly charred. | Warm the pita bread on the grill for about 1 minute on each side. | To assemble the platter, place grilled chicken skewers on a plate with warmed pita bread. | Serve with slices of cucumber, tomato, red onion, and a dollop of tzatziki sauce on the side. | Garnish with fresh parsley and lemon wedges for extra flavor if desired.

name: Chicken Stifado
description: Chicken Stifado is a traditional Greek stew featuring tender chicken simmered with pearl onions, aromatic spices, and red wine, resulting in a rich and flavorful dish.
instructions: Peel the small onions and parboil them in boiling water for about 5 minutes to soften, then drain. | Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and brown the chicken pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside. | In the same pot, add the drained onions and sauté until they begin to caramelize, about 10 minutes. | Add garlic and cook for an additional minute until fragrant. | Return the chicken to the pot and stir in the tomato paste, cinnamon stick, bay leaf, whole cloves, vinegar, red wine, and beef broth. | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 1 hour, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thickened. | Season with salt and pepper to taste, and remove the cinnamon stick, bay leaf, and cloves before serving. | Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and serve hot with crusty bread or rice.

name: Chicken Stuffed with Feta
description: Chicken breasts stuffed with a flavorful mixture of feta cheese and fresh herbs, lightly seared and baked to perfection, a traditional Greek-inspired dish.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Lay the chicken breasts flat and make a deep pocket in each for stuffing. | In a bowl, mix crumbled feta cheese, chopped fresh oregano, chopped fresh parsley, minced garlic, lemon zest, and a pinch of black pepper. | Stuff the chicken breasts with the feta mixture and secure with toothpicks if needed. | Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and sear the chicken breasts on both sides until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes per side. | Place the seared chicken breasts in a baking dish and drizzle with a little more olive oil and lemon juice. | Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and juices run clear. | Remove from oven and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Chicken Thighs with Kalamata Olives
description: A savory Mediterranean dish featuring tender baked chicken thighs with briny Kalamata olives, garlic, and herbs for a flavorful and rustic meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Heat olive oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium heat. | Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper, then brown them skin-side down in the skillet until golden, about 5 minutes. | Turn chicken and cook for another 3 minutes, then remove from heat. | Add chopped garlic, sliced onion, and chopped tomato to the skillet, sauté for 2-3 minutes until softened. | Stir in Kalamata olives and sprinkle dried oregano over the mixture. | Return the chicken thighs to the skillet, skin-side up, nestled among the olive mixture. | Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake for 20-25 minutes, until chicken is cooked through and juices run clear. | Remove from oven and garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

name: Chicken Wrapped in Vine Leaves
description: Chicken Wrapped in Vine Leaves features tender chicken breasts seasoned and encased in softened vine leaves, a method offering a flavorful and aromatic dish often enjoyed in Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisines.
instructions: Soak vine leaves in warm water for about 20 minutes to soften, then drain and pat dry. | Season chicken breasts with salt, pepper, and any preferred herbs such as dried oregano or thyme. | Place a vine leaf flat on a clean surface and put a seasoned chicken breast in the center. | Wrap the vine leaf tightly around the chicken, folding in the sides to secure the filling. | Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and carefully place the wrapped chicken seam side down. | Cook for 4-5 minutes on each side until the vine leaves are slightly browned and the chicken is nearly cooked through. | Transfer the wrapped chicken to a baking dish, add a splash of chicken broth, and cover loosely with foil. | Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 15-20 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked and tender. | Remove from oven and let rest for a few minutes before unwrapping. | Serve warm, optionally garnished with fresh parsley or lemon wedges.

name: Chicken and Chickpea Stew
description: A flavorful and hearty stew combining tender chicken with protein-rich chickpeas and aromatic spices for a satisfying meal.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. | Add chopped onion, minced garlic, and chopped carrot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. | Add diced chicken breast and cook until lightly browned on all sides. | Stir in ground cumin, smoked paprika, ground coriander, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute to release the spices' aroma. | Pour in chicken broth and bring to a boil. | Add chickpeas and diced tomatoes to the pot. | Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes until chicken is cooked through and flavors meld. | Season with salt and black pepper to taste. | Stir in chopped fresh cilantro before serving.

name: Chicken and Halloumi Skewers
description: Chicken and Halloumi Skewers are a flavorful and easy-to-make grilled dish combining tender marinated chicken with salty, grilled halloumi cheese. Perfect for a quick and satisfying meal with Mediterranean flair.
instructions: Cut the chicken breast into bite-sized cubes and cube the halloumi cheese in similar size. | In a bowl, mix olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, chopped parsley, salt, and black pepper to make a marinade. | Add the chicken pieces to the marinade and let them marinate for at least 30 minutes in the refrigerator. | Preheat the grill to medium-high heat. | Thread the marinated chicken and halloumi cubes alternately onto skewers. | Place the skewers on the grill and cook for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally until the chicken is cooked through and halloumi is golden and slightly charred. | Remove the skewers from the grill and garnish with additional fresh parsley if desired. | Serve warm with a side salad or flatbread.

name: Cappuccino
description: Cappuccino is an Italian coffee drink composed of a single shot of espresso and hot milk, topped with steamed milk foam, known for its rich and creamy texture.
instructions: Heat the milk in a saucepan or steam it using an espresso machine until it is hot and frothy. | Brew a shot of espresso using an espresso machine. | Pour the brewed espresso into a cup. | Gently pour the steamed milk over the espresso, holding back the foam with a spoon. | Spoon the milk foam on top to create a thick layer. | Optionally, sprinkle a pinch of cocoa powder or cinnamon on top for garnish.

name: Caprese Salad
description: Caprese Salad is a simple and fresh Italian salad featuring tomato, Mozzarella, and basil, dressed with olive oil and seasoned with salt and pepper.
instructions: Slice the tomato and Mozzarella cheese into even slices. | Arrange the tomato and Mozzarella slices alternately on a serving plate. | Place fresh basil leaves on top of the tomato and Mozzarella slices. | Drizzle olive oil evenly over the salad. | Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.

name: Caprese Side Salad
description: A fresh and simple Italian side salad consisting of sliced tomato, Mozzarella, and basil, dressed with olive oil and optionally balsamic vinegar, perfect for complementing main dishes.
instructions: Wash and slice the tomato into thin slices. | Slice the Mozzarella cheese into pieces similar in size to the tomato slices. | Arrange the tomato and Mozzarella slices alternately on a plate. | Tear fresh basil leaves and sprinkle them over the arranged tomato and Mozzarella. | Drizzle olive oil evenly over the salad. | Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. | Optionally, drizzle a small amount of balsamic vinegar or glaze over the salad before serving.

name: Caprese Skewers
description: Caprese skewers are a simple and fresh Italian appetizer featuring cherry tomatoes, Mozzarella, and basil on a skewer, drizzled with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
instructions: Wash the cherry tomatoes and fresh basil leaves thoroughly. | Drain the Mozzarella balls from their liquid and pat them dry. | Take small skewers or toothpicks and thread a cherry tomato, followed by a fresh basil leaf, and then a Mozzarella ball. | Repeat the layering if the skewer is long enough, ending with a tomato or Mozzarella ball. | Arrange the skewers on a serving platter. | Drizzle olive oil and balsamic vinegar over the assembled skewers. | Sprinkle with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. | Serve immediately or refrigerate until ready to serve.

name: Capricciosa Pizza
description: Capricciosa pizza is a classic Italian pizza featuring a tomato sauce base topped with Mozzarella, ham, artichokes, mushrooms, and black olives, finished with oregano and fresh basil for aromatic flavor.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 250°C (480°F) and prepare a pizza stone or baking tray. | Roll out the pizza dough on a floured surface to about 12 inches (30 cm) in diameter. | Spread the tomato sauce evenly over the rolled dough, leaving a small border around the edges. | Distribute the sliced Mozzarella cheese evenly over the tomato sauce. | Add sliced cooked ham, artichoke hearts (drained and quartered), sliced mushrooms, and black olives evenly on top of the cheese. | Drizzle a small amount of olive oil over the toppings and sprinkle with oregano. | Bake the pizza in the preheated oven for about 10-12 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbly. | Remove the pizza from the oven, let it cool slightly, then garnish with fresh basil leaves before slicing and serving.

name: Carbonara Sauce
description: Carbonara sauce is a classic Italian pasta sauce originating from Rome, made with eggs, cheese, cured pork, and black pepper to create a rich, creamy texture without cream.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta until al dente, reserving some pasta water before draining. | While pasta cooks, whisk together egg yolk, whole egg, grated Pecorino Romano cheese, and a generous amount of freshly ground black pepper in a bowl until smooth. | In a large skillet, cook diced guanciale over medium heat until fat is rendered and meat is crispy; remove from heat. | Add cooked, drained pasta to the skillet with guanciale and toss to combine, allowing pasta to absorb some fat. | Remove skillet from heat and quickly pour in the egg and cheese mixture, tossing vigorously to create a creamy sauce without scrambling the eggs; use reserved pasta water as needed to loosen the sauce. | Adjust seasoning with salt and more black pepper to taste, then serve immediately with extra Pecorino Romano sprinkled on top.

name: Carpaccio Di Manzo
description: Beef Carpaccio is a classic Italian appetizer featuring paper-thin slices of raw beef tenderloin dressed simply with olive oil, lemon juice, Parmesan, and arugula. It is light and elegant, perfect for a starter.
instructions: Arrange very thin slices of raw beef evenly on a chilled large plate or platter. | Drizzle olive oil generously over the beef slices. | Squeeze fresh lemon juice evenly on top of the beef. | Sprinkle salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste over the beef. | Scatter thin shavings of Parmesan cheese over the beef slices. | Add a handful of arugula leaves on top or around the beef as garnish. | Optionally, add capers scattered on the beef for extra flavor. | Serve immediately as a cold appetizer.

name: Carrot and Ginger Soup Italian Style
description: A smooth and warming Italian-style carrot and ginger soup, blending the sweetness of carrot with the zesty freshness of ginger and fragrant basil.
instructions: Peel and chop the carrot into small pieces. | Peel and finely grate the ginger. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. | Add chopped carrot and grated ginger to the pot and sauté for 5 minutes until softened. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Pour vegetable broth into the pot and bring to a boil. | Reduce heat to low and simmer for 20 minutes until the carrots are tender. | Use an immersion blender to purée the soup until smooth. | Season with salt and pepper to taste. | Add chopped fresh basil and stir well. | Ladle the soup into bowls and garnish with a drizzle of olive oil and a fresh basil leaf if desired.

name: Carrots with Marsala
description: Carrots sautéed and glazed with sweet Marsala wine, offering a flavorful and elegant side dish popular in Italian-inspired cuisine.
instructions: Peel and slice the carrots into uniform pieces, about half an inch thick. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. | Add the sliced carrots and sauté for about 5 minutes until they start to soften. | Add butter and continue cooking the carrots until tender and lightly browned, about 8 more minutes. | Pour in Marsala wine and cook for an additional 3 to 5 minutes, allowing the wine to reduce and glaze the carrots. | Season with salt and pepper to taste. | Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving if desired.

name: Carta Di Musica
description: Carta di Musica is a traditional Italian thin and crispy flatbread, often flavored with rosemary, perfect as a delicate accompaniment to antipasti and cheese boards.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C (430°F). | In a large bowl, mix the all-purpose flour, salt, and sugar. | Add the olive oil and gradually pour in the water, mixing continuously until the dough comes together. | Knead the dough on a floured surface for about 5 minutes until smooth and elastic. | Divide the dough into small equal portions and roll each portion out very thinly into paper-thin rounds or ovals. | Place the rolled-out dough onto baking trays lined with parchment paper. | Lightly prick the surface of the dough with a fork to prevent bubbles from forming. | Brush the surface with more olive oil and sprinkle with rosemary leaves and a pinch of salt. | Bake in the preheated oven for 7 to 10 minutes, or until the flatbreads are crisp and lightly golden. | Remove from the oven and allow to cool on a wire rack. | Serve the Carta di Musica as a crispy accompaniment to antipasti, cheeses, or spreads.

name: Dry Curry
description: Dry Curry, known as Keema Curry, is a flavorful Indian dry minced meat dish enriched with aromatic spices and herbs. It's popular as a versatile main course often served with bread or rice.
instructions: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and sauté finely chopped onion until golden brown. | Add minced garlic and grated ginger, cook until fragrant. | Add ground meat and cook until browned and cooked through, breaking it apart with a spoon. | Mix in chopped green chili and cook for a minute. | Add turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and chili powder, stirring to coat the meat with spices. | Add chopped tomato and cook until the mixture dries up and oil starts to separate. | Season with salt to taste and cook for a few more minutes, stirring occasionally. | Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro before serving.

name: Ebi Chahan
description: Ebi Chahan is a Japanese-style shrimp fried rice dish that combines fluffy rice with sautéed shrimp, egg, and vegetables, seasoned simply with soy sauce for a savory and comforting meal.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then cook it and allow it to cool completely, preferably refrigerate for several hours or overnight for best texture. | Peel and devein the shrimp if not already done, then lightly season with salt and pepper. | Beat the egg in a small bowl and set aside. | Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. | Add the shrimp and stir-fry until pink and just cooked through, then remove from pan and set aside. | In the same pan, add a little more oil if needed and pour in the beaten egg, stirring gently to create soft curds, then remove and set aside with shrimp. | Add the chopped onion and garlic to the pan and stir-fry until fragrant and soft. | Add the cooked rice to the pan, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry to heat through. | Return the shrimp and scrambled egg to the pan and mix well with the rice. | Add soy sauce and salt, then stir everything thoroughly to combine and heat evenly. | Remove from heat and garnish with chopped green onion before serving.

name: Ebi Doria
description: Ebi Doria is a Japanese-style shrimp rice gratin featuring creamy béchamel sauce baked with shrimp and Mozzarella cheese, offering a comforting fusion of Western and Japanese flavors.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (392°F). | Cook rice according to package instructions and set aside. | Heat butter in a saucepan over medium heat until melted. | Add finely chopped onion and garlic, sauté until translucent and fragrant. | Add flour and stir continuously to make a roux, cook for 1-2 minutes without browning. | Gradually add milk while stirring to create a smooth béchamel sauce. | Season the sauce with salt, pepper, and grated nutmeg, then simmer until thickened. | In a separate skillet, heat olive oil and sauté shrimp until pink and cooked through, then set aside. | Combine cooked rice with béchamel sauce and half of the shredded Mozzarella cheese, mix well. | Transfer half of the rice mixture into a baking dish. | Layer the cooked shrimp evenly over the rice. | Top with the remaining rice mixture and sprinkle the rest of the Mozzarella cheese on top. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 15-20 minutes or until the top is golden brown and bubbly. | Remove from oven and let it rest for a few minutes before serving.

name: Ebi Fry
description: Ebi Fry is a Japanese dish featuring breaded and deep-fried shrimp, known for its crispy exterior and tender interior, often served with tangy tonkatsu sauce and lemon.
instructions: Peel and devein the shrimp, leaving the tail intact, and make small slits on the underside to prevent curling during frying. | Season the shrimp lightly with salt and pepper. | Set up three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten egg, and one with panko breadcrumb. | Dredge each shrimp in flour, shaking off excess, then dip into the beaten egg, and finally coat evenly with panko breadcrumb. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan to about 170°C (340°F). | Fry the shrimp in batches for 2-3 minutes or until golden brown and crispy. | Remove the shrimp from oil and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. | Serve the fried shrimp hot with tonkatsu sauce or tartar sauce and a wedge of lemon, accompanied by shredded cabbage if desired.

name: Ebi Fry Bento
description: Ebi Fry Bento is a Japanese lunch box featuring breaded and deep-fried shrimp served with steamed rice, shredded cabbage, and dipping sauce. It offers a crispy texture and savory flavor, commonly enjoyed as a quick but satisfying meal.
instructions: Peel and devein shrimp, leaving tails intact, then pat dry with paper towels. | Season shrimp lightly with salt and pepper. | Prepare a breading station with three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten egg, and one with panko breadcrumbs. | Dredge each shrimp first in flour, shaking off excess, then dip into beaten egg, and finally coat evenly with panko breadcrumbs. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan or pot to about 180°C (350°F). | Fry shrimp in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes per side. | Remove fried shrimp and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. | Cook steamed white rice until tender and portion into bento box compartment. | Prepare shredded cabbage by washing and draining well, then place beside the rice. | Add a few lemon wedges and a small container of tonkatsu sauce or tartar sauce as dipping sauce for the shrimp. | Arrange the fried shrimp neatly in the bento box, garnish with parsley if desired. | Close bento box securely and serve at room temperature or slightly warm.

name: Ebi Fry Sandwich
description: Ebi Fry Sandwich is a popular Japanese sandwich featuring crispy breaded fried shrimp, fresh lettuce, and creamy Japanese mayonnaise, sometimes enhanced with tangy Tonkatsu sauce. It's a delightful fusion of textures and flavors perfect for a satisfying meal.
