instructions: Peel and devein the shrimp, then pat them dry with paper towels. | Season the shrimp lightly with salt and pepper. | Set up a breading station with three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten egg, and one with panko breadcrumbs. | Coat each shrimp first in flour, shaking off the excess, then dip in the beaten egg, and finally coat thoroughly with panko breadcrumbs. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or fryer to 180°C (350°F). | Fry the breaded shrimp in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes per batch. Remove and drain on paper towels. | Lightly toast the sandwich bread slices. | Spread Japanese mayonnaise evenly on one side of each bread slice. | Place lettuce leaves on the mayonnaise-coated bread slices. | Arrange the fried shrimp on top of the lettuce evenly. | Optionally, drizzle Tonkatsu sauce or a little more mayonnaise over the shrimp for added flavor. | Cover with the other slice of bread, cut the sandwich in half if desired, and serve immediately.

name: Ebi Fry Teishoku
description: Ebi Fry Teishoku is a Japanese meal set featuring breaded and deep-fried shrimp served with rice, miso soup, shredded cabbage, and tonkatsu sauce. This classic set meal is beloved for its crispy texture and balanced flavors.
instructions: Peel and devein the shrimp, leaving the tail intact, then make small incisions on the underside to prevent curling during frying. | Season the shrimp with a pinch of salt and pepper. | Prepare three separate shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten egg, and one with panko breadcrumbs. | Dredge each shrimp first in flour, shaking off excess, then dip into the beaten egg, and finally coat evenly with panko breadcrumbs. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or fryer to 170°C (340°F). | Deep-fry the breaded shrimp in batches until golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes. Remove and drain on paper towels. | Prepare Japanese white rice according to package instructions and keep warm. | Make miso soup by dissolving miso paste into hot dashi broth and adding tofu cubes and sliced green onions; keep warm. | Arrange shredded cabbage on plates as a fresh side salad. | Serve the fried shrimp with cooked rice, miso soup, shredded cabbage, and a small dish of tonkatsu sauce for dipping.

name: Ebi Gratin
description: Ebi Gratin is a Japanese-Western fusion dish featuring shrimp baked in a creamy white sauce topped with cheese and breadcrumbs. It offers a rich and comforting flavor perfect as an appetizer or light main course.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). | Boil the shrimp in salted water until just cooked, about 2-3 minutes, then drain and set aside. | Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, then add the flour and stir continuously to form a smooth roux. | Gradually whisk in the milk and heavy cream, stirring constantly until the sauce thickens and is smooth. | Remove the sauce from heat, then stir in salt, white pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg for flavor. | In a separate bowl, mix the cooked shrimp with the sauce, and a tablespoon of grated Parmesan cheese. | Transfer the mixture into individual gratin dishes or a baking dish, then sprinkle the top evenly with more grated Parmesan and breadcrumbs. | Place the dish in the preheated oven and bake for about 15-20 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and bubbly. | Remove from oven, let cool slightly, then serve hot as a rich and creamy appetizer or main dish.

name: Ebi Katsu
description: Ebi Katsu is a Japanese shrimp cutlet dish where minced shrimp are shaped, breaded, and deep-fried to a crispy golden perfection, typically served with tonkatsu sauce and shredded cabbage.
instructions: Peel and devein the shrimp, then finely chop them. | Place the chopped shrimp in a bowl and mix with salt, pepper, and a little mayonnaise to enhance moisture and flavor. | Form the shrimp mixture into small oval cutlets. | Prepare three separate shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten egg, and one with panko breadcrumbs. | Coat each cutlet first with flour, then dip into beaten egg, and finally press into panko breadcrumbs until evenly covered. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan to 170°C (340°F). | Deep fry the breaded cutlets until golden brown and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes per side. | Remove the cutlets from the oil and drain excess oil on paper towels. | Serve the Ebi Katsu hot with tonkatsu sauce and shredded cabbage on the side.

name: Ebi Nigiri
description: Ebi Nigiri is a traditional Japanese sushi consisting of cooked shrimp pressed onto vinegared sushi rice, often served with wasabi and soy sauce. It is a simple yet elegant dish showcasing the delicate flavor of shrimp.
instructions: Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the shrimp until they turn pink and opaque, about 2-3 minutes. Drain and immediately plunge the shrimp into ice water to stop cooking and keep them firm. Peel and devein the shrimp, leaving the tail intact. | Slice the shrimp lengthwise on the underside to flatten them slightly, being careful not to cut all the way through. | Moisten your hands with a mixture of water and rice vinegar to prevent sticking. Take about 20 grams of sushi rice and shape it into a small, oval mound. | Lightly dab a small amount of wasabi on top of the rice mound. | Place a shrimp on top of the rice, pressing gently to mold shrimp and rice together. | Optionally, secure the shrimp to the rice with a thin strip of nori sheet wrapped around the middle. | Serve the ebi nigiri with soy sauce, pickled ginger, and wasabi on the side.

name: Camarones Rancheros
description: Camarones Rancheros is a flavorful Mexican dish featuring shrimp cooked in a spicy tomato and chili sauce with fresh herbs and lime, perfect for a quick and vibrant main course.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. | Add diced onion, minced garlic, and chopped jalapeno to the skillet and sauté until softened. | Stir in chopped tomato and cook until the tomato starts to break down and release juices. | Add chili powder, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper, stirring to combine the spices with the tomato mixture. | Add peeled and deveined shrimp to the skillet and cook until they turn pink and are opaque, about 3-5 minutes. | Stir in chopped cilantro and a squeeze of fresh lime juice, mixing well. | Remove from heat and serve immediately, garnished with extra cilantro and lime wedges if desired.

name: Camarones a La Diabla
description: Camarones a la Diabla is a traditional Mexican dish featuring shrimp cooked in a spicy, flavorful chili sauce known as 'devil's sauce.' It is known for its bold heat and rich taste.
instructions: Rinse and peel the shrimp, leaving the tails intact if desired, then devein them. | In a blender, combine dried chili peppers, garlic, tomato sauce, onion, vinegar, salt, pepper, and oregano, and blend until smooth to create the spicy sauce. | Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat, then carefully pour in the chili sauce and cook for a few minutes to thicken slightly and develop flavors. | Add the shrimp to the skillet and cook in the sauce, stirring occasionally, until they turn pink and are cooked through, about 5 minutes. | Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary, adding salt or a pinch of sugar to balance the flavors as desired. | Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro and serve hot with white rice or warm tortillas.

name: Camote Al Horno
description: Camote al Horno is a traditional Filipino baked sweet potato dish that is simple and naturally sweet. This comforting treat is enjoyed as a snack or side dish, highlighting the natural flavor and softness of the sweet potato.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees Celsius (about 400 degrees Fahrenheit). | Wash the sweet potatoes thoroughly and pat them dry with a towel. | Prick the sweet potatoes several times with a fork to allow steam to escape during baking. | Place the sweet potatoes directly on the oven rack or on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. | Bake the sweet potatoes for about 45 to 60 minutes, or until they are tender when pierced with a fork. | Remove the sweet potatoes from the oven and let them cool slightly before serving. | Optionally, slice the sweet potatoes open and add butter, sugar, or cinnamon according to taste.

name: Camote Enmielado
description: Camote Enmielado is a traditional Filipino dessert featuring sweet potatoes cooked in a rich honeyed brown sugar syrup infused with cinnamon, offering a sweet and comforting treat.
instructions: Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into bite-sized chunks. | In a large skillet, combine the water, brown sugar, and a pinch of salt over medium heat. | Stir the mixture until the sugar dissolves and the syrup begins to simmer. | Add the sweet potato chunks to the skillet and mix to coat them evenly with the syrup. | Cover the skillet and let the sweet potatoes cook for about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. | Once the sweet potatoes are tender and the syrup has thickened, add the butter and cinnamon powder. | Stir gently until the butter melts and the sweet potatoes are well coated with the cinnamon-flavored syrup. | Remove from heat and let the dish cool slightly before serving as a dessert or side dish.

name: Camotes Poblanos
description: Camotes Poblanos is a traditional Mexican sweet potato candy made by cooking sweet potatoes with cinnamon and sugar until a thick, sweet paste forms, which is then cooled and cut into pieces for a delicious treat.
instructions: Peel the sweet potato and cut it into small cubes. | Place the sweet potato cubes in a pot and cover with water. | Add cinnamon sticks to the pot and bring to a boil over medium heat. | Cook until the sweet potatoes are very soft and can be easily mashed, about 20 minutes. | Drain the sweet potatoes, reserving some of the cooking liquid. | Mash the sweet potatoes until smooth. | In a separate pan, combine the sugar, a pinch of cinnamon, and a small amount of the reserved cooking liquid. | Heat the sugar mixture over medium heat until the sugar dissolves and the mixture thickens slightly. | Add the mashed sweet potatoes to the sugar mixture and stir constantly. | Cook the mixture over low heat, stirring continuously to prevent sticking, until it thickens and starts to pull away from the sides of the pan. | Remove the cinnamon sticks and transfer the mixture to a greased dish or tray. | Let the mixture cool and set until firm, approximately 4 hours or overnight at room temperature. | Once set, cut into squares or diamond shapes to serve.

name: Campechana De Mariscos
description: Campechana de Mariscos is a refreshing Mexican seafood cocktail featuring a mixture of clam, shrimp, and crab combined with fresh vegetables and lime juice, typically served as an appetizer.
instructions: Chop the onion, tomato, and cilantro finely and place them in a large mixing bowl. | Drain the canned clam and add it to the bowl along with the cooked shrimp and crab meat. | Add lime juice and tomato juice to the bowl and mix all ingredients well to combine. | Season the mixture with salt and black pepper to taste, stirring gently to distribute the seasoning. | Chill the mix in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld. | Serve the campechana chilled, accompanied by tostada or saltine crackers if desired.

name: Campechanas
description: Campechanas are a traditional sweet treat made from puff pastry filled with fruit jam, baked until golden and crispy. This simple dessert is popular in various regions for its delightful combination of flaky pastry and sweet filling.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Roll out the puff pastry sheet on a lightly floured surface to smooth any creases and maintain even thickness. | Cut the pastry into rectangular pieces, approximately 5 by 10 cm each. | Brush each pastry piece with melted butter on both sides. | Spread a thin layer of fruit jam evenly over one side of each pastry rectangle. | Fold the pastry pieces in half over the jam to form a smaller rectangle, pressing the edges gently to seal. | Crimp the edges with a fork to ensure they are well sealed. | Place the pastries on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. | Brush the tops with a little more melted butter and sprinkle generously with sugar. | Bake in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown and puffed. | Remove from the oven and allow to cool on a wire rack before serving.

name: Campeche Pan De Cazon
description: Campeche Pan de Cazon is a traditional Mexican casserole from Campeche featuring layers of corn tortillas and tender shark meat cooked in a flavorful tomato and epazote sauce.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Cook the shark fillets in salted water with bay leaves and peppercorns for about 15 minutes until tender, then drain and flake into small pieces. | In a saucepan, heat olive oil and sauté chopped onion and garlic until translucent. | Add diced tomato, epazote, chili powder, salt, and pepper to the saucepan, and cook for about 10 minutes to make the sauce. | Add the flaked shark to the tomato sauce, mix well, and cook for another 5 minutes. Remove from heat. | Lightly fry the corn tortillas in hot oil for a few seconds on each side to soften, then drain on paper towels. | In a baking dish, place a layer of tortillas, spread a layer of the shark filling, and repeat the layering finishing with the tomato-shark mixture on top. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 20 minutes until heated through and slightly golden on top. | Serve hot, optionally garnished with fresh epazote or a drizzle of crema.

name: Cantina Botana Spread
description: Cantina Botana Spread is a creamy, cheesy bar snack popular for its flavorful and easy-to-make combination of cream cheese, bacon, and taco seasoning. Perfect for serving with chips or crackers at casual gatherings.
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine the cream cheese and sour cream until smooth and creamy. | Add the shredded cheddar cheese, cooked and crumbled bacon, and diced green onions to the bowl. | Mix all the ingredients thoroughly to combine evenly. | Stir in the taco seasoning, adjusting the amount to your desired level of flavor and spice. | Transfer the mixture to a serving dish and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to allow the flavors to meld. | Serve chilled with tortilla chips, crackers, or fresh vegetable sticks as a flavorful bar snack.

name: Capirotada
description: Capirotada is a traditional Mexican bread pudding made with toasted bread, piloncillo syrup, nuts, raisins, and cheese baked to a sweet and savory delight typically served during Lent.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F). | Cut the bolillo bread into slices about 1 cm thick and lightly toast them in the oven until golden, about 10 minutes. Remove and set aside. | In a medium saucepan, combine the piloncillo, water, cinnamon sticks, and cloves. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the piloncillo dissolves and the syrup thickens slightly, about 15 minutes. Remove cinnamon and cloves. | Grease a baking dish with butter. Layer half of the toasted bread slices in the dish. | Sprinkle half of the nuts, raisins, and shredded cheese over the bread. | Pour half of the piloncillo syrup evenly over the layered ingredients. | Repeat with the remaining bread, nuts, raisins, cheese, and syrup. | Dot the top with small pieces of butter. | Bake uncovered for 30 to 40 minutes, or until the top is golden and bubbling. | Let cool slightly before serving to allow the syrup to absorb fully.

name: Broccoli Cream Soup
description: A smooth and creamy broccoli soup made by blending tender cooked broccoli with cream and aromatic vegetables. This comforting soup is simple, nutritious, and perfect as a starter or light meal.
instructions: Wash and chop the broccoli into small florets. | Peel and dice the onion and garlic. | In a large pot, heat the butter over medium heat until melted. | Add the onion and garlic to the pot and sauté until soft and translucent. | Add the broccoli florets to the pot and stir for a few minutes. | Pour the chicken broth into the pot and bring to a boil. | Reduce heat and simmer until the broccoli is tender, about 10-15 minutes. | Use an immersion blender or transfer the mixture to a blender to puree until smooth. | Return the soup to low heat and stir in the heavy cream. | Season with salt and pepper to taste and heat through without boiling. | Serve hot, optionally garnished with a sprig of parsley or a drizzle of cream.

name: Broccoli with Olive Oil and Lemon
description: A simple and healthy side dish of tender broccoli florets dressed with fresh olive oil and lemon juice, offering a bright and fresh flavor profile.
instructions: Wash and cut the broccoli into bite-sized florets. | Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. | Add the broccoli florets to the boiling water and cook for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. | Drain the broccoli and immediately plunge it into a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking process and preserve the bright green color. | Drain the broccoli from the ice water and pat dry with a clean towel. | Place the broccoli in a serving bowl. | Drizzle olive oil evenly over the broccoli. | Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the broccoli and olive oil. | Sprinkle with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. | Toss gently to combine all ingredients well before serving.

name: Butelo with Casulas
alias: Smoked Pork Sausage with Cabbage Stew
description: Butelo com Casulas is a traditional Portuguese dish featuring smoked pork sausage simmered with cabbage and potatoes to create a hearty stew rich in flavor and perfect for comforting meals.
instructions: Soak the smoked pork sausage (butelo) in cold water for a few hours or overnight to reduce excess salt and soften the casing. | Drain the butelo, then place it in a large pot and cover with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer gently for about 1 hour until tender. | While the sausage cooks, clean and chop the cabbage (casulas) into medium-sized pieces. | After the butelo has simmered for an hour, add the chopped cabbage to the pot. | Add the peeled and chopped potato, clove of garlic, bay leaf, salt, and pepper to the pot. | Simmer the mixture for an additional 30 to 40 minutes, until the cabbage and potato are soft and flavors are blended. | Remove the butelo from the pot, slice it into pieces, and set aside. | Discard the bay leaf and adjust seasoning of the stew to taste. | Serve the cabbage stew hot with slices of the butelo on top or on the side.

name: Cabbage Rice
description: Cabbage Rice is a simple, comforting dish featuring tender cabbage cooked with rice and seasoned with aromatic garlic and onion. Popular in various cuisines, it is a wholesome and flavorful vegetarian main dish.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until water runs clear, then drain. | Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. | Add the chopped onion and garlic to the pan and sauté until softened and translucent. | Add the shredded cabbage to the pan and cook until it begins to soften, about 5 minutes. | Add the rice to the pan and stir to combine with the cabbage mixture. | Pour in the vegetable broth and bring to a boil. | Reduce heat to low, cover the pan, and simmer for about 15-20 minutes, or until the rice is cooked and the liquid is absorbed. | Season with salt and black pepper to taste. | Fluff the cabbage rice with a fork and garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Cabbage and Carrot Slaw
description: A crisp and refreshing salad combining shredded cabbage and grated carrot with a tangy apple cider vinegar dressing, perfect as a light side dish.
instructions: Finely shred the cabbage and grate the carrot into a large mixing bowl. | In a separate small bowl, whisk together the apple cider vinegar, olive oil, honey, salt, and black pepper until well combined. | Pour the dressing over the shredded cabbage and grated carrot. | Toss the vegetables and dressing together until everything is evenly coated. | Let the slaw sit in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld. | Serve chilled as a refreshing side dish.

name: Cabbage and Meat Stew
description: A hearty and comforting stew combining tender beef with sweet cabbage and aromatic spices, perfect for a warming meal.
instructions: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes and season with salt and pepper. | Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and brown the meat on all sides. | Chop the cabbage into large pieces, peel and dice the onion, and crush the garlic. | Add the onion and garlic to the pot and sauté until softened and fragrant. | Pour in the beef broth and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes until the meat is tender. | Add the chopped cabbage, diced tomato, paprika, and caraway seeds to the pot. | Continue simmering for another 30 minutes until the cabbage is soft and flavors are well blended. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste before serving hot.

name: Cabbage and Potato Soup
description: A comforting and simple cabbage and potato soup made by simmering fresh vegetables in a flavorful broth, perfect for a healthy and warming meal.
instructions: Peel and dice the potato into small cubes. | Chop the cabbage into thin strips. | Peel and finely chop the onion and garlic. | Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. | Add the chopped onion and garlic to the pot and sauté until translucent and fragrant. | Add the diced potato and chopped cabbage to the pot and stir well. | Pour in the vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a boil. | Reduce heat to low and simmer for about 25 minutes or until the potatoes and cabbage are tender. | Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste. | Optional: use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup for a creamier texture or leave it chunky according to preference. | Serve the soup hot, garnished with fresh parsley if desired.

name: Cacholeira Sausage Fried
description: Cacholeira Sausage Fried is a simple and flavorful dish featuring the traditional Brazilian cacholeira sausage, sliced and fried until crispy and golden. It makes a delicious snack or appetizer with rich, savory flavors.
instructions: Slice the cacholeira sausage into bite-sized pieces. | Heat vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium heat. | Add the sliced sausage to the pan and fry until golden brown and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally. | Remove the sausage from the pan and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. | Optionally, season with a pinch of black pepper and serve hot as a snack or appetizer.

name: Cachorro Hot Dog Portuguese Style
description: Cachorro is a popular Portuguese-style hot dog characterized by a boiled sausage served in a bun with mayonnaise, fresh onions, cabbage, and parsley. It is a tasty and simple street food snack in Portugal.
instructions: Boil the hot dog sausage in water for about 5 minutes until heated through. | In a small pan, warm the hot dog bun lightly until slightly toasted. | Place the boiled sausage inside the bun. | Spread mayonnaise evenly over the sausage and bun. | Top with finely chopped onion and shredded cabbage for crunch. | Sprinkle some fresh parsley over the top for garnish. | Optionally, drizzle a bit of ketchup and mustard according to taste.

name: Caldeirada
description: Caldeirada is a traditional Portuguese fisherman's stew from Peniche, combining various fish and fresh vegetables simmered together to create a hearty and flavorful dish.
instructions: Clean and cut the fish into thick slices or chunks, keeping different types separate. | Slice the onion and bell pepper into rings, mince the garlic, and peel the tomatoes, removing seeds and chopping them. | In a large pot, layer half of the sliced onions, bell peppers, and tomatoes, then add half of the minced garlic, a sprinkle of salt, pepper, bay leaf, and a drizzle of olive oil. | Add a layer of mixed fish over the vegetables, then cover with the remaining onions, bell peppers, tomatoes, and garlic. Season again with salt and pepper, add the second bay leaf, and drizzle more olive oil and white wine over everything. | Add the diced potatoes evenly on top. Cover the pot and cook over medium heat for about 30-40 minutes until the fish is cooked and potatoes are tender, avoiding stirring too much to keep the layers intact. | Sprinkle chopped fresh parsley and drizzle extra olive oil before serving. | Serve hot with crusty bread on the side.

name: Breaded Pig Trotters
description: Breaded pig trotters are a traditional dish where tender boiled trotters are coated in flour, egg, and breadcrumbs, then deep-fried until crispy, offering a rich and flavorful delicacy.
instructions: Clean the pig trotters thoroughly by scraping and washing them several times with water. | Place the trotters in a large pot and cover them with water. | Add salt and optional aromatics like onion, garlic, and bay leaf to the pot for flavor. | Bring the water to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer the trotters for about 1.5 to 2 hours, or until they become tender. | Remove the cooked trotters from the pot and let them cool to a temperature safe to handle. | Once cooled, cut the trotters into smaller, manageable pieces if desired. | Prepare three separate bowls: one with flour, one with beaten egg, and one with breadcrumbs. | Coat each piece of trotter first in flour, then dip it in the beaten egg, and finally coat it with breadcrumbs to cover evenly. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan or deep fryer to around 175°C (350°F). | Fry the breaded trotters in batches until they are golden brown and crispy, approximately 3 to 5 minutes per batch. | Remove the fried trotters and place them on paper towels to drain excess oil. | Serve hot with your choice of dipping sauce or accompaniment.

name: Broad Bean Soup
description: Broad Bean Soup is a hearty and traditional dish made with tender broad beans and vegetables simmered in a flavorful broth. This comforting soup is popular in many cultures and showcases the creamy texture and earthy flavor of broad beans.
instructions: Soak 200 grams of dried broad bean in water overnight to soften. | Drain and rinse the soaked broad bean thoroughly. | Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. | Add 1 chopped onion and 2 cloves of minced garlic to the pot and sauté until they are soft and translucent. | Add the drained broad bean to the pot and stir to combine with the onion and garlic. | Pour in 1 liter of chicken broth and bring the mixture to a boil. | Reduce heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for about 45 minutes or until the beans are tender. | Add 1 chopped carrot and 1 chopped potato to the pot and continue to simmer for another 20 minutes until the vegetables are soft. | Season the soup with 1 teaspoon of salt and 0.5 teaspoon of black pepper. | Optionally, add 1 tablespoon of chopped fresh parsley for flavor. | Use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup to desired consistency, leaving some beans whole for texture. | Serve hot, garnished with a drizzle of olive oil and extra parsley if desired.

name: Broad Beans with Ham
description: Broad Beans with Ham is a traditional Spanish dish combining tender broad beans and flavorful ham, simmered together for a hearty and comforting meal.
instructions: Soak the broad beans in water overnight to soften them. | Drain the soaked broad beans and rinse thoroughly. | Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat and sauté chopped onion and garlic until translucent. | Add diced ham to the pan and cook until slightly browned. | Add the drained broad beans to the pan and stir to combine. | Pour in chicken broth and season with salt, pepper, and paprika. | Cover the pan and simmer on low heat until the beans are tender, about 20-30 minutes. | If desired, add some chopped parsley at the end for freshness. | Serve the broad beans with ham warm as a side dish or light main.

name: Broken Eggs with Chistorra and Potatoes
description: Huevos Rotos con Chistorra y Patatas is a traditional Spanish dish featuring crispy fried potatoes topped with flavorful chistorra sausage and fried eggs with runny yolks, meant to be broken and mixed together before eating.
instructions: Peel and cut the potatoes into thin strips like fries. | Heat a generous amount of vegetable oil in a frying pan over medium heat. | Fry the potato strips until golden and crispy, then remove and drain on paper towels, seasoning with salt. | In a separate pan, cook the chistorra sausage slices over medium heat until browned and cooked through. | Using the same pan or a clean one, fry the eggs sunny side up or to your preference, keeping the yolks runny. | Arrange the crispy potatoes on a serving plate, top with the cooked chistorra slices, then carefully place the fried eggs over the top. | Serve immediately, encouraging diners to break the eggs over the potatoes and sausage before eating.

name: Brown Crab
description: Brown Crab (Buey de Mar) is a popular seafood delicacy known for its sweet, tender meat. This simple recipe highlights the crab's natural flavors through boiling and fresh accompaniments.
instructions: Fill a large pot with water and add salt to create a seawater-like brine. | Bring the water to a rolling boil over high heat. | Grasp the live brown crab by its back legs and place it into the boiling water headfirst. | Boil the crab for about 15–20 minutes for a medium-sized crab (approximately 1.5 kg), adjusting time for size. | Prepare an ice bath by filling a bowl with cold water and ice cubes. | Once the crab is cooked, use tongs to remove it from the boiling water and immediately place it into the ice bath to stop the cooking process and preserve texture. | Let the crab cool in the ice bath for 5 minutes. | Remove the crab and let it drain. | Place the crab on a stable surface, and using kitchen shears or a crab cracker, remove the claws and legs by twisting them off. | Remove the top shell by lifting from the back, and discard the gills and other inedible parts inside. | Extract the meat from the claws and legs using a crab cracker or pick. | Break the body in half and pick out the sweet meat inside the chambers. | Serve the crab meat chilled or warm with lemon wedges and a simple mayonnaise or garlic butter dipping sauce.

name: Brussels Sprouts with Ham
description: A simple and flavorful dish featuring sautéed Brussels sprouts combined with savory ham, perfect as a side dish.
instructions: Wash the Brussels sprouts and trim the ends. Cut them in half if they are large. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. | Add the Brussels sprouts to the skillet and sauté for about 5-7 minutes until they start to brown. | Add diced ham to the skillet and cook for another 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the ham is heated through and the Brussels sprouts are tender. | Season with salt and pepper to taste. | Optionally, sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving.

name: Butifarra Con Mongetes
description: Butifarra con Mongetes is a classic Catalan dish featuring traditional pork sausages served with tender white beans cooked with garlic and olive oil for a simple, hearty meal.
instructions: Soak the dried white beans overnight in cold water. | Drain and rinse the beans, then place them in a pot with fresh water covering them by about 2 inches. | Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook the beans until tender, about 1 to 1.5 hours. | In a separate pan, heat a little olive oil over medium heat. | Add the garlic cloves and fry until golden and fragrant; remove and set aside. | In the same pan, add the butifarra sausages and cook until evenly browned and cooked through, about 10-15 minutes, turning occasionally. | Season the beans with salt, pepper, and olive oil. | Drain the cooked beans and mix them with the garlic-infused olive oil, stirring gently to combine. | Serve the sausages alongside the warm garlic-flavored beans. | Garnish with chopped fresh parsley if desired.

name: Butifarra a La Brasa
description: Butifarra a la Brasa is a traditional Catalan grilled pork sausage, characterized by its rich flavor and crispy skin from grilling over charcoal or an open flame.
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat. | Prick the butifarra sausages a few times with a fork to prevent bursting during grilling. | Place the sausages on the hot grill and cook for about 8-10 minutes, turning frequently to ensure even cooking and to develop a charred exterior. | While grilling, baste occasionally with a little olive oil to keep the sausages moist. | Once the sausages are cooked through and have a crispy, browned skin, remove them from the grill. | Serve hot, traditionally accompanied by grilled vegetables, white beans, or rustic bread.

name: Buñuelos De Bacalao
description: Buñuelos de Bacalao are traditional Spanish salt cod fritters, crispy on the outside and soft inside, flavored with garlic and parsley, making a popular appetizer or snack.
instructions: Soak the salt cod in cold water for 24-48 hours, changing the water several times to remove excess salt. | Drain the soaked salt cod and remove any skin and bones. | Boil the salt cod in fresh water for about 10 minutes, then drain and flake the fish into small pieces. | In a mixing bowl, combine the flaked cod, all-purpose flour, baking powder, finely chopped garlic, chopped fresh parsley, and beaten egg. | Gradually add milk to the mixture, stirring until you get a thick batter consistency. | Season the batter with a pinch of salt and black pepper to taste. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat. | Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil, frying a few at a time to avoid overcrowding. | Fry the fritters until they are golden brown and crispy on both sides, about 3-4 minutes per side. | Remove the fritters with a slotted spoon and drain them on paper towels. | Serve the buñuelos warm, garnished with extra parsley or a wedge of lemon if desired.

name: Buñuelos De Bacalao Dulce
description: Buñuelos de Bacalao Dulce are traditional sweet cod fritters made by incorporating flaked salt cod into a batter that is fried until golden, then optionally dusted with powdered sugar for a delightful sweet and savory treat.
instructions: Soak the dried salt cod in cold water for 24 hours, changing the water several times to remove excess salt. | Drain the cod and place it in a pot with fresh water; bring to a boil and simmer until the fish flakes easily, about 10 minutes. | Drain the cod and remove any skin and bones, then flake the fish finely with a fork. | In a mixing bowl, beat the eggs with sugar until pale and fluffy. | Add the flaked cod, all-purpose flour, baking powder, milk, lemon zest, and a pinch of cinnamon to the eggs and sugar mixture. Stir until you get a smooth batter. | Heat olive oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat. | Using a spoon, drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil, frying a few at a time to avoid overcrowding. | Fry the fritters until golden and puffed up, about 2-3 minutes per side. | Remove fritters with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. | Optionally, dust the fritters with powdered sugar before serving.

name: Goong Pad Sataw
description: Goong Pad Sataw is a flavorful Thai stir-fry dish featuring fresh shrimp and stink beans, known for their unique aroma and crunchy texture, combined with savory sauces for a balanced taste.
instructions: Rinse the stink beans and chop them into bite-sized pieces. | Peel and devein the shrimp, then rinse and pat dry. | Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. | Add minced garlic and sliced chili to the hot oil and stir-fry until fragrant. | Add the shrimp to the wok and stir-fry until they start to turn pink. | Add the chopped stink beans and continue stir-frying for a few minutes until the beans are tender but still crisp. | Season with fish sauce, oyster sauce, and a pinch of sugar, mixing well to combine all flavors. | Cook for another minute, then remove from heat. | Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Goong Pad Sauce Makham
description: Goong Pad Sauce Makham is a flavorful Thai stir-fried shrimp dish featuring tangy tamarind sauce, balanced with sweet, salty, and spicy elements, served with aromatic herbs.
instructions: Soak the tamarind pulp in 100 ml of warm water for about 10 minutes, then strain to extract the tamarind juice and set aside. | Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat. | Add the minced garlic and dried chili, stir-fry until fragrant, about 30 seconds. | Add the shrimp and stir-fry until they start to turn pink, about 2-3 minutes. | Pour in the tamarind juice, fish sauce, palm sugar, and ketchup, stirring well to combine. | Cook for another 2-3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and the shrimp are cooked through. | Sprinkle chopped spring onion and Thai basil leaves on top, stir briefly, then remove from heat. | Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Goong Pao
description: Goong Pao is a traditional Thai dish featuring grilled giant river prawns marinated in a flavorful mixture of herbs, spices, and fish sauce, served with a tangy dipping sauce enhancing its savory taste.
instructions: Prepare the marinade by mixing finely chopped garlic, sliced shallot, chopped cilantro root, chopped lemongrass, chopped bird's eye chili, palm sugar, fish sauce, and white pepper in a mortar and pestle; pound until well combined but coarse. | Clean the giant river prawns by removing the vein and shell slightly, leaving the head and tail intact; make a small incision on the back for marinade absorption. | Brush the prawn with the marinade thoroughly on both sides and let it marinate for 15-20 minutes. | Prepare a charcoal grill or preheat a grill pan over medium-high heat. | Grill the prawns for 3-4 minutes on each side until they turn pink and slightly charred; baste occasionally with remaining marinade during grilling. | For the dipping sauce, mix chopped shallot, chopped chili, sugar, lime juice, and fish sauce until balanced to taste. | Serve the grilled giant river prawns hot with the dipping sauce and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves.

name: Goong Phao
description: Goong Phao is a traditional Thai dish featuring flame-grilled river prawns marinated in a tangy, spicy sauce and served with a delicious dipping sauce, showcasing smoky and bold flavors.
instructions: Clean the river prawns by rinsing them under cold water and patting them dry with paper towels, leaving the shells intact. | Prepare the marinade by mixing fish sauce, lime juice, minced garlic, finely chopped chili, and a pinch of sugar in a bowl. | Brush the marinade generously over the prawns, ensuring they are well coated. Let them marinate for about 15 minutes to absorb the flavors. | Preheat a charcoal grill or gas grill to medium-high heat and oil the grates to prevent sticking. | Place the marinated prawns on the grill shell side down and cook for about 3-4 minutes. | Flip the prawns carefully and grill for another 2-3 minutes until the shells turn bright orange and the meat is opaque and slightly charred. | Remove the prawns from the grill and serve immediately, garnished with chopped cilantro and lime wedges on the side. | Serve with a spicy dipping sauce made from mixing fish sauce, lime juice, sugar, minced garlic, and chopped fresh chili, balanced to taste.

name: Goong Sarong
description: Goong Sarong is a Thai appetizer featuring shrimp wrapped in crispy fried rice vermicelli noodles, providing a delightful texture and savory flavor.
instructions: Soak rice vermicelli noodles in warm water for about 10 minutes or until soft, then drain and pat dry. | Peel and devein the shrimp, then finely chop half of them for the filling, leaving the rest whole for wrapping. | In a mixing bowl, combine chopped shrimp, minced garlic, finely chopped coriander root, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, white pepper, and beaten egg. Mix well to form the shrimp filling. | Heat vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the shrimp filling and cook until it firms up, about 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat and let cool. | Take one whole shrimp, place it on a small bundle of softened noodles, then carefully wrap the noodles around the shrimp to cover it completely. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or wok to 180°C (350°F). Fry the wrapped shrimp in batches until the noodles are golden brown and crispy, about 2-3 minutes. | Remove the fried shrimp with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. | Serve the Goong Sarong hot with sweet chili sauce or plum sauce for dipping.

name: Goong Tempura
description: Goong Tempura is a Thai-style shrimp tempura featuring light and crispy battered shrimp, often served with a tangy dipping sauce. This dish highlights the delicate texture and flavor of shrimp combined with a crunchy tempura coating.
instructions: Prepare the shrimp by peeling and deveining them, leaving the tail intact. Pat them dry with paper towels. | In a bowl, mix the tempura batter by combining cold water and tempura flour gently to keep the batter light and lumpy. Do not overmix. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan or wok to 180°C (350°F). | Dip each shrimp into the batter, allowing excess to drip off, then carefully place them into the hot oil. | Fry the shrimp in batches, turning occasionally, until they are golden crispy and cooked through, about 2-3 minutes. | Remove shrimp with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. | Serve the Goong Tempura hot with a dipping sauce made from soy sauce, lime juice, sugar, and chili flakes if desired.

name: Goong Tod Kratiam
description: Goong Tod Kratiam is a popular Thai appetizer featuring succulent shrimp deep-fried with fragrant garlic to a crispy perfection. The aromatic garlic flavor combined with crispy texture makes it a delightful snack or appetizer.
instructions: Peel and devein the shrimp, leaving the tail intact, then pat them dry with paper towels. | Crush the garlic cloves finely using a mortar and pestle or mince finely with a knife. | In a mixing bowl, combine the shrimp with the crushed garlic, salt, white pepper, and a tablespoon of rice flour, mixing gently to coat the shrimp evenly. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or wok to about 180°C (350°F) for deep frying. | Coat the garlic-seasoned shrimp lightly with rice flour to ensure crispiness. | Carefully place the shrimp into the hot oil in small batches, frying until golden brown and crispy, approximately 2-3 minutes per batch. | Use a slotted spoon to remove the shrimp and drain them on paper towels to remove excess oil. | Transfer the deep-fried garlic shrimp to a serving plate and sprinkle with fried garlic bits (if any) from the oil for extra flavor. | Serve immediately as an appetizer or snack, optionally accompanied by a spicy dipping sauce or fresh lime wedges.

name: Goong Yang
description: Goong Yang is a popular Thai dish featuring succulent river prawns grilled to perfection, typically served with a tangy and spicy dipping sauce that accentuates the natural flavors of the seafood.
instructions: Preheat the grill to medium-high heat. | Clean and devein the river prawns, leaving the shells on for grilling. | In a bowl, mix fish sauce, minced garlic, lime juice, sugar, and a pinch of chili flakes to prepare the marinade and dipping sauce. | Brush the prawns lightly with vegetable oil to prevent sticking on the grill. | Place the prawns on the grill shell side down, and cook for about 4-5 minutes until the shells turn bright orange and the flesh turns opaque. | Flip the prawns and grill for another 2-3 minutes until cooked through. | Remove the prawns from the grill and serve immediately with the prepared dipping sauce and fresh lime wedges.

name: Green Curry with Bamboo Shoot
alias: Gaeng Kiew Wan Sai nor Mai
description: Gaeng Kiew Wan Sai Nor Mai is a traditional Thai green curry featuring tender chicken, bamboo shoots, and fragrant herbs, creating a rich and spicy dish served with jasmine rice.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a pot over medium heat. | Add green curry paste and stir until fragrant, about 2 minutes. | Pour in coconut milk and bring to a gentle boil, stirring to combine with the curry paste. | Add bamboo shoot, sliced chicken breast, fish sauce, and palm sugar to the pot. | Simmer the curry for 10-15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the bamboo shoot is tender. | Add Thai eggplant and continue to simmer for 5 more minutes until the eggplant is soft. | Add kaffir lime leaves and Thai basil leaves to the curry, stir well and cook for another minute. | Remove from heat and serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Green Curry with Beef
description: A classic Thai green curry featuring tender beef simmered in creamy coconut milk with aromatic herbs and vegetables, served with jasmine rice.
instructions: Heat vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat. | Add green curry paste and sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. | Add sliced beef and cook until browned on all sides. | Pour in coconut milk and bring to a simmer. | Add sliced eggplant, bamboo shoots, and kaffir lime leaves. | Season with fish sauce and palm sugar, stirring to dissolve. | Simmer for 10-15 minutes until vegetables are tender and beef is cooked through. | Add Thai basil leaves and stir just before turning off the heat. | Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Borek Plate
description: Borek Plate is a traditional Turkish appetizer platter featuring an assortment of savory pastries filled with cheese, spinach, and ground meat wrapped in thin phyllo dough and baked to golden perfection.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Prepare the filling ingredients: crumble the white cheese, chop the spinach finely, and mix with a pinch of salt and pepper. | In separate bowls, prepare each filling: cheese filling with crumbled cheese and chopped parsley; spinach filling with cooked spinach, onion, and seasoning; and ground meat filling with sautéed onion, ground meat, and spices. | Cut phyllo dough sheets into appropriate sizes to make small triangles or rolls as preferred. | Brush a phyllo sheet lightly with olive oil, place a spoonful of one of the fillings at one end, and fold the dough over to enclose the filling, forming triangles or rolls. | Place the filled pastries on a baking tray lined with baking paper, brush the tops with olive oil. | Repeat for all dough sheets and fillings, mixing types on the tray. | Bake in the preheated oven for 25–30 minutes or until golden brown and crisp. | Remove from oven and let cool slightly before serving on a large plate as an appetizer assortment.

name: Bosnian Spiral Pastry
description: Bosnian Spiral Pastry, known as Bosnak Boregi, is a traditional savory pastry with layers of thin dough filled with white cheese and parsley, shaped into spirals and baked until golden.
instructions: Mix the flour with a pinch of salt in a large bowl to make the dough. | Add warm water and olive oil to the flour and knead until a smooth, elastic dough forms. | Cover the dough and let it rest for about 30 minutes. | In the meantime, prepare the filling by mixing crumbled white cheese with chopped parsley. | Divide the rested dough into equal portions. | On a floured surface, roll out each portion into a very thin, large circle or rectangle. | Brush each dough sheet with olive oil. | Spread a thin layer of the cheese and parsley mixture evenly over the dough. | Starting from one edge, roll the dough into a long, thin rope with the filling inside. | Coil the rope into a spiral shape and place it on a greased baking tray. | Repeat the process with remaining dough and filling, placing the spirals close to each other if desired. | Brush the spirals with olive oil or melted butter on top for a golden finish. | Bake in a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F) for about 30-35 minutes or until golden and cooked through. | Allow to cool slightly before serving.

name: Boza
description: Boza is a traditional fermented millet drink popular in parts of Eastern Europe and the Middle East known for its thick, slightly tangy taste and probiotic qualities.
instructions: Rinse the millet thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. | In a large pot, add the rinsed millet and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer until the millet is soft and the mixture thickens, about 30-40 minutes. | Allow the cooked millet mixture to cool to lukewarm temperature, around 30-35°C (86-95°F). | Add sugar and stir well to dissolve. | Add the active yeast to the millet mixture and mix thoroughly. | Cover the pot with a clean cloth or lid and leave it to ferment at room temperature for 2 to 3 days, until it becomes slightly tangy and bubbly. | After fermentation, stir the boza and strain it through a fine sieve or cheesecloth to remove any larger millet particles for a smoother texture. | Refrigerate the strained boza for several hours to chill before serving. | Serve cold, optionally garnished with a sprinkle of ground cinnamon or roasted chickpeas on top.

name: Breakfast Frankfurters
description: Breakfast Frankfurters are small, savory poultry sausages commonly served as part of a Turkish breakfast spread. They are quickly cooked and enjoyed warm alongside other traditional morning dishes.
instructions: Separate the breakfast frankfurters into individual pieces if in a linked coil form. | Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and add the frankfurters, cooking for about 5-7 minutes until they are browned and cooked through, turning occasionally. | Optional: While cooking, you may add a small amount of butter or olive oil to the pan if needed to prevent sticking and enhance flavor. | Remove the frankfurters from the skillet and place them on a plate lined with paper towels to absorb any excess fat. | Serve warm as a breakfast side dish with eggs, bread, or traditional Turkish breakfast accompaniments such as olives, cheese, tomatoes, and cucumbers.

name: Broad Bean Rice Pilaf
description: Broad Bean Rice Pilaf is a simple and flavorful Turkish side dish combining tender broad beans with fluffy rice, enhanced by sautéed onions and olive oil. It offers a nutritious and satisfying accompaniment to many meals.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for about 20 minutes. | Drain the rice and set aside. | Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. | Add the chopped onion and sauté until soft and translucent. | Add the broad beans and cook for a few minutes until they start to soften. | Add the rice to the pan and gently stir to coat the rice with the oil, onions, and beans. | Pour in the hot water or vegetable broth, add salt, and stir gently once. | Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the saucepan, and simmer for about 15-20 minutes or until the rice is cooked and the liquid is absorbed. | Remove the pan from the heat and let it rest, covered, for 10 minutes. | Fluff the rice pilaf with a fork and garnish with fresh parsley before serving.

name: Broccoli Gratin
description: Broccoli Gratin is a comforting French-inspired baked dish featuring tender broccoli coated in a creamy cheese sauce and topped with a golden crust. It makes a delicious and hearty side dish.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and blanch the broccoli florets for about 3-4 minutes until tender but still crisp. Drain and set aside. | In a saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 1-2 minutes to form a roux, stirring constantly. | Gradually whisk in the milk, continuing to stir until the sauce thickens and is smooth. | Remove the sauce from heat and stir in grated cheese, salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg until the cheese is melted and the sauce is creamy. | Place the blanched broccoli in a baking dish and pour the cheese sauce evenly over it. | Sprinkle additional grated cheese and breadcrumbs on top for a golden crust. | Bake in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes or until the top is bubbly and golden brown. | Allow to cool slightly before serving.

name: Broccoli Soup
description: A creamy, comforting Turkish-style broccoli soup that's simple to make and packed with nutrition. Perfect as a light starter or healthy main dish.
instructions: Wash and chop the broccoli into small florets. | Peel and chop the onion and garlic finely. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. | Add the chopped onion and garlic to the pot and sauté until translucent. | Add the broccoli florets and sauté for a few minutes. | Pour in the vegetable broth and bring to a boil. | Reduce heat and let it simmer until the broccoli is tender, about 15 minutes. | Use an immersion blender to purée the soup until smooth. | Stir in the cream and season with salt and pepper to taste. | Heat the soup gently for a few more minutes without boiling. | Serve hot, optionally garnished with fresh parsley or croutons.

name: Bukhara-style Pilaf
description: Bukhara-Style Pilaf, or Buhara Pilavi, is a traditional Central Asian dish featuring tender lamb, fragrant rice, and vegetables cooked together with warm spices, creating a hearty and aromatic meal.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in warm water for about 30 minutes. | Heat sunflower oil in a large pot over medium heat, then add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent. | Add cubed lamb to the pot and brown it on all sides. | Stir in peeled and chopped carrot cubes and cook for a few minutes until slightly softened. | Drain the soaked rice and add it to the pot, stirring gently to combine with the meat and vegetables. | Pour in hot water or broth, add salt, black pepper, and cinnamon; bring to a boil. | Reduce heat to low, cover the pot tightly, and simmer gently until the rice is cooked and liquid is absorbed, about 20-25 minutes. | Remove from heat and let the pilaf rest, covered, for 10 minutes. | Garnish with toasted almond slices and chopped parsley before serving.

name: Bulgur Soup
description: Bulgur Soup is a traditional Turkish soup made with bulgur wheat, vegetables, and aromatic spices. It is a comforting and nutritious dish commonly enjoyed in Turkish cuisine.
instructions: Rinse the bulgur under cold water and set aside. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. | Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until translucent. | Add the diced carrot and continue to cook for a few minutes until softened. | Pour in the chicken broth and bring to a boil. | Add the rinsed bulgur to the boiling broth. | Reduce heat to low and simmer for about 15-20 minutes until bulgur is tender. | Season the soup with salt, black pepper, and paprika according to taste. | In a small pan, melt butter and add dried mint; then pour this mixture into the soup for added flavor. | Stir the soup well and cook for an additional 5 minutes to blend the flavors. | Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley if desired.

name: Bulgur Wheat Pilaf
description: Bulgur wheat pilaf is a traditional Middle Eastern dish made by simmering bulgur in flavorful broth with onion and tomato paste, resulting in a fragrant and hearty side dish.
instructions: Rinse the bulgur wheat under cold water until the water runs clear, then drain well. | Heat the olive oil and butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. | Add the finely chopped onion and sauté until it becomes translucent and soft. | Add the tomato paste and stir well to combine with the onion, cooking for a minute. | Pour in the hot chicken broth and bring it to a boil. | Add the rinsed bulgur wheat to the boiling broth, stir once, then reduce the heat to low and cover the pan with a lid. | Simmer gently for about 15 minutes, or until the bulgur is tender and the liquid is fully absorbed. | Remove the saucepan from heat and let it sit, covered, for 10 minutes. | Fluff the pilaf gently with a fork before serving.

name: Braised Pork Shanks
description: Braised pork shanks are slowly cooked until tender in a rich sauce made with vegetables, red wine, and herbs, yielding a flavorful and hearty dish.
instructions: Pat the pork shanks dry with paper towels and season them generously with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. | Add the pork shanks to the pot and brown them on all sides until they develop a deep golden color, about 8-10 minutes. Remove the shanks and set aside. | In the same pot, add chopped onion, carrot, celery, and garlic. Sauté until the vegetables soften, about 5 minutes. | Add tomato paste and cook for another 2 minutes to deepen the flavor. | Pour in red wine and bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. | Add pork broth, bay leaf, dried thyme, and a pinch of black pepper. | Return the pork shanks to the pot, making sure they are partially submerged in the liquid. | Cover the pot with a lid and reduce the heat to low. Let it simmer gently for about 2 to 3 hours or until the meat is tender and falling off the bone. | Remove the pork shanks and keep warm. Increase the heat to medium-high and reduce the braising liquid until it thickens to a sauce consistency. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve the pork shanks with the sauce spooned over them, optionally garnished with fresh parsley.

name: Braised Short Ribs
description: Braised short ribs are a tender and flavorful dish where beef ribs are slowly cooked in red wine and aromatics until meltingly soft, offering a rich and comforting meal.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C (320°F). | Season the short ribs generously with salt and pepper on all sides. | Heat the vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed ovenproof pot over medium-high heat. | Brown the short ribs in batches, about 3-4 minutes per side, until well caramelized. Remove and set aside. | Add chopped onion, carrot, and celery to the pot and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes to deepen the flavor. | Pour in red wine and bring to a simmer, scraping up browned bits from the bottom. | Add beef broth, bay leaf, thyme sprig, and return the browned short ribs to the pot. | Bring to a simmer, cover with a lid, and transfer to the oven. | Cook for about 2.5 to 3 hours, until the meat is very tender and easily pulls away from the bone. | Remove the short ribs from the pot and strain the braising liquid into a saucepan. | Skim off excess fat and simmer the sauce until slightly thickened. | Serve the short ribs topped with the sauce and garnish with chopped parsley.

name: Bran Muffin
description: Bran muffins are a wholesome and hearty baked good made with wheat bran for added fiber, often enjoyed as a nutritious breakfast or snack.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit (190 degrees Celsius). | In a large bowl, mix together wheat bran, baking soda, salt, and whole wheat flour. | In another bowl, beat egg with brown sugar until smooth. | Add vegetable oil and milk to the egg mixture and stir to combine. | Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix until just combined. | Stir in raisins if using. | Spoon the batter into a greased muffin tin, filling each cup about two-thirds full. | Bake in the preheated oven for 15 to 20 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. | Allow muffins to cool in the tin for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: Bran Muffins
description: Classic American bran muffins are moist, slightly sweet, and wholesome, often enjoyed as a fiber-rich breakfast or snack.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and grease or line a muffin tin with paper liners. | In a large bowl, combine wheat bran, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. | In another bowl, beat together egg, brown sugar, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract until well blended. | Add the milk to the wet ingredients and stir in the molasses. | Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir just until moistened. | Fold in the raisins gently if using. | Spoon the batter into the prepared muffin cups, filling each about two-thirds full. | Bake in the preheated oven for 15 to 20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. | Let the muffins cool in the tin for a few minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: Bratwurst with Sauerkraut
description: Bratwurst with sauerkraut is a classic German dish featuring flavorful grilled sausages served alongside tangy fermented cabbage cooked with onions and spices.
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium heat and add the bratwurst sausages. | Cook the bratwurst for about 4-5 minutes on each side until evenly browned and cooked through. | Remove the bratwurst from the skillet and keep warm. | In the same skillet, add the butter and allow it to melt. | Add the sliced onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5 minutes. | Add the sauerkraut, caraway seeds, and beer to the skillet. | Stir to combine and simmer uncovered for 10-15 minutes to let the flavors meld and the liquid reduce slightly. | Season with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve the cooked bratwurst on a plate with a generous helping of sauerkraut on the side.

name: Bread Pudding Classic American
description: Classic American bread pudding is a simple, comforting dessert made by soaking bread in a sweet custard mixture and baking until golden and set.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F). | Grease a baking dish with butter or oil. | Cut the bread into cubes and place them in a large mixing bowl. | In another bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla extract, ground cinnamon, and salt until well combined. | Pour the egg mixture over the bread cubes and gently mix to soak all the bread. | Optional: Stir in raisins or other dried fruit if desired. | Let the mixture sit for about 15 minutes to allow the bread to absorb the custard. | Pour the soaked bread mixture into the prepared baking dish and spread evenly. | Bake in the preheated oven for 45 to 55 minutes, or until the pudding is set and the top is golden brown. | Remove from the oven and let cool slightly before serving. | Serve warm, optionally with a drizzle of caramel sauce or a dollop of whipped cream.

name: Bread Pudding New Orleans
description: Traditional New Orleans bread pudding is a warm, comforting dessert made from soaked French bread baked in a rich custard, often served with a sweet bourbon sauce for added flavor.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit (175 degrees Celsius). | Butter a medium-sized baking dish generously. | Tear the French bread into bite-sized pieces and place them in a large mixing bowl. | In a separate bowl, whisk together the eggs, sugar, milk, heavy cream, vanilla extract, cinnamon, and nutmeg until well combined. | Pour the egg mixture over the bread pieces and gently fold to ensure all bread is soaked. | Let the mixture sit for about 10 minutes to absorb the custard. | Add raisins and melted butter to the mixture and stir gently to combine. | Transfer the soaked bread mixture into the prepared baking dish, spreading evenly. | Bake in the preheated oven for 45 to 55 minutes or until the custard is set and the top is golden brown. | While the bread pudding bakes, prepare the bourbon sauce: in a saucepan, melt butter over medium heat, add brown sugar and stir until dissolved. | Slowly pour in the heavy cream and bourbon, stirring continually until the sauce thickens slightly, about 5 minutes. | Remove the bread pudding from the oven and let it cool slightly before serving warm with the bourbon sauce drizzled on top.

name: Bread and Butter Pickles
description: Bread and butter pickles are a sweet and tangy cucumber pickle variety popular in the southern United States, known for their distinctive mustard seed and turmeric flavor.
instructions: Slice cucumbers and onions into thin slices. | In a large bowl, combine sliced cucumbers and onions with salt and let sit for 1 hour to draw out excess water. | Rinse the cucumber and onion mixture and drain well. | In a saucepan, combine vinegar, sugar, mustard seed, celery seed, turmeric, and crushed red pepper, and bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. | Add drained cucumber and onion slices to the hot vinegar mixture and simmer for 5 minutes. | Remove from heat and pack pickles and liquid into sterilized jars while hot. | Seal jars and allow pickles to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate. | Let pickles marinate at least 24 hours before serving for best flavor.

name: Breaded Pork Chops
description: Crispy and flavorful breaded pork chops that are pan-fried to golden perfection and finished in the oven for juiciness.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit (190 degrees Celsius). | Prepare three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten egg, and one with bread crumbs. | Season the pork chops with salt and pepper on both sides. | Dredge each pork chop first in the flour, shaking off the excess. | Dip the pork chop into the beaten egg, ensuring it is fully coated. | Coat the pork chop with bread crumbs, pressing gently to adhere the crumbs well. | Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. | Add the breaded pork chops to the skillet and cook for about 3 minutes on each side until golden brown. | Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and bake for 10-15 minutes or until the pork chops reach an internal temperature of 145 degrees Fahrenheit (63 degrees Celsius). | Remove from the oven and let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Breakfast Burger with Hash Brown
description: A hearty breakfast burger combining a juicy beef patty with melted Cheddar, crispy bacon, a fried egg, and a golden hash brown for a filling and flavorful morning meal.
instructions: Preheat a skillet over medium heat and cook the hash brown according to package instructions until golden and crispy on both sides, then set aside. | Form the ground beef into a patty slightly larger than your burger bun and season both sides with salt and pepper. | In the same skillet, cook the beef patty for about 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium doneness or until desired doneness is reached. | During the last minute of cooking the patty, place a slice of Cheddar cheese on top and cover the skillet to melt the cheese. | In another pan, cook the bacon strips over medium heat until crispy, then drain on paper towels. | Fry the egg sunny side up or to your preferred doneness in a little oil or butter in the skillet. | Toast the burger bun lightly in the skillet or toaster. | Assemble the burger by spreading mayonnaise or ketchup on the bottom bun, adding the beef patty with melted cheese, followed by the crispy bacon, fried egg, and finally the hash brown on top. | Place the top bun over the hash brown and serve immediately while hot.

name: Cat's Tongue Cookie
description: Cat's tongue cookies are thin, crisp, buttery cookies traditionally shaped like a cat's tongue, popular in French and European baking.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper. | In a mixing bowl, cream the butter and sugar together until light and fluffy. | Beat in the egg and vanilla extract until well combined. | Sift the flour and salt together, then gradually add to the wet ingredients, mixing until a smooth batter forms. | Using a piping bag fitted with a plain round nozzle, pipe thin strips of batter onto the prepared baking sheet, about 5 cm long and spaced apart. | Bake in the preheated oven for 8 to 10 minutes or until the edges are golden brown. | Remove the cookies from the oven and allow them to cool on the baking sheet for a few minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely. | Once cooled, the cookies can be served as is or used as a decorative element for desserts.

name: Cauliflower Gratin
description: Cauliflower Gratin is a creamy baked dish combining tender cauliflower with a rich cheese sauce, topped with melted cheese and optionally breadcrumbs for a golden crust. This comforting French-inspired side dish is perfect to accompany a variety of meals.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190 degrees Celsius (375 degrees Fahrenheit). | Cut the cauliflower into florets and steam or boil them until just tender, about 5-7 minutes; drain and set aside. | In a saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat, then whisk in the flour to make a roux, cooking for about 2 minutes without browning. | Slowly add the milk while whisking continuously to create a smooth béchamel sauce; cook until thickened, about 5 minutes. | Remove the sauce from heat and stir in half of the grated cheese along with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg if using, until the cheese is melted and sauce is smooth. | Place the cooked cauliflower in a baking dish and pour the cheese sauce evenly over it. | Sprinkle the remaining cheese on top and optionally add breadcrumbs for extra crunch. | Bake uncovered in the preheated oven for 20-25 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling. | Let the gratin cool for a few minutes before serving.

name: Celeriac Purée
description: Celeriac purée is a smooth and creamy side dish made from celeriac root cooked and blended with butter and cream, offering a delicate and earthy flavor.
instructions: Peel the celeriac and cut it into small cubes. | Place the celeriac cubes in a pot and cover with water, add a pinch of salt. | Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the celeriac is very tender, about 20-25 minutes. | Drain the celeriac well and transfer to a blender or food processor. | Add butter, cream, salt, and pepper to the celeriac. | Blend until smooth and creamy, adjusting seasoning to taste. | If the purée is too thick, add a little warm milk to reach the desired consistency. | Serve warm as a side dish.

name: Celeriac Remoulade
description: Celeriac remoulade is a classic French salad featuring finely shredded celery root dressed in a tangy mayonnaise-based sauce with mustard and capers. It's a refreshing and crunchy side dish that complements many meals.
instructions: Peel the celeriac and cut it into thin matchstick-sized strips using a knife or a mandoline. | Place the celeriac strips in a bowl of cold water with a squeeze of lemon juice to prevent browning. | In a separate bowl, mix together the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, lemon juice, capers, and chopped parsley to create the remoulade sauce. | Drain the celeriac and pat dry with paper towels. | Combine the celeriac strips with the remoulade sauce and mix well to ensure the celeriac is thoroughly coated. | Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. | Chill the remoulade in the refrigerator for at least an hour before serving to allow the flavors to develop.

name: Chantilly Cream
description: Chantilly cream is a classic French sweetened whipped cream flavored with vanilla, perfect for topping desserts and pastries.
instructions: Chill a mixing bowl and whisk or beaters in the refrigerator for at least 15 minutes. | Pour cold heavy cream into the chilled bowl. | Add powdered sugar and vanilla extract to the cream. | Whisk the mixture at medium-high speed until soft peaks form, being careful not to overwhip to avoid turning the cream into butter. | Use immediately or keep refrigerated until ready to serve.

name: Charcutiere Sauce
description: Charcutiere sauce is a classic French sauce made with shallots, white wine, mustard, and chopped cornichons, typically served with grilled or roasted meats.
instructions: Finely chop the shallot. | In a small saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. | Add the chopped shallot and sauté until softened and translucent, about 2-3 minutes. | Pour in the white wine and bring to a simmer, allowing it to reduce by half. | Add the beef stock and continue to simmer until the sauce thickens slightly. | Stir in the Dijon mustard and chopped cornichon. | Season the sauce with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. | Remove from heat and stir in the chopped fresh tarragon. | Serve warm with grilled or roasted meats, especially beef.

name: Charente Butter Cookie
description: Charente butter cookie is a traditional French biscuit renowned for its rich buttery flavor and crisp texture, originating from the Charente region of France.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180 degrees Celsius (350 degrees Fahrenheit). | In a mixing bowl, cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy. | Add the egg yolk and continue mixing until well combined. | Sift in the flour and a pinch of salt, then gently fold the mixture to form a smooth dough. | Transfer the dough onto a lightly floured surface and roll it out to about 0.5 cm thickness. | Cut the dough into desired cookie shapes using a cookie cutter or knife. | Place the cookies on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, spacing them evenly. | Bake in the preheated oven for 12 to 15 minutes or until the edges are lightly golden. | Remove from the oven and let the cookies cool on the baking sheet for a few minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.

name: Chateau Potatoes
description: Chateau Potatoes are classic French pan-fried potatoes shaped into smooth ovals and cooked until golden and crispy, often served as an elegant side dish.
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut them into small, smooth oval shapes about 3-4 cm long, known as chateau shapes. | Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and add the cut potatoes. | Cook the potatoes in boiling water until just tender but still firm, approximately 8-10 minutes. | Drain the potatoes well and let them dry on a clean kitchen towel. | In a large skillet, heat butter and olive oil over medium heat. | Add the parboiled potatoes and sauté them, turning frequently to brown all sides evenly and create a golden crust. | Season with salt and pepper to taste while sautéing. | Once the potatoes are evenly browned and crisp on the outside and tender inside, remove them from the heat. | Sprinkle with freshly chopped parsley before serving to add color and flavor.

name: Cheese Fondue
description: Cheese fondue is a classic Swiss melted cheese dish served in a communal pot, perfect for dipping bread and vegetables and sharing socially.
instructions: Grate the cheese and toss it with the cornstarch to coat evenly. | Rub the inside of a fondue pot or heavy saucepan with the cut side of the garlic clove, then discard the garlic. | Pour the white wine into the pot and heat over medium heat until hot but not boiling. | Gradually add the cheese mixture to the wine, stirring constantly in a figure-eight motion until the cheese is melted and smooth. | Add the lemon juice, kirsch, and a pinch of nutmeg and pepper, stirring to combine. | Reduce the heat to low and keep the fondue warm and smooth, stirring occasionally. | Serve immediately with cubed bread and vegetable pieces for dipping.

name: Cheese Matchstick Pastries
description: Cheese Matchstick Pastries are crispy, golden puff pastry strips topped with melted Cheddar cheese, perfect as a savory snack or appetizer.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Roll out the puff pastry sheet on a lightly floured surface into a rectangle about 3 mm thick. | Spread the grated cheese evenly over the entire surface of the pastry. | Cut the pastry lengthwise into thin strips, about 1 cm wide, to create the 'matchsticks'. | Place the strips on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, spacing them slightly apart. | Bake in the preheated oven for 10 to 15 minutes or until the pastries are golden brown and crispy. | Remove from the oven and let cool slightly on a wire rack before serving.

name: Chicken and Leek Pie
description: Chicken and Leek Pie is a comforting British savory pie featuring tender chicken breast and softened leeks in a creamy sauce, encased in golden puff pastry.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F). | In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat and sauté chopped leek until softened. | Add diced chicken breast to the skillet and cook until no longer pink. | Sprinkle flour over the chicken and leek mixture and stir well to combine. | Gradually pour in chicken broth and milk while stirring, cooking until the sauce thickens. | Season the mixture with salt, pepper, and dried thyme. | Transfer the chicken and leek filling into a pie dish. | Roll out the puff pastry to cover the pie dish and place it over the filling, trimming excess pastry. | Cut a small slit in the pastry to allow steam to escape and brush the top with beaten egg. | Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown. | Remove from the oven and let the pie rest for a few minutes before serving.

name: Chicken and Mushroom Stew Greek-style
description: A hearty Greek-style chicken and mushroom stew flavored with herbs and tomato paste, simmered in white wine and chicken broth for tender, savory results.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. | Add chopped onion and garlic and sauté until softened. | Add chicken pieces and brown them on all sides. | Add chopped mushroom and cook until they release their moisture. | Stir in tomato paste, dried oregano, and dried thyme, cooking for a minute to combine flavors. | Pour in white wine and let it reduce slightly. | Add chicken broth and bring the mixture to a simmer. | Cover and cook for 30 minutes, until chicken is tender. | Season with salt and black pepper to taste. | Stir in chopped fresh parsley just before serving.

name: Chicken and Orzo One-pot
description: This Chicken and Orzo One-Pot is a simple and flavorful dish where tender chicken cooks together with orzo pasta in a savory broth, making for an easy and comforting meal.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. | Add chicken pieces and cook until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. | Remove chicken from the pot and set aside. | In the same pot, add chopped onion and garlic, sauté until translucent and fragrant. | Add diced tomato and cook for 2 minutes. | Pour in chicken broth and bring to a simmer. | Add orzo pasta to the pot, stir to combine. | Return the chicken pieces to the pot, cover, and simmer on low heat for 15-20 minutes until the orzo is tender and the chicken is cooked through. | Season with salt, pepper, and chopped parsley. | Serve hot, garnished with additional parsley if desired.

name: Chicken and Potato Lemon Bake
description: A simple and flavorful baked chicken dish layered with tender lemon-infused potatoes, perfect for a hearty family meal.
