instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F). | Peel and thinly slice the potato into rounds. | Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper on all sides. | In a baking dish, arrange a layer of potato slices, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and drizzle with olive oil. | Place the chicken pieces on top of the potatoes. | Sprinkle minced garlic and chopped rosemary evenly over the chicken and potatoes. | Pour fresh lemon juice and white wine over the chicken and potatoes. | Scatter lemon slices over the top for extra flavor and decoration. | Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil and bake in the preheated oven for 35 minutes. | Remove the foil and bake for an additional 15 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are tender and golden. | Remove from the oven and let rest for a few minutes before serving.

name: Chicken and Rice Pilaf
description: Chicken and Rice Pilaf is a flavorful, one-pot dish featuring tender chicken and aromatic rice cooked together with herbs and broth, offering a comforting meal popular in many cuisines.
instructions: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for 20 minutes and drain. | Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and sauté chopped onion until translucent. | Add minced garlic and cook for an additional minute until fragrant. | Add the chicken pieces and cook until they are browned on all sides. | Stir in the drained rice and toast it lightly with the chicken and onions for about 2 minutes. | Pour in chicken broth, add salt, pepper, and dried thyme, then bring to a boil. | Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 20 minutes or until the rice is cooked and the liquid is absorbed. | Remove from heat and let it rest, covered, for 5 minutes. | Fluff the rice with a fork, garnish with chopped parsley, and serve hot.

name: Chicken with Artichokes Avgolemono
description: Chicken with Artichokes Avgolemono is a traditional Greek dish featuring chicken cooked in a tangy lemon-egg sauce with tender artichokes, creating a comforting and flavorful meal.
instructions: Place chicken pieces in a large pot and cover with water or chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until chicken is tender, about 40 minutes. | Remove chicken from broth and set aside to cool. Strain the broth and reserve about 4 cups for the soup. | While broth simmers, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add sliced artichoke hearts and chopped onion, cook until soft and lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes. | Season with salt and pepper. Add artichokes and onion to the reserved broth and simmer together for 10 minutes. | Shred the cooled chicken into bite-sized pieces, discarding skin and bones. | In a bowl, whisk egg yolks and lemon juice until smooth. | Temper the egg-lemon mixture by slowly whisking in about 1 cup of hot broth to avoid curdling. | Gradually stir the tempered mixture back into the pot with the broth, artichokes, and onion. | Add the shredded chicken to the soup and heat gently on low, stirring frequently, until warmed through but not boiling, about 5 minutes. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley if desired.

name: Chicken with Eggplant and Feta Bake
description: A flavorful baked dish combining tender chicken, roasted eggplant, and tangy feta cheese, typical of Mediterranean cuisine.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F). | Slice the eggplant into 1 cm thick rounds and sprinkle with salt. Let sit for 15 minutes, then pat dry to remove excess moisture and bitterness. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add chicken pieces and cook until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside. | In the same skillet, add more olive oil if needed and sauté chopped onion and garlic until soft and translucent. | Add diced tomato and cook for 5 minutes until they start to soften. | Layer half of the eggplant slices in the bottom of a baking dish. | Place the browned chicken pieces on top of the eggplant layer. | Spread the tomato, onion, and garlic mixture evenly over the chicken. | Layer the remaining eggplant slices on top. | Sprinkle the crumbled feta cheese evenly over the top. | Drizzle with olive oil and season with black pepper and a pinch of salt. | Cover the baking dish with foil and bake in the oven for 30 minutes. | Remove the foil and bake for an additional 10-15 minutes until the eggplant is tender and the cheese is golden. | Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Chicken with Fennel and Olives
description: A flavorful Mediterranean-inspired dish combining tender roasted chicken with aromatic fennel and briny green olives, enhanced by fresh herbs and garlic.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). | Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium heat. | Add the chicken pieces skin side down and cook until golden brown, about 5 minutes, then flip and cook 3 minutes on the other side. | Remove the chicken and set aside. | In the same skillet, add sliced fennel and chopped garlic, sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. | Add green olives and chopped fresh thyme, stir to combine. | Return the chicken to the skillet, nestling it among the fennel and olives. | Pour chicken broth over the mixture. | Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and roast for 25-30 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the fennel is tender. | Remove from oven, garnish with fresh parsley, and serve warm.

name: Chicken with Green Beans and Tomato
description: A simple and healthy dish featuring tender chicken simmered with fresh green beans and ripe tomatoes, flavored with garlic and herbs.
instructions: Rinse the chicken pieces and pat dry with paper towels. | Trim the ends of the green beans and rinse them under cold water. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. | Add the chicken pieces to the skillet, season with salt and pepper, and cook until golden brown on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. | Remove the chicken from the skillet and set aside. | In the same skillet, add minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. | Add chopped tomato to the skillet and cook for 3-4 minutes until softened. | Return the chicken to the skillet, then add the green beans. | Pour in chicken broth to cover the ingredients halfway, then bring to a simmer. | Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the green beans are tender. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve the chicken with green beans and tomatoes on a plate and garnish with fresh parsley.

name: Chicken with Okra
description: Kotopoulo me Bamies is a traditional Greek dish featuring tender chicken simmered with fresh okra and tomatoes, offering a hearty and flavorful meal.
instructions: Preheat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat. | Season chicken pieces with salt and pepper, then brown them in the hot oil until golden on all sides. Remove and set aside. | In the same pan, sauté chopped onion until translucent. | Add minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Stir in diced tomato and tomato paste, cooking until the tomato softens and the mixture thickens slightly. | Add the browned chicken back to the pan and pour in chicken broth to cover the chicken halfway. | Add cleaned okra pods to the mixture, stir gently. | Season with salt, pepper, and dried oregano. | Cover the pan and simmer on low heat for about 40 minutes or until the chicken is tender and cooked through, and the okra is soft but not mushy. | Uncover and cook for a few more minutes to thicken the sauce if necessary. | Garnish with freshly chopped parsley before serving.

name: Carta Di Musica
description: Carta di Musica is a traditional Italian thin crispbread known for its delicate crisp texture. It is commonly served as a side or appetizer accompaniment in Italian cuisine.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F). | In a mixing bowl, combine the all-purpose flour and salt. | Add the olive oil and gradually mix in the water to form a smooth, elastic dough. | Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for about 5 minutes until smooth. | Divide the dough into small portions and roll each portion out very thinly on parchment paper. | Transfer the rolled dough on the parchment papers to baking sheets. | Brush the dough lightly with olive oil and sprinkle with a pinch of salt and optional rosemary leaves if desired. | Bake in the preheated oven for 5-7 minutes until crisp and golden at the edges. | Remove from the oven and let cool on a wire rack to achieve maximum crispness. | Serve as a delicate crispbread accompaniment to soups, salads, or appetizers.

name: Cartellate Pugliesi
description: Cartellate Pugliesi are traditional fried pastries from the Puglia region of Italy, shaped into decorative bows and coated with a sweet honey syrup, offering a delightful crunchy and sweet treat.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, white wine, olive oil, salt, and lemon zest to form a firm dough. | Knead the dough on a floured surface for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then cover it and let it rest for 30 minutes. | Divide the dough into small portions and roll each portion into thin strips about 1 inch wide. | Cut each strip into rectangles approximately 3 inches long, then fold each rectangle lengthwise to form a bow shape by pinching the edges in the center. | Heat sunflower oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat until hot. | Fry the shaped cartellate in batches until golden and crispy, about 2-3 minutes per side, then drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. | In a small saucepan, heat honey and sugar together gently until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is smooth. | Dip the fried cartellate into the warm honey syrup, ensuring they are well coated. | Place the coated pastries on a wire rack to set and cool before serving.

name: Casarecce with Swordfish
description: Casarecce with Swordfish is an Italian seafood pasta dish featuring tender swordfish cubes sautéed with garlic, tomatoes, olives, and capers, tossed with casarecce pasta for a fresh and flavorful meal.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook casarecce pasta until al dente, then drain and set aside, reserving some pasta water. | Cut swordfish into bite-sized cubes and season with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and sauté chopped garlic until fragrant. | Add swordfish cubes to the skillet and cook until golden brown and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes per side. | Stir in chopped cherry tomato and cook until softened. | Add chopped black olives and capers, stirring to combine. | Pour in white wine and let it reduce slightly, about 2 minutes. | Add freshly chopped parsley and chili flakes, stirring well. | Add cooked casarecce pasta to the skillet and toss to coat with the sauce, adding reserved pasta water if needed to loosen. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve hot, garnished with more fresh parsley if desired.

name: Casatiello Napoletano
description: Casatiello Napoletano is a traditional Neapolitan savory Easter bread filled with cured meats, cheeses, and hard-boiled eggs, celebrated for its rich flavor and festive presentation.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, salt, sugar, and dry yeast. Mix well. | Gradually add the lukewarm water and olive oil to the dry ingredients, kneading to form a smooth, elastic dough. | Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place until it doubles in size, about 1 to 2 hours. | Preheat the oven to 180°C (356°F). | On a floured surface, roll out the dough into a rectangle about 1 cm thick. | Evenly distribute diced salami, cubed provolone cheese, grated pecorino romano, and sliced hard-boiled eggs over the dough. | Roll the dough tightly into a log and then form it into a ring shape, pinching the ends to seal it. | Place the dough ring into a greased round baking pan. | Insert several whole peeled cloves of garlic at intervals into the dough ring. | Let the shaped dough rest and rise for another 30 minutes. | Brush the top of the dough with beaten egg for a glossy finish. | Bake in the preheated oven for 40 to 50 minutes, or until golden brown and cooked through. | Remove from the oven and let it cool slightly before slicing and serving.

name: Casoncelli Alla Bergamasca
description: Casoncelli alla Bergamasca is a traditional stuffed pasta from Bergamo, Italy, featuring a savory filling of mixed meats, amaretti biscuit, and aromatic herbs, typically served with butter and sage sauce.
instructions: Prepare the pasta dough by mixing flour and eggs until a smooth, elastic dough forms. Wrap in plastic wrap and let rest for 30 minutes. | For the filling, finely chop the beef, pork, garlic, parsley, and amaretti biscuits. | In a skillet, sauté the beef and pork with a little olive oil until cooked through. Let cool. | In a bowl, combine the cooked meat mixture, chopped garlic, parsley, grated Parmesan, crushed amaretti biscuits, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix well to create a uniform filling. | Roll out the pasta dough into thin sheets on a floured surface. | Cut the dough into oval shapes approximately 7 cm by 5 cm. | Place a small spoonful of filling in the center of each oval. | Fold the dough over the filling to form a half-moon shape, then press the edges together, creating a slightly twisted, pointed end. | Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. | Cook the casoncelli in boiling water for about 3 to 4 minutes or until they float to the surface. | Drain the pasta, reserving some cooking water. | In a pan, melt butter and sauté sage leaves until fragrant. | Add the cooked casoncelli to the pan with butter and sage, tossing gently to coat and warm through. Add a little pasta water if needed to keep moist. | Serve immediately with grated Parmesan cheese sprinkled on top.

name: Cassata Al Forno
description: Cassata al Forno is a traditional Sicilian baked ricotta cheese cake, enriched with candied fruits and dark chocolate, offering a creamy and flavorful dessert.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Line a 22 cm (9-inch) round cake pan with parchment paper and lightly butter the sides. | In a large bowl, mix together the ricotta cheese and powdered sugar until smooth and creamy. | Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. | Gently fold in the candied fruit, chopped chocolate, and lemon zest. | Pour the mixture into the prepared cake pan and smooth the top. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 45 minutes, or until the cake is set and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. | Remove the cake from the oven and let it cool in the pan for 15 minutes, then transfer it to a wire rack to cool completely. | Once cooled, dust the top with a little powdered sugar if desired before serving.

name: Cassata Gelata
description: Cassata Gelata is a traditional Sicilian frozen dessert made with creamy sweetened ricotta, candied fruits, chocolate chips, and soaked sponge cake, offering a refreshing and rich cake-like treat.
instructions: Line a loaf pan with plastic wrap, leaving an overhang for easy removal later. | Drain the ricotta in a fine sieve or cheesecloth for a few hours to remove excess moisture. | In a bowl, combine the drained ricotta with powdered sugar and vanilla extract, mixing until smooth. | Chop candied orange peel, citron, and glacé cherries into small pieces and fold into the ricotta mixture along with mini chocolate chips. | In a separate shallow dish, dip sponge cake slices briefly into a liqueur mixture made with Marsala wine and a little orange juice. | Arrange a layer of soaked sponge cake slices at the bottom of the prepared pan. | Spread half of the ricotta mixture over the sponge cake layer evenly. | Add another layer of soaked sponge cake slices on top. | Spread the remaining ricotta mixture over the second sponge cake layer, smoothing the top. | Cover the pan with plastic wrap and freeze for at least 6 hours or overnight until firm. | Before serving, unmold the cassata by lifting the plastic wrap from the pan and transfer it to a serving plate. | Optionally, decorate the top with extra candied fruit pieces, chopped pistachios, or whipped cream. | Slice carefully and serve chilled.

name: Cassata Siciliana
description: Cassata Siciliana is a traditional Sicilian layered dessert featuring ricotta cheese, sponge cake, and candied fruits, celebrated for its richness and vibrant decoration.
instructions: Line a round cake pan with plastic wrap, leaving extra overhang to cover the top later. | Slice the sponge cake horizontally to create thin layers. | Cut the sponge cake layers into rounds matching the pan size. | Soak the sponge cake rounds lightly with a simple syrup (made from sugar and water). | In a large bowl, combine ricotta cheese, powdered sugar, and chopped candied fruit, mixing until smooth. | Fold in chopped chocolate and a splash of liqueur (optional). | Spread a layer of ricotta mixture over the bottom of the lined pan. | Place a soaked sponge cake round over the ricotta layer and press gently. | Repeat layering with remaining ricotta mixture and sponge cake rounds, finishing with a sponge cake layer on top. | Cover the top with the overhanging plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight, allowing it to set. | To serve, invert the cassata onto a serving plate and remove the plastic wrap. | Decorate the top and sides with more candied fruit and chopped pistachios as desired.

name: Cassatelle Siciliane
description: Cassatelle Siciliane are traditional Sicilian fried pastries filled with sweet ricotta, chocolate, and candied orange peel, offering a delightful balance of creamy and crispy textures.
instructions: Mix the ricotta with sugar, chopped chocolate, and finely chopped candied orange peel until evenly combined. | Roll out the dough on a floured surface to about 3 mm thickness and cut into circles approximately 10 cm in diameter. | Place a spoonful of the ricotta mixture in the center of each dough circle, fold over to form a half-moon shape, and press the edges firmly to seal, crimping with a fork if desired. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan to 175°C (350°F). | Fry the cassatelle in batches until golden and crisp, about 3-4 minutes per side, turning carefully. | Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. | Once cooled, dust generously with powdered sugar before serving.

name: Castagnaccio
description: Castagnaccio is a traditional Tuscan chestnut flour cake, naturally gluten-free and flavored with pine nuts, raisins, walnuts, and fresh rosemary, offering a rustic, earthy sweet treat.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | In a large bowl, sift the chestnut flour to remove lumps. | Gradually add water to the chestnut flour while stirring continuously until you obtain a smooth, thin batter similar to pancake batter consistency. | Add olive oil, a pinch of salt, and mix well. | Pour the batter into a lightly greased round baking pan, spreading it evenly. | Sprinkle the pine nuts, raisins, and chopped walnuts evenly over the batter surface. | Add fresh rosemary leaves on top as garnish. | Drizzle a little olive oil over the top of the batter. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 40-45 minutes, until the surface is dry and a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. | Remove from oven, allow to cool slightly, then cut into slices and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Ebi Tempura
description: Ebi Tempura is a classic Japanese dish featuring shrimp coated in a light, crispy batter and deep-fried to golden perfection, often served as an appetizer or side dish.
instructions: Start by peeling the shrimp, leaving the tails intact, then devein and make shallow cuts on the belly side to prevent curling during frying. | Pat the shrimp dry with paper towels and set aside. | In a mixing bowl, combine cold water and egg yolk, mixing lightly. | Add cake flour and cornstarch to the egg mixture and gently mix with chopsticks or fork until just combined; the batter should be lumpy and cold. Do not overmix. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan to 170-180°C (340-355°F). | Lightly dust the prepared shrimp with flour to help the batter adhere. | Dip each shrimp into the batter, then carefully place it into the hot oil, frying a few pieces at a time to avoid overcrowding. | Fry until the batter is golden and shrimp are cooked through, about 2-3 minutes, turning if necessary. | Remove the shrimp tempura with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. | Serve immediately with tentsuyu dipping sauce or a sprinkle of salt.

name: Ebiten
description: Ebiten is a Japanese appetizer featuring shrimp coated in a light, crispy tempura batter and fried on a skewer, perfect for dipping and sharing.
instructions: Peel the shrimp, leaving the tail intact, and devein them by making a shallow cut along the back and removing the vein. | Make small incisions on the undersides of the shrimp to straighten them and prevent curling during frying. | Prepare the tempura batter by mixing chilled water with tempura flour gently; do not overmix to keep it light and airy. | Skewer each shrimp onto a bamboo stick lengthwise to create the tempura stick shape. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or a deep pan to 180°C (356°F). | Dip each skewered shrimp into the tempura batter, allowing excess batter to drip off. | Carefully lower the battered shrimp sticks into the hot oil and fry until they turn golden and crispy, about 2-3 minutes. | Remove the fried shrimp tempura sticks from the oil and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. | Serve the Ebiten sticks hot with tentsuyu sauce or preferred dipping sauce.

name: Echizen Oroshi Soba
alias: Grated Daikon Radish Soba from Fukui
description: Echizen Oroshi Soba is a traditional Japanese dish from Fukui prefecture featuring cold buckwheat noodles served with refreshing grated daikon radish and a flavorful dipping sauce. This simple yet delicious dish highlights the natural flavors and is especially popular in summer.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and cook the soba noodles according to the package instructions until al dente. | Drain the cooked soba noodles and rinse them under cold running water to stop cooking and remove excess starch. Set aside. | Peel and finely grate the daikon radish to prepare oroshi (grated daikon). | Prepare the dipping sauce by mixing soy sauce, mirin, and dashi stock in a bowl. Adjust the taste as preferred. | Divide the soba noodles into serving portions and place on individual plates. | Top each portion of soba noodles with a generous amount of grated daikon. | Pour the dipping sauce into small separate bowls for each diner. | Garnish the soba with thinly sliced green onion and a small amount of wasabi if desired. | To eat, dip the soba noodles with grated daikon into the sauce and enjoy.

name: Edamame
description: Edamame are young, green soybean pods boiled and salted, served as a healthy and popular Japanese snack or appetizer.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add a pinch of salt. | Add the edamame pods to the boiling water and cook for 5 minutes until tender but still firm. | Drain the edamame and immediately rinse under cold water to stop the cooking process. | Sprinkle with sea salt or kosher salt to taste. | Serve warm or at room temperature by squeezing the beans out of the pods with your fingers or teeth.

name: Edamame Potage
description: Edamame potage is a creamy Japanese-inspired soup made from pureed edamame beans, offering a nutritious and velvety texture with a fresh green flavor.
instructions: Shell the edamame and rinse under cold water. | In a medium pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. | Add the chopped onion and garlic, and sauté until translucent and fragrant. | Add the shelled edamame, vegetable broth, salt, and pepper to the pot. | Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until the edamame is tender. | Use an immersion blender or transfer to a blender to puree the soup until smooth and creamy. | Return to pot if needed, adjust seasoning with salt and pepper, and warm through. | Serve hot, garnished with a swirl of cream and a sprinkle of chopped chives if desired.

name: Edo-mae Sushi
description: Edo-Mae Sushi is a traditional Tokyo-style sushi featuring vinegared rice topped with fresh fish or other toppings, emphasizing simplicity and freshness, served with classic condiments.
instructions: Rinse sushi rice under cold water until water runs clear. | Cook the sushi rice according to package instructions or in a rice cooker with appropriate water ratio. | While the rice cooks, prepare sushi vinegar by combining rice vinegar, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan and heating gently until dissolved; then let cool. | Once the rice is cooked, transfer it to a wooden or non-metallic bowl and evenly pour the sushi vinegar over the hot rice. | Fold the rice gently using a spatula to mix and cool it quickly, fanning the rice simultaneously to give it a shiny texture. | Prepare fillings and toppings by slicing fresh fish such as tuna, salmon, and eel into thin slices. | Lightly grill the eel with unagi sauce if desired, and prepare any other toppings like tamago (sweet egg omelette) sliced thinly. | Wet your hands with a mixture of water and a little rice vinegar to prevent sticking, then take a small amount of rice and shape it into an oval mound. | Place a slice of fish or topping on top of the rice mound, pressing lightly to adhere. | Optionally, apply a small dab of wasabi between the rice and fish for authentic flavor. | Serve the sushi immediately with soy sauce, pickled ginger, and wasabi on the side. | Enjoy the sushi fresh, ideally within the day of preparation for best taste and safety.

name: Egg Tofu Soup
description: Egg Tofu Soup is a light, comforting Chinese soup featuring soft egg tofu cubes and silky egg ribbons in a savory broth, garnished with fresh green onion.
instructions: Cut the egg tofu into small cubes and set aside. | Beat the eggs in a bowl until smooth. | Heat vegetable oil in a pot over medium heat. | Add minced garlic and sauté until fragrant. | Pour the beaten eggs into the pot and gently stir to form soft curds. | Add vegetable broth and bring to a gentle boil. | Add the egg tofu cubes into the soup and simmer for 3-5 minutes. | Season the soup with salt and white pepper to taste. | Garnish with chopped green onion before serving.

name: Ehomaki
description: Ehomaki is a traditional Japanese sushi roll eaten during Setsubun for good luck, filled with seven ingredients symbolizing good fortune and rolled in nori seaweed.
instructions: Prepare sushi rice by rinsing 300 g of short-grain rice until water runs clear, then cook with 360 ml of water until done and let it cool. | Mix 60 ml of rice vinegar, 25 g of sugar, and 5 g of salt in a small bowl until dissolved, then gently fold into the cooled rice to season it evenly. | Place a bamboo sushi mat on a flat surface and lay a sheet of nori seaweed shiny side down. | Spread a thin, even layer of sushi rice over the nori, leaving a 2 cm border at the top edge. | Arrange the fillings in a horizontal line near the bottom edge of the rice: 75 g of cucumber strips, 75 g of kanpyo (dried gourd) rehydrated and simmered in soy sauce and sugar, 75 g of tamagoyaki (Japanese rolled omelette) cut into strips, 50 g of cooked eel, 75 g of shiitake mushroom simmered in soy sauce and sugar, and 50 g of oboro (seasoned fish flakes). | Using the bamboo mat, carefully roll the sushi from the bottom edge, tucking in the fillings tightly, and roll until the nori seals the roll. | Wrap the roll in plastic wrap and let it rest for 10 minutes to maintain shape. | Cut the roll into 6-8 equal slices using a sharp, wet knife to prevent sticking. | Serve the ehomaki whole or sliced, and eat facing the lucky direction for the year while making a silent wish.

name: Ehou Maki
description: Ehou Maki, known as Fortune Roll, is a traditional Japanese sushi roll eaten during the Setsubun festival for good luck and fortune. It features an uncut thick roll filled with various ingredients symbolizing prosperity.
instructions: Prepare sushi rice by rinsing 250 g of sushi rice until water runs clear, then cook it with 300 ml of water. Once cooked, mix the rice gently with 50 ml of rice vinegar, 20 g of sugar, and 5 g of salt, then let it cool to room temperature. | Lay a bamboo sushi rolling mat on a flat surface and place a sheet of nori (seaweed) shiny side down on the mat. | With wet hands, spread an even layer of sushi rice (about 150 g) over the nori, leaving a 2 cm margin at the top edge. | Place the fillings in a line along one edge of the rice covered nori: 50 g of cooked eel, 30 g of tamagoyaki (Japanese sweet omelette) strips, 20 g of cucumber strips, 20 g of carrot strips, and 15 g of pickled gourd (takuan). | Carefully roll the sushi using the bamboo mat, applying gentle pressure to keep the roll tight and compact, ensuring the fillings are enclosed. | Seal the edge of the roll with a little water and wrap the roll tightly using the bamboo mat. Let it rest for a few minutes to firm up. | Using a sharp knife, slice the roll into 6 equal pieces by cutting cleanly without crushing the roll. | Serve the rolls with soy sauce, wasabi, and pickled ginger on the side.

name: Ekiben
description: Ekiben is a traditional Japanese station bento box featuring rice, tamagoyaki, chicken teriyaki, pickled vegetables, and other regional delicacies. It is specially designed for eating on train journeys and offers a flavorful and balanced meal.
instructions: Cook the Japanese short-grain rice according to package instructions until tender and slightly sticky. | Season the cooked rice with a little rice vinegar, sugar, and salt, then let it cool slightly. | Prepare the tamagoyaki: whisk eggs with soy sauce and a bit of sugar, then cook in a rectangular pan in thin layers, rolling each as it cooks to form a rolled omelet. Slice into bite-sized pieces. | Cook the chicken teriyaki: marinate chicken thigh pieces in soy sauce, mirin, and sugar for 15 minutes, then pan-fry until cooked through and glaze with the marinade. | Prepare pickled vegetables by slicing cucumber and daikon radish thinly, then soak in a mixture of rice vinegar, sugar, and salt for 30 minutes. | Assemble the bento box by placing a portion of rice, topped or accompanied by the tamagoyaki, chicken teriyaki, pickled vegetables, and a few steamed vegetables such as broccoli or green beans. | Add a small serving of umeboshi (pickled plum) on the rice for traditional flavor and preservation. | Optionally, include a portion of grilled salmon or a small piece of fried fish for variety. | Pack all components neatly into a compartmentalized box, ready for eating on a train journey.

name: Capirotada
description: Capirotada is a traditional Mexican bread pudding served during Lent, featuring layers of toasted bread, nuts, cheese, raisins, and a spiced piloncillo syrup that creates a sweet, rich flavor.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Slice the bread into thick slices and toast them in the oven until golden and crispy; set aside. | In a saucepan, combine piloncillo (or dark brown sugar), water, cinnamon sticks, and cloves. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes to make the syrup. | Remove cinnamon sticks and cloves from the syrup. | Butter a baking dish and layer toasted bread slices at the bottom. | Sprinkle chopped nuts (such as pecans and peanuts), shredded cheese, and raisins evenly over the bread layer. | Pour some of the warm piloncillo syrup over the layers to moisten them. | Repeat the layering process (bread, nuts, cheese, raisins, syrup) until the ingredients are used up, finishing with a layer of bread and syrup on top. | Bake the assembled capirotada in the oven for 30-40 minutes until the top is bubbling and golden. | Allow the capirotada to cool slightly before serving; it can be served warm or at room temperature.

name: Carlota De Limón
description: Carlota de Limón is a no-bake Mexican lime-flavored dessert featuring layers of lime-infused cream and graham crackers, chilled to set into a refreshing and tangy treat.
instructions: In a medium bowl, whisk together sweetened condensed milk and fresh lime juice until smooth and slightly thickened. | In a separate large bowl, beat heavy cream with vanilla extract until stiff peaks form. | Gently fold the lime-condensed milk mixture into the whipped cream until well combined, being careful to maintain the airy texture. | Line a loaf pan or mold with plastic wrap, leaving excess hanging over the sides for easy removal. | Arrange a layer of whole graham crackers or marie biscuits at the bottom of the pan, breaking as needed to fit. | Spread a layer of the lime cream mixture over the crackers evenly. | Repeat layering with more crackers and cream until all mixture is used, finishing with a cream layer on top. | Cover the top with plastic wrap and refrigerate the charlotte for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, to allow it to set and the flavors to meld. | To serve, gently lift the charlotte out of the pan using the plastic wrap, place on a serving plate, and remove the plastic. | Optionally garnish the top with thin lime slices or lime zest before slicing and serving.

name: Carne Asada
description: Carne Asada is a traditional Mexican dish featuring marinated and grilled flank steak, known for its smoky, citrusy, and spiced flavor profile, perfect for tacos or as a main entree.
instructions: Combine lime juice, olive oil, garlic, cilantro, cumin, oregano, salt, black pepper, and chili powder in a bowl to prepare the marinade. | Place flank steak in a shallow dish or resealable plastic bag and pour the marinade over the meat, making sure it is well coated. | Cover the dish or seal the bag and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, preferably 4 hours or overnight, for the flavors to infuse. | Preheat the grill to high heat and oil the grates to prevent sticking. | Remove the steak from the marinade and shake off excess liquid. | Grill the steak for about 4 to 6 minutes per side for medium-rare, or cook longer to desired doneness. | Transfer the steak to a cutting board and let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing. | Slice the steak thinly against the grain and serve with warm tortillas, salsa, and optional toppings.

name: Carne Asada Burrito
description: Carne Asada Burrito is a flavorful Mexican dish featuring marinated grilled steak wrapped in a flour tortilla with rice, beans, and fresh toppings.
instructions: Marinate the steak by combining lime juice, olive oil, garlic, cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper in a bowl, then coat the steak and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes. | Preheat a grill or grill pan over high heat and cook the steak for 4-5 minutes per side until desired doneness is reached. | Remove the steak from the grill and let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing thinly against the grain. | Warm the flour tortilla on the grill or in a skillet until pliable. | Place the sliced carne asada in the center of the tortilla. | Add toppings such as cooked rice, black beans, chopped cilantro, diced onion, sliced avocado, and sour cream if desired. | Fold the sides of the tortilla and roll it up tightly to form a burrito. | Serve the burrito with salsa or hot sauce on the side.

name: Carne Asada Tampiqueña
description: Carne Asada Tampiqueña is a traditional Mexican dish featuring grilled marinated skirt steak served with white rice, refried beans, and warm flour tortillas, popular in the Tampico region.
instructions: Prepare the marinade by mixing olive oil, lime juice, minced garlic, salt, black pepper, dried oregano, and ground cumin in a bowl. | Place the skirt steak in a shallow dish and pour the marinade over it, ensuring the meat is well coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight. | Preheat the grill to medium-high heat. | Remove the steak from the marinade and grill it for about 4-5 minutes per side or until desired doneness is reached. | While the steak grills, soak the white rice in water for 10 minutes, then cook it with water and a pinch of salt until tender. | Heat the refried beans in a saucepan over medium heat until warmed through. | Warm the flour tortillas on the grill or in a pan until soft and pliable. | Slice the grilled steak across the grain into thin strips. | Arrange the sliced steak on a serving plate alongside portions of white rice, warmed refried beans, and flour tortillas. | Garnish with a sprig of fresh parsley and serve with lime wedges and a side of pico de gallo or salsa if desired.

name: Carne Con Chile
description: Carne con Chile is a traditional Mexican dish featuring tender beef slow-cooked in a rich, flavorful chile sauce made from dried chiles and aromatic spices.
instructions: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes and set aside. | Toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant, about 2 minutes, then remove stems and seeds. | Soak the toasted chiles in hot water for 15 minutes until softened, then blend with garlic, onion, cumin, oregano, and a little soaking water until smooth to make the chile sauce. | Heat vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. | Brown the beef cubes in batches until they develop a nice crust, then remove and set aside. | In the same pan, sauté diced onion and minced garlic until translucent. | Pour in the chile sauce and cook for 5 minutes to deepen the flavors, stirring frequently. | Return the browned beef to the pan and add beef broth to cover the meat slightly. | Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for about 1.5 to 2 hours until the beef is tender. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh cilantro if desired.

name: Carne Con Nopales
description: Carne con Nopales is a traditional Mexican dish featuring tender beef cooked with nopales (edible cactus pads), seasoned with fresh vegetables and herbs for a flavorful and nutritious meal.
instructions: Rinse the nopales pads under cold water to remove the sticky sap, then cut them into small strips. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and add the chopped onion and garlic, sautéing until softened. | Add the beef strips to the skillet and cook until browned on all sides. | Stir in the chopped nopales, diced tomatoes, chopped jalapeno, and mix well. | Season with salt, black pepper, and chopped cilantro, then cover and cook for about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender and nopales are cooked. | Adjust seasoning to taste and serve hot, garnished with extra cilantro if desired.

name: Carne Con Papas
description: Carne con Papas is a traditional Latin American stew featuring tender beef simmered with potatoes in a flavorful broth of tomatoes, cumin, and paprika, garnished with fresh cilantro.
instructions: Peel and dice the potato into medium-sized cubes. | Cut the beef into bite-sized pieces and season with salt and pepper. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat and brown the beef pieces on all sides, then remove and set aside. | In the same skillet, add diced onion and minced garlic; sauté until translucent and fragrant. | Add diced tomatoes and cook for a few minutes until they start to break down. | Return the beef to the skillet and pour in beef broth to cover the meat partially. | Add the diced potatoes to the skillet and stir to combine. | Season with cumin and paprika, and add salt and pepper to taste. | Cover and simmer on low heat for about 45 minutes, or until beef and potatoes are tender. | Garnish with chopped fresh cilantro before serving.

name: Carne Con Rajas
description: Carne con Rajas is a traditional Mexican dish combining tender strips of beef with smoky roasted poblano pepper strips, sautéed with onions for a flavorful and colorful main course.
instructions: Slice the beef into thin strips. | Roast the poblano peppers over an open flame or in the oven until the skin blisters. Place them in a covered bowl to steam for 10 minutes. | Peel the charred skin off the poblano peppers, remove the seeds, and slice them into strips. | Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. | Add the sliced beef to the skillet and cook until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. | Add the sliced poblano strips and sliced onion to the skillet with the beef. | Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion is translucent and the peppers are tender, about 5 minutes. | Add salt and pepper to taste and stir well to combine. | Serve hot with warm corn tortillas or rice.

name: Carne Deshebrada
description: Carne Deshebrada is a traditional Mexican dish featuring slow-cooked shredded beef seasoned with aromatic spices and tomato sauce. It is versatile and commonly used as a filling for tacos or served with rice and beans.
instructions: Place the beef brisket in a large pot and cover with water. Add a pinch of salt and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. | Reduce heat and simmer the beef for about 2 hours or until tender and easily shredded. | Remove the beef from the pot and let it cool slightly. Reserve the broth for later use. | Using two forks, shred the beef into thin pieces. | In a skillet, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until translucent. | Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. | Add the shredded beef to the skillet and stir to combine with the onion and garlic. | Pour in the tomato sauce and add the cumin, oregano, and chili powder. Stir well to evenly coat the beef. | Pour in about 100 ml of the reserved beef broth to keep the mixture moist, and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. | Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste. | Serve hot as a filling for tacos, burritos, or alongside rice and beans.

name: Caldeirada De Peixe
description: Caldeirada de Peixe is a traditional Portuguese fish stew made with layered fish, potatoes, and vegetables gently cooked in olive oil and wine, offering a hearty and flavorful meal.
instructions: Prepare the fish by cleaning and cutting it into chunks, keeping different types separate to layer later. | Peel and slice the potatoes thinly and peel and slice the onion and tomatoes. | In a large pot, drizzle olive oil and add the sliced onion and garlic, sautéing until soft. | Add the sliced tomatoes and cook until they start breaking down. | Layer the sliced potatoes over the tomato and onion base in the pot. | Add bay leaf, paprika, salt, and pepper over the potatoes. | Place the fish chunks on top of the potatoes, layering different types if using multiple. | Pour enough water and white wine over the layered ingredients to barely cover them. | Sprinkle chopped parsley and a pinch of saffron over the stew. | Cover the pot and simmer gently for about 30 to 40 minutes or until the potatoes are tender and fish is cooked through. | Adjust seasoning to taste and sprinkle more fresh parsley before serving.

name: Caldo De Peixe
description: Caldo de Peixe is a traditional Brazilian fish soup known for its rich, comforting flavors created from fresh fish, tomatoes, and cilantro. It's a simple yet hearty dish commonly enjoyed along the coastal regions of Brazil.
instructions: Rinse the fish thoroughly under cold water and cut into large chunks, reserving the heads and bones for stock if desired. | In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat and sauté the chopped onion until translucent. | Add the minced garlic and cook until fragrant, about one minute. | Pour in the diced tomatoes and cook down for 5 minutes to form a flavorful base. | Add the fish chunks, reserving delicate fillets for later, and season with salt, black pepper, and paprika. | Pour in the fish stock or water and bring to a gentle simmer, cooking for 10-15 minutes until the fish is tender and flavors meld. | Add the reserved fish fillets and cook for an additional 5 minutes until just cooked through. | Stir in the chopped cilantro and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. | Serve hot with lime wedges on the side for squeezing over the soup.

name: Caldo Verde
description: Caldo Verde is a traditional Portuguese green soup made with potatoes, kale, and chorizo, known for its simple, comforting flavors and vibrant green color.
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the potatoes, then place them in a large pot with the chicken broth and bring to a boil over medium heat. | Cook the potatoes until tender, about 15-20 minutes, then blend the soup with an immersion blender or in batches in a blender until smooth. | Peel and thinly slice the garlic, and sauté it in olive oil over medium heat until fragrant and lightly golden. | Slice the kale leaves into very thin strips, removing the tough stems. | Add the sautéed garlic, kale, and sliced chorizo to the blended potato soup and simmer for another 10-15 minutes until the kale is tender but still vibrant green. | Season the soup with salt and pepper to taste. | Ladle the soup into bowls and drizzle with a little more olive oil before serving.

name: Caracóis
description: Caracóis is a traditional Portuguese dish of freshwater snails simmered in a flavorful broth made with garlic, onion, herbs, and spices. It is commonly enjoyed as a popular appetizer or snack.
instructions: Rinse the snails thoroughly in cold water several times to remove any dirt or impurities. | Bring a large pot of water to a boil and blanch the snails for 2-3 minutes, then drain and rinse again to clean. | In a large pot, heat olive oil and sauté chopped garlic, onion, and chopped fresh coriander until soft and fragrant. | Add paprika, chili flakes, and black pepper to the pot and stir for a minute to release the aromas. | Pour in white wine and let it reduce slightly for about 2 minutes. | Add chicken broth, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt to the pot and bring to a simmer. | Add the cleaned snails to the broth and simmer gently for 30-40 minutes, until the snails are tender and infused with the flavors. | Adjust seasoning with salt and more lemon juice if desired. | Serve the snails hot in small bowls with some broth and garnish with fresh coriander leaves. | Provide toothpicks or small forks for easy eating.

name: Caramel Flan with Coffee
description: Caramel Flan with Coffee is a smooth, creamy custard dessert topped with rich caramel and infused with brewed coffee, blending sweetness and slight bitterness for a delightful treat.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C (320°F). | In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt the sugar until it becomes a golden amber caramel. Quickly but carefully pour the caramel into the bottom of ramekins or a baking dish, tilting to coat evenly. Set aside to harden. | In a mixing bowl, whisk together the eggs and egg yolks until smooth. | Add the sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk, brewed coffee, and vanilla extract to the eggs, mixing thoroughly. | Strain the custard mixture through a fine sieve to ensure smoothness. | Pour the custard mixture over the set caramel in the ramekins or baking dish. | Place the ramekins in a larger baking pan and add hot water to the pan until it reaches halfway up the sides of the ramekins, creating a water bath. | Bake for 50-60 minutes or until the custard is set but still slightly jiggly in the center. | Remove from the oven and water bath, then cool to room temperature. | Refrigerate the flan for at least 4 hours or overnight to fully set and chill. | To serve, run a knife around the edges of the flan to loosen it. Invert onto a serving plate so that the caramel sauce flows over the flan. | Serve chilled and enjoy.

name: Caramelized Orange Slices
description: Caramelized orange slices are a simple, elegant dessert featuring thin orange rounds cooked in a rich caramel sauce, perfect for a light and flavorful treat.
instructions: Peel the orange carefully to remove the skin and white pith, then slice into 0.5 cm thick rounds. | Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat and add the sugar. | Allow the sugar to melt slowly until it turns a deep amber color, swirling the pan occasionally to prevent burning. | Add the orange slices to the caramel and cook for 1-2 minutes on each side until they are translucent and caramel-coated. | Remove the orange slices carefully with a spatula and place them on a plate to cool slightly. | Optional: garnish with a sprig of fresh mint or a dusting of powdered sugar before serving.

name: Carob Cake Algarve
description: Carob Cake Algarve is a traditional Portuguese dessert from the Algarve region featuring carob powder, a popular cocoa substitute. This moist and naturally sweet cake offers a unique flavor and is often enjoyed with a drizzle of honey or a dusting of powdered sugar.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Grease and flour a 9-inch round cake pan. | In a bowl, sift together the carob powder, flour, baking powder, and a pinch of salt. | In another large bowl, beat the eggs and sugar until creamy and pale. | Gradually add the olive oil to the egg mixture while continuing to beat. | Slowly incorporate the dry ingredients into the wet mixture until well combined. | Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan and smooth the top. | Bake for 40 to 45 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. | Allow the cake to cool in the pan for 10 minutes before turning out onto a wire rack to cool completely. | Optionally, dust with powdered sugar or drizzle with honey before serving.

name: Carrot Fritters
description: Carrot fritters are a simple, flavorful vegetarian dish made by combining grated carrots with spices and chickpea flour, then pan-frying into crispy patties. They make a delicious gluten-free main or side dish.
instructions: Peel and grate the carrot using a fine grater. | In a bowl, combine the grated carrot, chopped onion, and chopped fresh parsley. | In a small bowl, whisk the egg with salt, pepper, and cumin powder. | Add the egg mixture to the grated carrot mixture and stir to combine. | Sprinkle the chickpea flour over the mixture and mix well to form a thick batter. | Heat olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat. | Spoon dollops of the batter into the pan and flatten slightly to form small patties. | Fry the fritters for 3-4 minutes on each side until golden brown and cooked through. | Place the cooked fritters on paper towels to drain excess oil. | Serve warm with a side of yogurt or a dipping sauce of choice.

name: Carrot Rice
description: Carrot rice is a simple and flavorful Indian rice dish made by cooking basmati rice with grated carrots and aromatic spices, resulting in a colorful and nutritious meal.
instructions: Rinse the basmati rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear, then soak it in water for 20 minutes and drain. | Heat oil in a pan over medium heat and add mustard seeds; let them splutter. | Add cumin seeds, chopped green chili, and grated ginger, sauté for a minute until fragrant. | Add chopped onion and sauté until it turns translucent. | Add the grated carrot and cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly softened. | Add turmeric powder and salt, mix well. | Add the soaked and drained rice, and gently stir to combine with the carrot mixture. | Add water and bring to a boil. | Reduce the heat to low, cover the pan, and cook for 15 minutes or until the rice is cooked and water is absorbed. | Turn off the heat and let it sit covered for 5 minutes. | Fluff the rice gently with a fork and garnish with chopped coriander leaves before serving.

name: Carrot and Coriander Salad
description: A fresh and vibrant salad featuring grated carrot combined with fragrant coriander, dressed in a light lemon and honey dressing. This simple and healthy side dish is perfect for any season.
instructions: Peel and grate the carrot into thin strips using a grater or food processor. | Finely chop the fresh coriander leaves and set aside. | In a small bowl, whisk together the lemon juice, olive oil, honey, salt, and black pepper to make the dressing. | Place the grated carrot and chopped coriander in a large bowl. | Pour the dressing over the carrot and coriander mixture and toss well to combine. | Let the salad sit for 10 minutes to allow flavors to meld before serving.

name: Buñuelos De Calabaza
description: Buñuelos de Calabaza are traditional pumpkin fritters from Latin America, featuring a crispy exterior and soft pumpkin-flavored interior, often enjoyed as a snack or dessert.
instructions: Peel the pumpkin and cut it into small chunks. | Boil the pumpkin chunks in water until soft, then drain and mash until smooth. | In a large bowl, combine the mashed pumpkin, flour, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt. | Add the beaten egg and mix well to form a thick batter. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan over medium heat for frying. | Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the hot oil and fry until golden brown on all sides, turning occasionally. | Remove the fritters with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. | Sprinkle with powdered sugar or cinnamon sugar while still warm if desired. | Serve warm as a snack or dessert.

name: Buñuelos De San Jose
description: Buñuelos de San Jose are traditional Spanish fritters made from a simple dough fried until golden and dusted with cinnamon sugar, commonly enjoyed during Saint Joseph's Day celebrations.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, sugar, baking powder, and a pinch of salt. | Gradually add water and olive oil to the dry ingredients while mixing with a spoon or your hands until a smooth, elastic dough forms. | Cover the dough with a clean cloth and let it rest for about 30 minutes. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat until hot but not smoking. | Divide the dough into small pieces and roll each piece into thin rounds approximately 10 cm in diameter. | Carefully place the dough rounds into the hot oil, frying a few at a time without overcrowding. | Fry each fritter until golden brown and puffed, about 2-3 minutes per side, flipping once. | Remove the fritters from the oil and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. | While still warm, sprinkle the fritters generously with cinnamon and sugar mixture. | Serve the Buñuelos warm or at room temperature as a traditional treat for Saint Joseph's Day.

name: Buñuelos De Semana Santa
description: Buñuelos de Semana Santa are traditional fried fritters enjoyed during Holy Week in Spanish-speaking countries. They are crispy on the outside, soft inside, and dusted with cinnamon sugar for a sweet treat.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, salt, sugar, and cinnamon. | Make a well in the center and add beaten eggs, milk, and melted butter. | Mix the ingredients until you form a smooth, elastic dough. Cover the dough and let it rest for about 30 minutes. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep fryer or heavy pot to 180°C (350°F). | Pinch off small pieces of dough and shape them into flat, round discs. | Carefully drop the dough discs into the hot oil and fry until golden brown on both sides, about 2-3 minutes per side. | Remove the fritters with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels. | While still warm, sprinkle the fritters generously with sugar and cinnamon mixture. | Serve warm or at room temperature as a traditional Holy Week treat.

name: Buñuelos De Todos Los Santos
description: Buñuelos de Todos los Santos are traditional Spanish sweet fritters enjoyed during All Saints' Day, featuring a light batter fried to golden perfection and dusted with cinnamon sugar.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, sugar, and a pinch of salt and mix well. | In a separate bowl, beat the egg and whisk in the milk and olive oil until fully combined. | Gradually add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, stirring continuously until a smooth, thick batter forms. If the batter is too thick, add a little more milk. | Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or fryer to 180°C (350°F). | Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil, frying in batches to avoid overcrowding, and cook each fritter for about 2-3 minutes on each side or until golden brown and puffed up. | Remove the buñuelos with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. | While still warm, sprinkle the buñuelos generously with cinnamon sugar. | Serve warm as a sweet treat commonly enjoyed during the All Saints' Day celebrations.

name: Cabrito Al Ajillo
description: Cabrito al Ajillo is a traditional Mexican dish featuring tender kid goat meat cooked with garlic, fresh herbs, and lime juice, creating a flavorful and aromatic main course.
instructions: Rinse the kid goat meat and pat dry with paper towels. | Cut the meat into serving pieces, removing excess fat if necessary. | In a large bowl, marinate the meat with minced garlic, salt, black pepper, and lime juice. Let it rest for at least 30 minutes. | Heat olive oil in a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat. | Add the marinated goat pieces to the skillet and sear until browned on all sides, about 8 to 10 minutes. | Reduce the heat to medium-low and add chopped fresh parsley and bay leaf to the skillet. | Add a splash of chicken broth to the pan, cover, and let the meat simmer for about 45 minutes to 1 hour until tender, turning occasionally and adding more broth if needed. | Once the meat is tender and the sauce has reduced, remove the bay leaf and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. | Serve hot, garnished with additional fresh parsley if desired.

name: Cabrito Asado
description: Cabrito Asado is a traditional Mexican dish featuring kid goat meat roasted with a flavorful garlic and herb marinade, resulting in tender and aromatic meat.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Wash the kid goat thoroughly and pat it dry with paper towels. | In a bowl, mix garlic, salt, black pepper, oregano, cumin, and olive oil to create a marinade. | Rub the marinade all over the kid goat, including the cavity, ensuring even coverage. | Place the kid goat on a roasting rack in a roasting pan. | Roast in the preheated oven for about 1.5 to 2 hours, basting occasionally with the pan juices to keep the meat moist. | Check for doneness by ensuring the internal temperature reaches 75°C (165°F) or the juices run clear when pierced. | Once cooked, remove from oven and let it rest for 10 to 15 minutes before carving. | Serve the roast kid goat with your preferred side dishes such as roasted vegetables or a fresh salad.

name: Cachopo Asturiano
description: Cachopo Asturiano is a traditional Spanish dish from Asturias consisting of two breaded veal cutlets stuffed with ham and cheese, fried until golden, then baked to melt the cheese inside. It's a hearty and flavorful main course.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Place the veal cutlets between two sheets of plastic wrap and gently pound them with a meat mallet or rolling pin until about 1 cm thick. | Season both sides of the veal cutlets with salt and pepper. | Place a slice of ham on one veal cutlet, then top with slices of cheese, then cover with the second veal cutlet to form a sandwich. | Press the edges gently to seal the cutlets. | Prepare three shallow bowls: one with flour, one with beaten egg, and one with breadcrumbs. | Dip each stuffed veal cutlet first in flour, then in beaten egg, and finally coat well with breadcrumbs. | Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. | Fry the breaded cutlets for about 3-4 minutes on each side until golden brown. | Transfer the cutlets to a baking tray and bake in the preheated oven for 10-15 minutes to ensure they are cooked through and the cheese is melted. | Remove from the oven and let rest for a few minutes before slicing and serving.

name: Cachopo Asturiano
description: Cachopo Asturiano is a traditional Spanish dish from Asturias featuring tender veal slices filled with ham and cheese, breaded and fried to golden perfection.
instructions: Place two large veal slices on a clean surface. | Season both sides of the veal slices with salt and pepper. | On one veal slice, layer slices of ham and cheese evenly, then cover with the second veal slice to form a sandwich. | Press the edges slightly to seal. | Prepare three shallow dishes: one with beaten egg, another with flour, and the last with breadcrumbs. | Dredge the veal sandwich first in the flour, then dip it into the beaten egg, and finally coat it thoroughly with breadcrumbs. | Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. | Fry the breaded veal sandwich in the hot oil until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. | Remove from the skillet and drain excess oil on paper towels. | Serve hot with a side of fried potatoes or salad if desired.

name: Calabacines Rellenos
description: Calabacines Rellenos is a traditional Spanish dish featuring zucchini stuffed with a flavorful mixture of vegetables, optionally meat or rice, baked with cheese until tender and golden.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Cut the zucchini lengthwise and scoop out the flesh, leaving about 1 cm border to form a shell. | Chop the scooped-out zucchini flesh finely and set aside. | Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat, then sauté the chopped onion and garlic until translucent. | Add the chopped zucchini flesh and cook until soft. | Add diced tomato and cook for another 5 minutes until the mixture thickens slightly. | Season with salt, pepper, and chopped parsley, then remove from heat. | Optionally, mix in cooked ground meat or rice to the filling for added protein or texture. | Fill the zucchini shells with the cooked mixture, then place them in a baking dish. | Sprinkle grated cheese over the stuffed zucchinis. | Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes until the zucchinis are tender and the cheese is golden and bubbly. | Serve warm as a main or side dish.

name: Calamares a La Romana
description: Calamares a la Romana is a traditional Spanish dish featuring tender squid rings coated in flour and deep-fried to golden perfection, often served as a popular appetizer.
instructions: Clean the squid thoroughly and slice it into rings about 1 cm thick. | Place the squid rings in a bowl and season with salt and pepper. | In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour and a pinch of salt. | Dip each squid ring into the flour mixture, ensuring it is well coated, then shake off any excess flour. | Heat the vegetable oil in a deep frying pan or deep fryer to 180°C (350°F). | Carefully place the floured squid rings into the hot oil in batches to avoid overcrowding. | Fry the squid rings until they are golden and crisp, about 2-3 minutes. | Use a slotted spoon to remove the fried squid rings and drain them on paper towels to remove excess oil. | Serve the fried squid rings hot, garnished with lemon wedges and optionally with a side of alioli or a simple garlic mayonnaise.

name: Green Curry with Chicken
description: Green Curry with Chicken is a traditional Thai dish featuring a fragrant and spicy green curry paste simmered with chicken, eggplant, and aromatic herbs in creamy coconut milk. It offers a perfect balance of heat, sweetness, and savory flavors.
instructions: Prepare the green curry paste by blending green chili, garlic, shallot, ginger, lemongrass, coriander root, cilantro stem, kaffir lime zest, roasted cumin, and shrimp paste into a fine paste. | Heat vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the green curry paste until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes. | Add sliced chicken breast to the pan and cook until the chicken is no longer pink. | Pour in coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. | Add sliced eggplant and cook until tender, about 5-7 minutes. | Stir in fish sauce, palm sugar, and Thai basil leaves. | Add kaffir lime leaves and continue simmering for another 2 minutes. | Serve the green curry hot over steamed jasmine rice.

name: Green Curry with Duck
description: Green Curry with Duck is a flavorful Thai dish featuring tender duck breast simmered in a fragrant green curry sauce with coconut milk, eggplant, and fresh herbs, served with jasmine rice.
instructions: Warm vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat. | Add green curry paste and sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. | Pour in coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer while stirring to combine with the curry paste. | Add sliced duck breast to the pan and cook for about 5-7 minutes until the meat is tender and cooked through. | Add sliced eggplant, bamboo shoots, and kaffir lime leaves to the curry and simmer for another 5 minutes until the vegetables are tender. | Stir in fish sauce, palm sugar, and Thai basil leaves, adjusting seasoning to taste. | Serve the green curry hot over steamed jasmine rice and garnish with additional Thai basil if desired.

name: Green Curry with Eggplant
description: A classic Thai green curry featuring tender eggplant in a fragrant and creamy coconut milk sauce, seasoned with green curry paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar, garnished with fresh Thai basil.
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pan or wok over medium heat. | Add the green curry paste and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. | Add the sliced eggplant to the pan and stir to coat with the curry paste. | Pour in the coconut milk and stir well to combine. | Add fish sauce and palm sugar, stirring to dissolve the sugar. | Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer and cook for about 10 minutes until the eggplant is tender. | Add the Thai basil leaves and stir just before turning off the heat. | Serve the green curry hot with steamed jasmine rice if desired.

name: Green Curry with Fish Balls
description: Green Curry with Fish Balls is a classic Thai dish combining spicy green curry with tender fish balls, cooked in creamy coconut milk with aromatic herbs and vegetables.
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat. | Add the green curry paste and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. | Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. | Add the fish balls and cook for 5 minutes until they start to float. | Add the sliced eggplant and kaffir lime leaves, simmer for another 5 minutes until the eggplant is tender. | Stir in the fish sauce and palm sugar, adjusting to taste. | Add the Thai basil leaves and cook for another minute until wilted. | Remove from heat and serve the curry hot, garnished with extra basil leaves if desired.

name: Green Curry with Pork
description: Green Curry with Pork is a flavorful Thai dish featuring tender pork cooked in a spicy and aromatic green curry sauce with coconut milk, eggplant, and fresh herbs. It's traditionally served with steamed jasmine rice.
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat. | Add the green curry paste and sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes. | Add the pork slices and cook until they begin to brown. | Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a simmer. | Add the fish sauce, palm sugar, and stir to dissolve the sugar. | Add the eggplant and kaffir lime leaves, cook until the eggplant is tender. | Add the Thai basil leaves and stir well. | Adjust seasoning with additional fish sauce or sugar as needed. | Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Green Curry with Shrimp
description: Green Curry with Shrimp is a classic Thai dish featuring a spicy and creamy green curry sauce with tender shrimp, enhanced by aromatic herbs and coconut milk.
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat. | Add the green curry paste and stir-fry until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes. | Pour in the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring to combine with the curry paste. | Add the shrimp and cook until they turn pink and are cooked through, about 3-5 minutes. | Stir in the fish sauce, sugar, and kaffir lime leaves (if using) for flavor and simmer for another 2 minutes. | Add the sliced eggplant and cook until tender, about 5 minutes. | Add the Thai basil leaves and stir well. | Remove from heat and serve the curry hot, garnished with extra basil if desired.

name: Green Curry with Tofu
description: Green Curry with Tofu is a flavorful Thai dish featuring tofu simmered in aromatic and spicy green curry sauce with coconut milk and fresh vegetables. It offers a rich and vibrant vegetarian main course with authentic Southeast Asian flavors.
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat. | Add the green curry paste and sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. | Add the sliced onion and cook until softened, about 3 minutes. | Add the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer. | Add the tofu cubes and cook for 5 minutes to absorb the flavors. | Add the sliced bell pepper, sliced zucchini, and bamboo shoots, and cook for another 5 minutes until vegetables are tender. | Stir in the fish sauce, brown sugar, and Thai basil leaves, and cook for 1 more minute. | Serve the green curry hot with steamed jasmine rice.

name: Green Pandan Coconut Pudding
description: Green Pandan Coconut Pudding, or Khanom Tuay, is a traditional Thai dessert featuring a smooth, fragrant green pudding made from pandan and coconut milk, steamed to a delicate texture and served with sweetened coconut sauce.
instructions: Combine rice flour, tapioca flour, sugar, and a pinch of salt in a mixing bowl. | Gradually add water and pandan leaf extract to the dry ingredients and whisk until smooth and well combined. | Pour the mixture into small heatproof ceramic or silicone cups, filling them about three-quarters full. | Prepare a steamer and bring water to a gentle boil. | Place the filled cups into the steamer basket and steam for about 15-20 minutes until the pudding sets and becomes translucent. | While the pudding is steaming, prepare coconut sauce by combining coconut milk, sugar, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan. | Heat the coconut sauce over medium heat, stirring frequently until the sugar dissolves. Remove from heat and set aside. | Once the puddings are cooked, let them cool slightly before removing from the cups. | Serve each pudding with a spoonful of the warm coconut sauce poured over the top.

name: Grilled Sai Krok Isan
description: Grilled Sai Krok Isan is a traditional spicy fermented Thai sausage from the Isan region, characterized by its tangy flavor and smoky grilled taste. It is typically served with fresh herbs and sticky rice, making it a popular street food and appetizer.
instructions: Prepare the sausages by pricking them lightly with a fork to allow even cooking and prevent bursting. | Preheat the grill to medium heat. | Place the sausages on the grill and cook, turning occasionally to ensure even grilling on all sides. | Grill the sausages for about 15-20 minutes until they are cooked through and have a crispy, golden-brown exterior. | Remove the sausages from the grill and let them rest for a few minutes before serving. | Serve the grilled sausages with sliced fresh ginger, garlic, and Thai bird's eye chilies on the side for dipping, along with sticky rice if desired.

name: Guava Juice Nam Farang
description: Guava Juice Nam Farang is a refreshing Thai-style guava juice, made by blending ripe guava with water and sugar, then straining to produce a smooth, sweet beverage.
instructions: Wash the ripe guava thoroughly under running water. | Peel the guava and cut it into small pieces, removing any seeds. | Place the guava pieces into a blender. | Add water to the blender to help blend the guava into juice; adjust amount based on desired thickness. | Add sugar to the blender to sweeten the juice according to taste. | Blend the mixture until smooth and well combined. | Strain the blended mixture through a fine mesh sieve or cheesecloth into a jug to remove pulp and seeds, pressing to extract as much juice as possible. | Pour the strained guava juice into serving glasses filled with ice cubes. | Optionally, garnish with a slice of guava or a sprig of mint before serving.

name: Burdur Shish Kofta
description: Burdur Shish Kofta is a traditional Turkish dish featuring seasoned ground meat skewered and grilled to perfection, originating from the Burdur region. It stands out for its use of sumac and cumin, offering a distinct tangy and warm flavor profile.
instructions: Mix ground lamb and ground beef together in a large bowl. | Add finely chopped onion, finely chopped parsley, bread crumbs, sumac, black pepper, salt, and cumin to the meat mixture. | Knead the mixture thoroughly until all ingredients are well incorporated and the mixture becomes sticky. | Cover the bowl and let the mixture rest in the refrigerator for 30 minutes to an hour to develop flavors. | Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. | Moisten your hands with water and shape the meat mixture into small, elongated meatballs around wooden skewers. | Place the skewered meatballs on the grill and cook, turning occasionally, until evenly browned and cooked through, about 10 to 15 minutes. | Serve the Burdur Shish Kofta hot, accompanied by grilled vegetables or a fresh salad as desired.

name: Burma Kadayif
description: Burma Kadayif is a traditional Turkish dessert featuring rolled shredded pastry filled with pistachios, baked until crisp and soaked in a fragrant sugar syrup.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | Prepare the syrup by combining sugar and water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the syrup thickens slightly. Remove from heat and add lemon juice. Let the syrup cool completely. | Separate the shredded pastry into manageable portions and gently loosen the strands. | Brush a sheet of pastry with melted butter, then sprinkle with ground pistachio nuts evenly. | Roll the pastry tightly into a cylindrical shape, then coil it into a circular 'snail' shape on a buttered baking tray. Repeat with remaining pastry and filling. | Brush the coils generously with melted butter. | Bake in the preheated oven for about 30 minutes or until golden and crisp. | Remove the coils from the oven and immediately pour the cooled syrup evenly over the hot pastry. | Allow the dessert to absorb the syrup and cool to room temperature before serving.

name: Bursa Candied Chestnuts
description: Bursa Candied Chestnuts are a traditional Turkish sweet delicacy from Bursa, made by simmering peeled chestnuts in a thick sugar syrup until tender and glossy.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the chestnuts. Boil for about 15 minutes to soften the shells. | Drain the chestnuts and carefully peel them while still warm, removing both the hard outer shell and the thin inner skin. Take care not to break the chestnuts. | In a saucepan, combine sugar and water to make a simple syrup. Heat over medium heat until sugar dissolves and the syrup starts to simmer. | Add the peeled chestnuts into the simmering syrup gently and cook over low heat for about 1 to 2 hours until the syrup thickens and chestnuts become translucent and tender. Stir occasionally and be careful not to break the chestnuts. | Remove the candied chestnuts with a slotted spoon and place them on a wire rack to dry and cool. | Once dried, store the Bursa candied chestnuts in an airtight container and keep in a cool place or refrigerate for longer shelf life.

name: Bursa Milk Halva
description: Bursa Milk Halva is a traditional Turkish dessert from the city of Bursa, made by toasting semolina in butter and slowly cooking it with sweetened milk until thickened. It is known for its rich, creamy texture and delicate nutty flavor.
instructions: In a heavy-bottomed pan, melt the butter over medium heat until it is fully melted and slightly bubbling. | Add the semolina to the melted butter and stir continuously to coat the semolina well with butter and to toast it until it turns golden brown and emits a nutty aroma. This should take about 10-12 minutes. | Meanwhile, in a separate saucepan, combine the milk, sugar, and salt. Heat this mixture over medium heat, stirring occasionally until the sugar dissolves completely and the milk is warm but not boiling. | Slowly pour the warm milk mixture into the toasted semolina while stirring continuously to avoid lumps. | Keep stirring the mixture over low heat until it thickens significantly and the semolina absorbs the milk completely. This process usually takes around 10 minutes. | Remove the pan from heat and spread the halva evenly in a serving dish or mold. | Allow the halva to cool down to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours to set properly before serving. | Serve chilled, optionally garnished with ground pistachio or cinnamon according to preference.

name: Bursa Pideli Kofte
description: Bursa Pideli Kofte is a traditional Turkish dish featuring grilled spicy meatballs served on soft soaked pide bread, topped with rich tomato sauce and melted butter. This specialty originates from Bursa and combines savory flavors and comforting textures.
instructions: Soak the pide bread slices in warm meat broth until they are nicely absorbed but not soggy. | In a pan, melt butter and sauté the soaked pide slices briefly to heat and add flavor, then arrange them on serving plates. | Grill or pan-fry the small meatballs until they are cooked through and nicely browned on all sides. | Place the cooked meatballs on top of the prepared pide slices on the plates. | In a saucepan, warm tomato sauce with a pinch of chili flakes and garlic to create a flavorful, slightly spicy sauce. | Pour the tomato sauce generously over the meatballs and pide slices. | Garnish the dish with melted butter drizzled on top and chopped fresh parsley for freshness. | Serve the Bursa Pideli Kofte hot, accompanied by plain yogurt on the side if desired.

name: Butter Honey Bread
description: Butter Honey Bread is a soft and slightly sweet Turkish bread brushed with melted butter and honey, perfect for breakfast or tea time.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). | In a large bowl, combine the flour, sugar, salt, and yeast. | In a separate bowl, warm the milk slightly and add to the dry ingredients along with the melted butter and egg. | Mix all ingredients until a dough forms, then knead on a floured surface for about 8 minutes until smooth and elastic. | Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with a cloth, and let it rise for about 1 hour or until doubled in size. | Punch down the dough and shape it into a loaf or desired bread shapes. | Place the shaped dough onto a baking tray lined with parchment paper and let it rise for another 30 minutes. | Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes until golden brown and cooked through. | Remove the bread from the oven and while still warm, brush generously with melted butter. | Drizzle honey over the buttered bread and let cool slightly before slicing and serving.

name: Butter Rice Pilaf
description: Tereyagli Pilav is a classic Turkish butter rice pilaf known for its rich, buttery flavor and fluffy texture, making it a perfect side dish for a variety of meals.
